fix: reject a gpu resource that is not one of its declared forms

`Resources.gpu` is typed `Union[Accelerators, int, Device, None]`, but
`__post_init__` only ever checked the int and str arms. Any other value fell
through unvalidated, was carried untouched by `get_device` -- whose
`Optional[Device]` annotation then lied -- and killed the request much later,
inside serialization:

    Resources(gpu=("A100", 4))   # accepted here
    ...
    AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'quantity'

That is an SDK-frame crash naming neither the field nor the task definition
that caused it, at a point far from the mistake.

A `(device, quantity)` tuple is the likely way to land here: it is what an
accelerator string decomposes into, and what `get_device` was documented as
returning. That docstring is corrected here too, since it is what points
users at a tuple in the first place.

`__post_init__` now rejects anything that is not an accelerator string, a
device count or a `Device`, naming the accepted forms. Every declared form
still works unchanged, `gpu=0` included -- it keeps meaning "no accelerator"
rather than raising.

Same family as the previously fixed `Resources(gpu=0)` (flyteorg/flyte#7995)
and the open `Resources(disk=)` / `Resources(shm=)` KeyError
(flyteorg/flyte#7991): a value accepted by the constructor that only fails
once it reaches the serializer.

add HF dataset plugin (#992) This PR adds a Hugging Face datasets plugin for Flyte. It lets tasks consume Hub datasets directly via `from_hf(...)` and transparently materializes them as `datasets.Dataset` or `datasets.IterableDataset` with optional shared caching through `cache_root`. ```python from flyteplugins.huggingface.datasets import from_hf @env.task async def train( ds: datasets.Dataset = from_hf( "stanfordnlp/imdb", name="plain_text", split="train", cache_root="s3://my-bucket/flyte-hf-cache", ), ) -> int: return len(ds) ``` The plugin streams converted parquet shards from the Hub, stores them as sharded parquet artifacts, and reuses cached materializations across runs when available. You can also return and pass real `datasets.Dataset` objects between tasks: ```python @env.task async def create_dataset() -> datasets.Dataset: return datasets.Dataset.from_dict( { "text": ["hello", "world", "flyte"], "label": [0, 1, 0], } ) @env.task async def filter_positive(ds: datasets.Dataset) -> datasets.Dataset: return ds.filter(lambda row: row["label"] == 1) ``` --------- Signed-off-by: André Ahlert Signed-off-by: Samhita Alla Co-authored-by: André Ahlert

test(integration): add clustered (JobSet) integration test (#1244)

## Motivation
None of the `examples/clustered/` examples were covered by
`examples/integration_tests.py`, so regressions in the JobSet-backed
clustered runtime would not be caught by the integration suite.

## Summary
- Adds a `CLUSTERED (JOBSETS)` section to
`examples/integration_tests.py` with one tier-1 test:
`test_clustered_failure_cascade`.
- The test exercises `examples/clustered/failure_cascade.py` (2 CPU
pods, gloo backend), which covers the JobSet lifecycle end-to-end:
rendezvous, deliberate rank failure, whole-set restart, and checkpoint
resume.
- Reuses the existing `_run_and_wait` / `_verify_log_links` helpers —
log-link verification works as-is for JobSet attempts.

## Test Plan
Ran against `playground.canary.unionai.cloud` after enabling the
`clustered-task` propeller plugin (cloud#16667) and installing the
JobSet helm chart on the cluster:

\`\`\`
uv run pytest examples/integration_tests.py -k clustered_failure_cascade
-v
\`\`\`

Result: PASSED in 75s on attempt 1. Verified two JobSet worker pods
(`<run>-a0-0-workers-0-{0,1}`) reached rendezvous, rank 1 crashed
mid-training, the JobSet restarted the whole set, and training resumed
from the last checkpoint to SUCCEEDED.

GPU and stress variants (`ddp_train`, `ddp_train_restart`, `load_16pod`)
were prototyped and validated locally on playground but pulled from this
PR to keep tier-1 minimal; they can be added in a follow-up once GPU CI
capacity is wired up.

Lineage costs nothing for users who don't use it

- Deploy version: the labels fingerprint is hashed only when the deploy writes
  a label (deploy --label, env labels or task labels), so a label-free deploy
  computes the same auto version as main.
- Trigger.create: deploy as main did (no lookup, no revision); only on a
  revision conflict (FAILED_PRECONDITION from the backend's optimistic lock, or
  ALREADY_EXISTS / ABORTED) fetch the current revision and retry once. A plain
  create is one RPC again.
- New flyte._internal.lineage_gate (any_lineage / task_declares_lineage /
  is_handle), which imports none of the lineage modules. flyte.deploy skips
  refresh_envs, lineage_summary and check_references (and their imports) when
  nothing declares lineage, and returns Deployment.lineage=None; deploy and run
  set emit_lineage_tags only for a plan / task that declares lineage.
- flyte.artifacts resolves the handle and refresh names lazily (PEP 562, with
  TYPE_CHECKING imports and __dir__), so the type engine no longer loads
  _handle/_refresh in every pod. App Parameter / consumes_artifacts desugar,
  app serialization and App.replace skip the handle and lineage imports when
  nothing needs them.

fix: wrap KeyError at user-module import as ModuleLoadError

When a user module does `os.environ["GCP_ADR"]` at top level and the env
var is missing, the resulting KeyError escaped the module loader and
bubbled into Sentry as if it were an SDK crash (FLYTE-SDK-3D).

This adds KeyError to both `except (ImportError, SyntaxError, NameError,
AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError)` clauses in module_loader.py so
that env-var-missing failures at user-code import time surface as
ModuleLoadError — consistent with NameError/TypeError already wrapped.
ModuleLoadError is a RuntimeUserError subclass and is already filtered
by flyte/_sentry.py:_is_user_error.

fixes FLYTE-SDK-3D

fix: retry App update on revision conflict with a fresh refetch

App is the only SDK entity with optimistic-concurrency (revision)
semantics. If the App's stored revision is bumped between our get and
our update (by another deploy, the console, or a server-side
reconciler), the update is rejected with a revision-mismatch error
that previously surfaced as a hard deploy failure. Retry a bounded
number of times with a fresh get+revision to close that window.

fix: raise clear error when flyte.TriggerTime is used as a task default (#1070)

## Summary

When a user declares a task with `flyte.TriggerTime` as the default
value for a regular parameter:

```python
@env.task
async def my_task(t: datetime = flyte.TriggerTime):
    ...
```

deploy fails with an opaque `TypeTransformerFailedError`:

> Expected value of type `<class 'datetime.datetime'>` but got
`<flyte._trigger._trigger_time object at …>`

That happened because `convert_upload_default_inputs` passed the
`flyte.TriggerTime` sentinel through to the datetime literal
transformer.

`flyte.TriggerTime` is only valid as a *value* inside
`flyte.Trigger(inputs=...)` — it cannot be used as a regular task
default. This PR detects the sentinel in `convert_upload_default_inputs`
and raises a clear `ValueError` explaining the supported pattern, so
users get an actionable error at deploy time instead of a transformer
crash.

## Sentry

Fixes [FLYTE-SDK-2Q](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/7480549137/)

## Test plan
- [x] Added regression test
`test_convert_upload_default_inputs_rejects_trigger_time`
- [x] `make fmt`
- [x] Existing convert / trigger_serde / triggers test suites pass (132
tests)

feat(shell): stage shell-task File inputs under NAMED_DIR (#1229)

Follow-up to #1220 (which added the file_input_layout knob to
ContainerTask but did not wire it into shell tasks). Shell tasks
reference inputs through a glob (/var/inputs/<name>/*), so a single File
must be staged inside a per-input directory under its original basename
— otherwise CoPilot stages it extensionless and tools that sniff format
by extension reject it (e.g. salmon on *.fastq.gz staged as "0").

- shell/_runtime.py: _ShellContainerTask now passes
file_input_layout="NAMED_DIR" to ContainerTask, so shell tasks always
stage File/list[File] into per-input dirs under their original basenames
(the renderer already globs them).
- _container.py: local docker staging is now layout-aware so `--local`
matches remote CoPilot — NAMED_DIR keeps original basenames
(index-prefix dedup on collision), DIRECT uses bare indices (0, 1, ...).
Replaces the prior unconditional name-preserving behavior.
- pyproject.toml: bump flyteidl2 pin to 2.0.24 — shell tasks always
request NAMED_DIR, and the emit raises on older flyteidl2 that lacks
DataLoadingConfig.file_input_layout.
- tests: lock DIRECT->indices for raw container list[File]; exercise
name/extension preservation and collision dedup via the public
file_input_layout="NAMED_DIR" param; assert single File renders to a
glob; add data_loading_config emit tests (DIRECT unset, shell emits
NAMED_DIR).

feat(cli): add `flyte gen docs --type json`

Emits the command tree as data: path, group-ness, help, arguments, options, and
the distribution that provided each command. The markdown path is untouched --
generated output is byte-identical apart from the line documenting this option.

The JSON reports what the CLI *is*. It takes no view on who should see what:
audience is a decision belonging to the documentation that consumes this, not a
property of the CLI. So there is no grouping by variant here, only a per-command
label, and help text is normalised with inspect.cleandoc but otherwise verbatim
-- no escaping, no code fencing, no markup.

Provenance is inherited from the nearest stamped ancestor, which is not a
nicety. Only 35 plugin commands are entry points; `flyte explore volume` and the
three `flyte undelete` subcommands are defined inside a plugin's own group and
carry no stamp. Attributing by entry point alone would report them as core --
the same defect from the other side, and one the __module__ guess happened to
get right.

Verified against flyteplugins-union 0.8.1: the 39 commands this reports as
plugin-provided are exactly the 39 the renderer gates to the union variant,
with no difference in either direction.

Add --plugin-config and --clustered options to flyte run python-script (#1410)

## Summary
- `--plugin-config <yaml>` lets `flyte run python-script` run under a
task-type plugin (Ray, PyTorch, Spark, Databricks, or any other
fully-qualified plugin config dataclass, e.g. from an external package
like skypilot). The YAML names the plugin class and its constructor
args, including nested classes, resolved via a recursive dict→dataclass
builder driven by type hints. The resolved config is also serialized
through the `InternalTaskResolver` so it's re-hydrated inside the
running container (Ray/Spark read `self.plugin_config` from
`pre()`/`execute()` at runtime, not just at registration time).
- `--clustered` routes the script to a `ClusteredTaskEnvironment`
(Kubernetes JobSet) instead of a plain `TaskEnvironment`, for
distributed multi-node execution via `torchrun`, with flags for
`--replicas`, `--nproc-per-node`, `--rdzv-backend`,
`--torchrun-max-restarts`, `--cluster-max-restarts`,
`--restart-on-host-maintenance`, and `--ttl-seconds-after-finished`.
Mutually exclusive with `--plugin-config` since
`ClusteredTaskEnvironment` manages its own plugin config internally.
- Also fixes 3 pre-existing, unrelated `ty` type errors (in
`databricks_example.py`, `spark_dataframe_example.py`,
`spark_example.py`) that were blocking `make ty` / the pre-commit hook
on this branch.

## Test plan
- [x] New unit tests for the recursive YAML→dataclass builder,
`load_plugin_config`, plugin_config serialize/deserialize round-trip,
and `run_python_script(plugin_config=...)` /
`run_python_script(clustered=..., replicas=..., nproc_per_node=...,
runtime=..., failure_policy=...)`
(`tests/user_api/test_run_python_script.py`)
- [x] New CLI tests for `--plugin-config` and `--clustered` flag
parsing, validation, and forwarding
(`tests/cli/test_run_python_script.py`)
- [x] End-to-end smoke test against the real `flyteplugins.spark.Spark`
and `flyteplugins.databricks.Databricks` plugin config classes
- [x] End-to-end smoke test confirming `--clustered` builds a real

Fix malformed node links, add depth-limited lazy loading for the lineage graph

Node links were malformed (e.g.
"https://...cloudhttps://...cloud/v2/.../runs/...") because the dashboard
prepended a derived CONSOLE_BASE to Run/Artifact/App .url properties that are
already fully-qualified absolute URLs (confirmed against
ControlPlaneClient._resource_url, which builds
f"{scheme}://{domain}/v2/..."). Removed the CONSOLE_BASE plumbing entirely
(the _derive_console_base() helper, the console_base field/param, and the
double-prepend at both node-click and "Open in console" sites) in favor of
using .url directly.

Also addresses the dashboard being slow to load: build_artifact_lineage()
previously walked the *entire* upstream chain back to the origin and the
*entire* downstream tree unconditionally, which for the downstream side in
particular can mean several RPCs per hop (a label-filtered run scan plus,
per watched task, a full recent-run scan with an input_literals fetch per
run). Replaced the single max_depth safety cap with explicit
upstream_depth/downstream_depth parameters (both default 1 -- "one step" in
each direction), and added has_more_upstream/has_more_downstream flags to
LineageGraph so the UI knows when there's more to load. The dashboard now
renders two "load more" buttons on the canvas that bump the respective depth
and refetch, growing the graph incrementally instead of paying for the whole
thing up front.

Verified with headless Chromium against a mocked backend: node clicks and the
"Open in console" link resolve to the correct (non-malformed) URL, and
clicking "Load more upstream" grows the graph and flips the button to
"Origin reached" once exhausted. Also spot-checked build_artifact_lineage()
directly against the live playground cluster: depth=1 now returns 4 nodes
(vs. 6 with the prior unbounded walk) with correctly-detected has_more flags.
Redeployed to the live dashboard app, which reached ACTIVE.

fix: truthiness checks for the null task context; restore inline flyte.ctx() style in examples

Follow-up to the NULL_TASK_CONTEXT change (flyte.ctx() now returns a falsy
null object instead of None):

- flyte/_logging.py's log-record factory still used `if c is not None:`, so
  the null context entered the branch and `c.action.run_name` raised
  AttributeError inside the factory on every log call made outside a task.
  This killed DynamicBatcher's processing loop before it could set the
  future's exception, hanging test_error_propagation (and any await on a

fix: filter OSError(ENOSPC) from Sentry as user environment error (#1133)

## Summary

`OSError` with `errno=ENOSPC` ("No space left on device") surfaces from
`shutil._fastcopy_sendfile` during `flyte deploy` bundle uploads when
the user's machine is out of disk. It is currently captured by the
`@_sentry.capture_errors` decorator on the deploy CLI invoke path and
reported to the SDK's Sentry project as if it were an SDK crash.
Disk-full is a user environment problem the SDK cannot fix, so it
shouldn't reach Sentry.

This change extends `flyte/_sentry.py:_is_user_error` to recognize
`OSError(errno=ENOSPC)` anywhere in the `__cause__`/`__context__` chain
via a new tightly scoped helper `_is_user_environment_oserror`.

The filter is intentionally narrow — only `ENOSPC` for now. Other
`OSError` errnos (`EACCES`, `ENOENT`, etc.) may legitimately indicate
SDK bugs and continue to be reported. A regression test pins this
behavior.

## Closes

- [FLYTE-SDK-32](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/FLYTE-SDK-32/) —
`OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` from
`shutil._fastcopy_sendfile` during deploy bundle copy.

fix: resolve AppEnvironment caller frame across __post_init__ chains

ConnectorEnvironment.__post_init__ calls super().__post_init__(), which
added an extra frame and caused AppEnvironment to capture the dataclass
__init__ frame as `_caller_frame` instead of the user's module. The app
env resolver then derived a wrong module name, the import failed, and
the fallback `extract_obj_module` resolved to the class definition file
(_connector_environment.py). In editable installs that file is not under
root_dir, producing:

  ValueError: Object ConnectorEnvironment(...) module file
  .../src/flyte/app/_connector_environment.py is not relative to source
  directory .../examples/apps/custom_connector_app and is not an
  installed package.

Walk up the stack past any __post_init__/__init__ frames so the caller
frame always lands on user code, regardless of subclass depth.

fix: run sync sandbox tools off the event loop so traced tools work in agent code mode (#1523)

## Problem

With `Agent(code_mode=True)`, live runs showed **every** tool call
failing with:

```
Deadlock detected: blocking call used in syncify thread flyte_syncify when calling
function <function _fetch_action_outputs ...>, use .aio() if in an async call.
```

Root cause: when the agent is entered through a syncified call (e.g. a
sync `agent.run()`), the whole Monty sandbox loop runs on the
`flyte_syncify` background loop. `ExternalFunctionBridge.execute_monty`
invoked external functions **inline**, so a sync `@flyte.trace` tool's
wrapper made its blocking syncify call (`_fetch_action_outputs`) from
the syncify thread itself — a guaranteed deadlock that the SDK detects
and aborts. The JSON tool-calling path was unaffected because
`_make_callable_tool` already dispatches sync tools via
`asyncio.to_thread`.

Downstream workaround that motivated this fix: unionai/unionai-agents#86
(had to disable code mode entirely).

## Fix

`ExternalFunctionBridge` now routes every non-coroutine-function
external through `asyncio.to_thread` (new `_call_external` helper, used
by both `execute_monty` and `_map_callable`):

- `asyncio.to_thread` copies contextvars, so the Flyte task context —
and therefore tracing — works exactly as it does on the JSON tool path.
- The blocking syncify calls inside sync trace wrappers now happen on a
worker thread while the syncify loop stays free to serve them.
- Side benefit: slow sync tools no longer stall the event loop driving
the sandbox (previously they blocked it outright), including under
`flyte_map`.
- Coroutine functions (`TaskTemplate.aio`, async tools, call-handler
wrappers) keep their inline path, and the existing unwrap loop still
drains coroutines returned by non-coroutine callables (local-mode
`TaskTemplate.aio()`).

## Also in this PR: remove a flaky Python 3.14 test

CI on this PR surfaced a pre-existing flaky failure, unrelated to the
sandbox change:
`test_task_call_sequence.py::test_interleaved_allocations_prevent_id_reuse`
asserted that CPython never hands a freed override object's address to a
later allocation when a same-size "noise" object is allocated in
between. That's unspecified allocator behavior, and the 3.14 runner
reused an address once (`seqs [1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2,1,1]`).

The `id()`-keyed sequencing that test demonstrates is also historical —
the remote controller has keyed sequences on a call key (task identity +
inputs hash + group) via `TaskCallSequencer` since #607, with
deterministic coverage in `test_action_name_stability_gaps.py`. The test
is removed and the file's docstring now notes that the remaining
demonstrations (which hold every object alive, so ids are guaranteed
distinct) are deterministic and describe pre-#607 behavior.

## Verification

- New regression tests drive `orchestrate_local` on the syncify loop
with a sync tool that makes a blocking syncify call (direct call and via
`flyte_map`) — they reproduce the exact production error before the fix
and pass after.
- Repro script confirmed: unfixed bridge → `Deadlock detected: blocking
call used in syncify thread flyte_syncify ...`; fixed bridge → returns
the tool result.
- `tests/flyte/sandbox/` + `tests/flyte/ai/`: 694 passed; sequencing
suites (`test_task_call_sequence.py`,
`test_action_name_stability_gaps.py`): 22 passed. Lint/mypy/ty clean.

feat(cli): add --version to flyte run (#1575)

## What

Adds `--version` to `flyte run`, passed through to
`flyte.with_runcontext(version=...)`.

## Why

- Python callers can set a run's version with
`with_runcontext(version=...)`. The CLI couldn't.
- `with_runcontext` raises `ValueError("Version is required when
copy_style is 'none'")` whenever `copy_style="none"` has no version. So
`flyte run --copy-style none` failed every time, in local mode too:
  ```
$ flyte run --local --copy-style none my_example.py my_task --name World
  ✕ Execution failed: Version is required when copy_style is 'none'
  ```

## Equivalence with the programmatic path

`flyte run <file> <task>` builds its runner with the same
`flyte.with_runcontext(...)` a Python caller uses, then calls
`run.aio(task, ...)`. This change passes `version=` into that call, so
`_Runner` receives exactly what `with_runcontext(version=...)` would
give it. Inside the runner, `version` is used the same way for both:

- **Remote runs of a local task** (`_build_task_spec_from_template`) and
**hybrid runs** (`_run_hybrid`) use `self._version or
code_bundle.computed_version` as the task version.
- **Local runs** (`_run_local`) use `"na"`, so `version` is ignored
there. The `copy_style="none"` check in `with_runcontext` still applies,
which is why local runs need it too.

Two details:

- **Both file-run call sites pass it**, the direct run and the TUI path.
Otherwise `--version` would silently do nothing in the TUI.
- **`deployed-task` does not use it.** `_run_remote` takes a fetched
task's version from the task itself (`task.pb2.task_id.version`), so
`--version` there would be silently ignored. It's rejected instead,
pointing to `env.task:version`. The check runs in
`TaskFiles.get_command`, before anything loads config or fetches the
task: `RunRemoteTaskCommand.get_params` contacts the backend before
`invoke` runs, so a check in `invoke` never fires when there is no
config. The second commit fixes that; CI caught it.

## Tests

Six new tests in `tests/cli/test_run.py`:
- the option exists;
- `from_dict` parses it;
- it's passed to `with_runcontext`, and defaults to `None`;
- `--copy-style none` fails without `--version` and succeeds with it,
through the real `with_runcontext`;
- it's rejected for `deployed-task`.

Results:
- `tests/cli`: 468 passed, both with a Flyte config and in a CI-like
environment with none.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: pass.
- `make check-docstrings`: clean.
- `flyte gen docs --type json | python maint_tools/check_cli_json.py`:
57 commands described, all keys present.

Also run by hand with this branch's CLI:
- `flyte run --local --copy-style none --version v1.0.0 my_example.py
my_task --name World` prints `Hello, World!`.
- The same without `--version` fails with the version error.
- `flyte run --version v1.0.0 deployed-task my_env.my_task` is rejected
with the `env.task:version` hint.

## Noticed, not changed

`flyte run` offers `--copy-style custom`, but `with_runcontext` always
rejects `"custom"` ("not yet supported through with_runcontext"), so
that choice can never succeed from the CLI.

types: preserve pydantic Field metadata on Annotated task inputs

Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^s3://")] and Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, le=1)]
on a task input were flattened to a bare string / float: the type engine
unwrapped Annotated to find a transformer and discarded the metadata, and the
JSON schema builder only read LiteralType.metadata for STRUCT types.

TypeEngine.to_literal_type now records the JSON-schema keys that pydantic
field metadata (Field, annotated_types constraints, StringConstraints,
WithJsonSchema) adds over the bare type in LiteralType.metadata, using
pydantic's own TypeAdapter so the constraint mapping (minLength vs minItems,
exclusiveMinimum, ...) matches pydantic. Structural keys and `default` are
never copied; required-ness still comes from the signature. For unions the
metadata is pushed onto the non-None variants, mirroring pydantic.

literal_type_to_json_schema overlays that metadata for non-STRUCT types and
turns integral doubles from the protobuf Struct back into ints.

EnumTransformer now unwraps Annotated instead of raising, so
Annotated[MyEnum, Field(description=...)] works end to end.

fix: ClusteredTaskEnvironment registers empty custom via flyte deploy (#1598)

## Motivation

flyte deploy registered every ClusteredTaskEnvironment task with an
empty custom, so each run failed in the backend with
[BadTaskSpecification] invalid ClusteredTaskSpec: nil Struct Object
passed after ~34 minutes of retries. ClusteredTaskTemplate read its
settings back through the parent_env weakref, which copy.copy (used by
_deploy._with_local_sys_paths, on by default) and cloudpickle (notebook
bundles) both drop. The same copy also blanked TaskSpec.environment.name
for every deployed task since v2.5.14.

##  Summary

- ClusteredSettings: a frozen snapshot of the clustered fields built in
ClusteredTaskEnvironment.__post_init__ and carried on
_ClusteredPlugin.settings; custom_config/container_args read it instead
of parent_env, so custom and the --runtime=jax arg survive copy and
pickle. A settings-less marker (the in-container routing case) now
raises a clear RuntimeUserError if it ever reaches serialization instead
of registering {}.
- TaskTemplate.__copy__: a shallow copy keeps parent_env; the pickle
hooks are unchanged. Restores environment.name/description on deployed
specs (cloud persists the name and groups actions on it).
- _run.py: run-level _F_SYS_PATH is emitted only for ephemeral task
specs. For a deployed target (TaskDetails, base.task_spec_source ==
DEPLOYED, or the trigger-fire path) the registered spec already carries
the deploy-time value; re-sending the launcher's copy was the wrong
source and duplicated the key, which JobSet (a CRD with env as a
name-keyed map) rejects with a 422. Deployed reruns also strip the
inherited key.
- Tests: copy and cloudpickle round-trips keep custom/runtime flag; bare
marker fails loudly; clone_with rebuilds settings; deploy dry-run keeps
environment.name; _apply_overrides gate cases (ephemeral / deployed /
deployed base / ephemeral base / explicit).

 ## Test Plan

- uv run pytest tests/flyte/clustered tests/flyte/test_deploy.py
tests/flyte/test_task_copy.py tests/flyte/test_run_runspec_chars.py
tests/flyte/test_rerun.py tests/flyte/test_run_trigger.py
tests/user_api/test_run_python_script.py — 249 passed.
- Repro from the issue: on main, copy.copy(f).custom_config(None)
returns {}; on this branch it matches f.custom_config(None).
- Dogfood, default settings (no --no-sync-local-sys-paths): flyte deploy
--version eng26-1349-t1 examples/clustered/ddp_train.py env registers
custom={replicas:2, nprocPerNode:1, runtime:{torchrun:{}},
failurePolicy:{maxRestarts:1}} with environment.name='ddp_env' and
_F_SYS_PATH in the container env (the previously failing copy path ran).
- flyte run deployed-task ddp_env.train_ddp:eng26-1349-t1 --steps 50 →
run ud6zq7ssg47lwj8vx6pz SUCCEEDED, 1 attempt, 2×L4 DDP; runSpec.envs
has no _F_SYS_PATH. Same run with the SDK's previous behavior
(ut9x7v8g6bj7swtvzfrl) failed in 43 ms on the duplicate env name

Reject a script that writes to an output the task never declared

Found by running the example with `outputs` commented out: the job failed on the
cluster with `FLYTE_OUTPUT_SUMMARY: unbound variable`, because the variable is
only exported for a declared output. Correct, but late, and only loud because
that script happens to `set -u`.

Without `set -u` the same mistake expands to the empty string: `cp ./summary.json
""` fails with `cp: cannot create regular file ''`, and if that is not the last
command in a script without `set -e`, the job exits 0 having written nothing.
Nothing downstream catches it, because an output the task never declared is not
something the connector knows to look for. So the failure mode ranges from a
confusing message to silence.

SlurmScriptTask now scans the script at definition time, alongside the existing
File/Dir type check, and refuses a `$FLYTE_OUTPUT_*` reference it will not
export. The error names the variable, what the task does declare, and both fixes.
It also catches a typo against a real output -- $FLYTE_OUTPUT_SUMARY against a
declared `summary`.

Only `$NAME` and `${NAME}` expansions count. Prose in a comment is not a
reference, and a name assembled at run time (`${FLYTE_OUTPUT_${kind^^}}`) does
not match at all, so a script doing something dynamic is left alone rather than
wrongly refused -- a heuristic that fails a valid script would be worse than the
runtime error it replaces.

The variable-name transform moves to script.py, which task.py and connector.py
both already import, so the names the connector exports and the names the check
accepts cannot drift apart. A test asserts they agree.

fix: clustered (JobSet) restart — non-zero exit on failure + terminal-only error.pb (#1204)

## Motivation

Clustered (JobSet) tasks restart the **whole pod set** up to
`failure_policy.max_restarts` times *inside a single Flyte attempt*. Two
things were broken in that flow:

1. **`error.pb` was written on every failed attempt** to the same output
path. A later successful restart left the stale `error.pb` behind, so
the run could be misreported as FAILED despite succeeding. (The original
version of this PR worked around it by *deleting* the stale file on
success — fragile, and it left a window where the error could be read
mid-restart.)
2. **A task failure never produced a non-zero pod exit.** The runtime's
contract is "write `error.pb`, exit 0" (correct for normal tasks, where
the backend reads `error.pb`). But the JobSet controller keys its
gang-restart off the **pod exit code**, not `error.pb`. So a clustered
worker that hit an exception exited 0 → torchrun exited 0 → the Job
"succeeded" → **the JobSet never restarted**, even with `max_restarts >
0`.

## Summary

Replaces the delete-on-success workaround with two complementary fixes:

**1. Write `error.pb` only on the terminal JobSet attempt** (`io.py`)
- `upload_error` skips the write on transient restarts and only writes
once the restart budget is exhausted (`JOBSET_RESTART_ATTEMPT >=
JOBSET_MAX_RESTARTS`).
- New helpers `_get_clustered_max_restarts()` /
`_is_terminal_clustered_attempt()`. Safe fallback: if the budget env is
absent (older operator) or the task isn't clustered, it writes as before
— errors are never silently hidden.
- Removed `_clear_stale_clustered_error_if_needed` / `_delete_path` (no
stale file is ever written now, so there's nothing to delete).

**2. Clustered workers exit non-zero on failure** (`taskrunner.py`)
- After the (now gated) `error.pb` handling, a clustered worker
(`TORCHELASTIC_RUN_ID` present) calls `sys.exit(1)` so torchrun → Job →
JobSet detects the failure and triggers the gang restart. Normal tasks
keep the exit-0 contract.
- Added `_is_clustered_worker()` (refactored out of
`_is_nonzero_rank_clustered_worker`).

Together: the non-zero exit makes the JobSet climb through restart
attempts; the terminal-only `error.pb` write keeps those transient
attempts from poisoning the eventual success.

## Test Plan

- **Unit** — `pytest tests/flyte/internal/runtime/test_taskrunner.py
tests/flyte/clustered/`:
- `upload_error` gating: transient attempt → no write; terminal attempt
→ write; non-clustered → write; missing-budget-env fallback → write;
`max_restarts=0` → write; non-zero rank → no write; `upload_outputs` no
longer deletes.
- exit behavior: clustered failure → `SystemExit(1)`; non-clustered
failure → no exit; clustered success → no exit.
- **End-to-end** — `examples/clustered/ddp_train_restart.py`
(`max_restarts=1`, fails on attempt 0): with the new wheel **and** the
operator deployed, attempt 0 exits non-zero → JobSet restarts → attempt
1 trains → run **SUCCEEDED** with no stale `error.pb`.

local runs and tui should respect disable run cache (#732)

This pull request introduces support for a run-level override to disable
task result caching, ensuring that when caching is disabled for a run,
no cache hits are reported, cache writes are skipped, and the UI
reflects this status. The changes span the core execution logic,
persistence layers, TUI display, and add comprehensive tests for the new
behavior.

Key changes include:

**Run cache disabling logic and propagation:**
- Added a `disable_run_cache` field to `TaskContext`, and ensured this
flag is propagated through local and remote task execution, so that when
it is set, cache reads and writes are skipped.

**Persistence and tracking:**
- Extended the database schema and record-keeping to include the
`disable_run_cache` field, ensuring this information is stored and
loaded with run records. (`src/flyte/_persistence/_db.py`,
`src/flyte/_persistence/_recorder.py`,
`src/flyte/_persistence/_run_store.py`,
`src/flyte/cli/_tui/_tracker.py`)

**TUI (Terminal UI) display improvements:**
- Updated the TUI to display when run cache is disabled at the run
level, both in cache icons and detail screens, overriding any cache
hit/miss indicators. (`src/flyte/cli/_tui/_app.py`,
`src/flyte/cli/_tui/_explore.py`)

**Testing:**
- Added and extended tests to verify that disabling run cache is
correctly handled, persisted, and displayed in the TUI, including new
test cases for the cache icon and run detail screen.
(`tests/cli/test_tui_explore.py`, `tests/cli/test_tui_tracker.py`)

These changes ensure that disabling task result caching for a run is
respected throughout the system and clearly communicated to users.

feat(vllm,sglang): speculative decoding, cache-aware routing, and current engine pins (#1460)

## Motivation

This PR fills in current gaps in the plugin implementation:

- A draft model is a *second* set of weights, and both environments have
room for exactly one — they own a single `model_path` and raise on both
`parameters` and `args`.
- vLLM's `--speculative-config` is JSON and `fserve` runs the command
through a shell, so the blob has to be quoted or the shell eats its
inner quotes.
- Mounts have to sit under `/tmp`, not `/root` — the released Flyte base
image runs non-root.
- The pinned engines (vLLM 0.11.0, SGLang 0.5.2) predate the algorithms
the recipes are about, and both engines have since moved to CUDA 13
wheels that the images' hand-pinned flashinfer layers cannot match.
- Cache-aware routing has to live inside the pod, because Flyte apps
have no session affinity or per-replica address — and the plugin had no
way to express it.

This PR closes those gaps so the recipes' configurations are expressible
natively.

## Summary

**Speculative decoding (both plugins).** New `speculative_config`, plus
optional `draft_model_path` / `draft_model_hf_path`. Draft weights are
mounted as a second `Parameter` next to the target and wired into the
engine — vLLM's single `--speculative-config` JSON blob, SGLang's flat
`--speculative-*` flags (`{"algorithm": "EAGLE3"}` →
`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE3`). Draft-model-free methods (ngram) work
with no mounted weights. The Flyte streaming loader is process-wide and
describes a single set of weights, so configuring a draft model falls
back to downloading both models and warns rather than silently feeding
the target's tensors to the drafter.

**Shell-safe args (both plugins).** `fserve` runs the app with `Popen("
".join(args), shell=True)` (`flyte/_bin/serve.py`), so any token with
spaces or quotes reached the engine mangled — `--speculative-config`
being the obvious casualty. Args are now `shlex.quote`d, except `$VAR`
tokens, which `fserve` expands *before* joining and which quoting would
turn into literals.

**Writable mount path (both plugins).** Model mounts move from
`/root/flyte` to `/tmp/flyte/...`. `_ensure_dest_writable` needs the
image's user to create the parent directory, and the released base image
runs non-root, so `/root` failed with `Permission denied` before the
engine ever started.

**SGLang cache-aware routing.** `router=True` swaps the entrypoint to
`sglang_router.launch_server`; worker count and policy stay ordinary
server args (`--dp-size`, `--router-policy`). Streaming is unavailable
in this mode — the router launches its workers as separate processes
that never load the patched loader — so it falls back to download and
warns.

**SGLang host binding.** The server now binds `0.0.0.0` unless the
caller passes their own `--host`. SGLang's own default is `127.0.0.1`,
which is unreachable from outside the container.

**Engine pins and images.** vLLM `0.11.0` → `0.26.0` (DFlash needs
0.20.1+) and SGLang `0.5.2` → `0.5.16` (DFLASH landed 2026-04, on the
Spec V2 engine that became default in the 2026-06 line). Both now pull
CUDA 13 wheels, so:

- **vLLM image**: `flashinfer-jit-cache` moves to the `cu130` index,
pinned to vLLM's own flashinfer version (`0.6.14`), in a layer *after*
vLLM — layers resolve independently, so an earlier unpinned layer is
just overwritten by vLLM's exact pin and leaves the cache mismatched.
`flashinfer-cubin` is dropped: it publishes no `0.6.14`. Without a
matching jit-cache, the FlashInfer sampler JIT-compiles during warmup
and dies on missing `nvcc`, long after the weights load.
- **SGLang image**: CUDA toolkit `12.8` → `13.0`; the hand-pinned
flashinfer layers are dropped (SGLang pins `flashinfer_python[cu13]`
itself, and a `cu128` jit-cache against a `cu13` flashinfer is actively
wrong); `pre=True` added, which is required rather than cosmetic —
0.5.16 depends on the pre-release `flash-attn-4>=4.0.0b18`, and without
it uv reports the package as simply unsatisfiable. Also ships
`sglang-router` for `router=True`.

Version-tracking constants (`FLASHINFER_VERSION`,
`FLASHINFER_JIT_CACHE_INDEX_URL`, `SGLANG_ROUTER_VERSION`,
`CUDA_TOOLKIT_PACKAGE`) are pulled into `_constants.py` with notes on
what has to be re-checked together on the next bump.

**Examples.** Every example using these plugins hand-rolled an image
that was a near-copy of the plugin default, and each had drifted to a
version *below* the new minimum (vllm 0.11.0 / 0.19.0 / 0.20.0, sglang
0.5.7) — so the shims' version check would have rejected them at
container startup, and their `cu128`/`cu129` flashinfer layers could not
match engines pinning CUDA 13 wheels. Rather than re-pin nine copies,
they now build on `DEFAULT_VLLM_IMAGE` / `DEFAULT_SGLANG_IMAGE`: six use
it as-is, three `.clone(name=...)` it and add only what they actually
need (TriAttention, librosa/soundfile, a separate build cache). The
engine version, its matching flashinfer build and the CUDA toolkit now
live in exactly one place and cannot drift again.

One casualty: the `transformers==4.57.6` pins are gone, because vLLM
0.26 requires `transformers>=5.5.3` — no vLLM new enough for the plugin
can satisfy the old pin. In `vllm_app_artifact.py` that pin carried a
comment claiming newer transformers break the `fserve` tokenizer load
path; there was no way to keep both, so that claim needs re-validating
on a real deploy.

**Prefetch sharding pin.** `flyte.prefetch.hf_model(shard_config=...)`
shards a checkpoint with vLLM's `save_sharded_state`, and this plugin's
`FlyteModelLoader._load_sharded_model` is the only thing that reads
those files back — rebuilding the expected `state_dict` from *its own*
vLLM's model implementation and raising `Missing keys ... in loaded
state!` on anything it cannot fill. The two are halves of one format,
but nothing tied their versions together: `VLLM_SHARDING_IMAGE_PACKAGES`
asked for `vllm>=0.11.0`, a floor rather than a pin, so it installed
whatever was newest at image-build time — two prefetch runs weeks apart
could shard with different vLLMs, and neither was pinned to the one
doing the serving. It is now pinned to `0.26.0`, and the sharding
image's CUDA toolkit moves 12.9 → 13.0 to match the wheels vLLM 0.26
pins (the toolkit is there so startup JIT compiles have an `nvcc`; one
from the wrong CUDA major fails inside a warmup compile). A test in the
vLLM plugin's suite asserts the two constants stay equal, so a one-sided
bump fails in CI rather than at model-load time on a real deploy.

## Test Plan

- 13 new vLLM tests and 19 new SGLang tests covering: draft-model
mounting, HF draft models, draft-model-free (ngram) configs, forced
download when a draft model or the router is configured, the
`speculative_config` validation errors, flag rendering (including
`speculative_`-prefixed keys and booleans), shell quoting of JSON args,
`$VAR` args left unquoted, router entrypoint selection, host defaulting,
and `clone_with` round-trips that add or drop a draft model.
- 2 new tests guarding the prefetch/plugin version contract, verified to
actually fail (with an actionable message) when the two constants are
desynced.
- Existing suites pass unchanged apart from the two intentional
mount-path assertions: **39 passed** (vLLM), **43 passed** (SGLang),
**64 passed** (`tests/flyte/prefetch`).
- All nine example modules import and their app envs build with the
inherited images; `make fmt`, `make mypy`, `make ty` and `make
check-docstrings` clean across the repo.
- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean on both plugins; `mypy`
clean on the changed files (the 2 remaining errors are pre-existing, in
the untouched SGLang shim).

⚠️ **Not exercised:** the container image builds themselves, which need
a GPU-class builder and a registry
(`maint_tools/build_plugin_image.py`). The pins are verified against
PyPI and the flashinfer indexes — `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.14` exists
on `cu130`, and the previously pinned `cu128`/`cu129` indexes top out at
`0.6.9`, so they could never have matched the new engines. Worth a real
build + serve before merge.

**Out of scope, adjacent:** `examples/ml/batch_inference_saturate.py`
and `batch_inference_saturate_app.py` install an unpinned `vllm`
alongside `flashinfer-python==0.6.4` / a `cu129` jit-cache. Unpinned
resolves to 0.26.x, which pins flashinfer exactly at 0.6.14 — so those
layers are both overwritten and CUDA-mismatched. Same bug class as this
PR fixes, but a different subsystem: they use vLLM directly and touch
neither plugin nor the sharded-state format, so they are left alone
here.

## Summary

Adds the missing BigQuery-to-pandas DataFrame decoder.

BigQuery connector outputs use `bq://project:dataset.table` URIs, which
previously fell back to the Parquet decoder and failed with `Protocol
not known: bq`.

The decoder:

- Reads results through the BigQuery Storage API
- Supports column projection
- Handles empty result tables
- Registers automatically with the `bq` protocol

## Testing

- Added decoder, URI parsing, projection, and empty-table tests
- All 42 BigQuery plugin tests pass

Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0


Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's
releases.




2.8.0


🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support


urllib3
is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure
long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or
organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in
Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing
financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and
maintained for the long-haul.


Thank you for your support.


Security


Fixed the following security issues:


    

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or
overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
    • 

  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked()
could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High
severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
    • 

  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium
severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)
    • 





[!IMPORTANT]
urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or
overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that
behavior may require changes.


Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in
proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with
proxy_assert_hostname or
proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates
and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy
connections.






[!NOTE]
CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of
release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.




Deprecations & Removals


    

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry
option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)
    • 



Features


    

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and
Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the
result of parse_url(). (#4945)
    • 

  • Added basic_auth_encoding and
proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to
urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)
    • 



Bugfixes


    

  • 

    Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header
lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112,
preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as
Set-Cookie. (#1362)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with
ProxyManager when
use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing
ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for
HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a
FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)
    

    • 

  • 

    Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool
initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the
queue module after the ConnectionPool is
instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls
class property. This is done because sometimes the
queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such
as by gevent. (#3289)
    

    • 

  • 

    Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of
ValueError when retrying a request whose body had
tell() but not seek(). (#3779)
    

    • 

  • 

    Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating
with the proxy server. (#3785)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread
response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt
when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms
accepted by socket.connect, such as hex
(0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal
integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate
verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading
FullPoolError instead of ValueError when
called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created
with block=True. (#5059)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values
instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool
selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and
HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071,
#5101)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the
assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint
parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy
forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before
sending requests. (#5079)
    

    • 

  • 

    Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential
security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and
HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and
Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on
newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the
same security fixes. (#5091)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding
ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy
identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when
forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.
    

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI,
assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and
continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an
HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax,
rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters,
malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in
HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel
targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization
rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved
characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained
percent-encoded octets. (#5095)
    

    •

overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that
behavior may require changes.

proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with
proxy_assert_hostname or
proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates
and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy
connections.

release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.




Deprecations & Removals


    

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry
option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)
    • 



Features


    

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and
Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the
result of parse_url(). (#4945)
    • 

  • Added basic_auth_encoding and
proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to
urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)
    •

  • 

    Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header
lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112,
preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as
Set-Cookie. (#1362)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with
ProxyManager when
use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing
ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for

FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)
    

    • 

  •

initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the
queue module after the ConnectionPool is
instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls
class property. This is done because sometimes the

    •

response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt

    •

verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created

rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters,
malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in
HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel
targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization
rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved
characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained
percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

fix: normalize ".." in tar member names to prevent extraction failure (#814)

## Motivation:
When a file path referenced via ls_relative_files contains .. (e.g.
project/../sibling/module.py), pathlib's / operator
preserves the .. lexically. This causes create_bundle to write a tar
member name like project/../sibling/module.py, which GNU tar refuses to
extract and some implementations (bsdtar/macOS) create a literal ..
directory instead.

##  Summary:
- `create_bundle (_packaging.py)`: resolve ws_file and source before
relative_to so tar member names are always normalized.
- `ls_relative_files (_utils.py)`: resolve paths before relative_to in
the hash loop so equivalent paths (e.g. project/../sibling/module.py vs
sibling/module.py) produce the same bundle digest.
- Regression test added: creates a two-sibling directory layout, passes
a project/../sibling/module.py path through the full bundle pipeline,
and asserts no tar member contains '..'

Correct how the default cache policy fails for a script task

I had been writing that FunctionBodyPolicy returns sha256("") for a task with no
function, "one constant shared by every script task", and that two unrelated
script tasks would collide. Checked it instead of repeating it: the policy
returns the empty string (`if params.func is None: return ""`), and the cache key
is hash(inputs + task_name + interface + version), so the task name and
interface still separate different tasks. Nothing collides.

The actual defect is narrower and is the one that matters: an empty version
leaves the script out of the key, so editing a script keeps hitting the entry the
previous version wrote. That is what the substituted version fixes, and it is
now what the docstring and README say.

feat(plugins): add flyteplugins-routing, client-side multi-cluster routing

Routes runs across several control planes from the client, using the config
file's `profiles:` section as the target set. For teams running multiple
clusters for data separation or across clouds who want placement decided
locally -- from what the code and its arguments say -- rather than shipped to
a control plane that then re-routes.

The SDK carries no routing code. This is built entirely on named profiles,
`flyte.use_profile`, and the existing CLI plugin-hook mechanism.

Policy: rendezvous ("highest random weight") hashing of task, project, domain
and arguments onto the profile set. The same task on the same arguments
always lands on the same cluster, so repeat work returns to the cluster
holding its cache and its data. Rendezvous rather than `hash(key) % n`
because modulo reshuffles nearly every key when a profile is added or
removed, discarding the locality the policy exists to provide. It declines
when `--profile` already pinned a choice.

Naming: routed runs are named `<tag>-<random>`, so a run can be found later
with no stored state and no search. The tag alphabet excludes `u`, `r` and
`l` -- the platform reserves names starting with those and classifies runs by
the first character -- which is affordable only because the tag is
hash-derived rather than spelled from the profile name. The suffix is random,
not derived from the routing key: two runs of the same task on the same
arguments route to the same profile and would otherwise collide, the second
returning RunAlreadyExistsError.

Two paths, and the split is deliberate:

- `flyte run ...` is routed transparently by a CLI hook. `run` resolves
  through a chain of Click groups, so the hook rewrites `get_command` at each
  level; at the leaf both the task and its parsed arguments are in hand.
- `flyte.run(...)` from a script or orchestrator never goes through Click and
  is NOT routed -- it goes to the default profile. `flyteplugins.routing.run`
  and `.with_runcontext` are drop-ins that apply the same policy there,
  mirroring the `flyte` signatures so the swap is mechanical. Documented
  under "Two paths" and asserted by a test rather than left to be discovered.

Reads: hooks on `get run/logs/action/io/condition`, `abort run/action`,
`signal condition` and `rerun` decode the tag and point the core command at
the right profile. Resolution is pure string work -- a name this plugin did
not mint resolves to nothing and the command runs against the default
profile. There is no search: probing every cluster would cost a round trip
per profile on every lookup and make one unreachable cluster everybody's
problem on every command. Stale and colliding tags take the same path, for
the same reason.

`rerun` needs its profile settled earlier than the rest, since it reads the
source run's interface while Click is still parsing; its hook wraps
`parse_args` and reads the run name from argv beforehand.

These are hooks, not replacement commands, so the core command still runs and
the plugin only chooses the profile it runs under.

fix: show distinct sys.modules keys in duplicate-env error message

When the same file is loaded twice under different import paths (the
classic src/ layout dual-import scenario), ``_check_duplicate_env``
told the user the file was "imported twice under different module
names ('multi_status' and 'multi_status')" -- the two displayed names
were identical, defeating the entire purpose of the message.

The bug: ``_find_env_module`` returned the module object, and the
error formatter read ``module.__name__``. But when the SDK's path-
based loader creates a module via
``importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(file_path.stem, ...)``, both
module objects end up with the *same* ``__name__`` (the file stem),
even though they sit at different sys.modules keys.

Switch ``_find_env_module`` to iterate ``sys.modules.items()`` and
return the (key, module) tuple. The error message now uses the
sys.modules keys -- the distinguishing import paths the user can
actually act on.

Sentry issues
Fixes [FLYTE-SDK-2S](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/7481668212/)

feat(run): unify run/rerun/recover on one _Runner; add flyte.rerun (#1236)

Re-running a finished run used to mean a separate replay path that
duplicated half of `_run_remote`. This folds it into the existing
`_Runner` so `run`, `rerun`, `recover`, and (downstream) `debug` all
share one `with_runcontext`-style API and all return a `remote.Run`.

## Usage

**Python**

```python
import flyte
flyte.init_from_config()

# Re-run a prior run with its exact inputs (fetches task + inputs from the platform — no local code):
flyte.rerun("ul56wcvgqrb9vzhzz5l2")

# Change input parameters (converted against the prior run's interface):
flyte.rerun("ul56wcvgqrb9vzhzz5l2", x_list=[1, 2, 3])

# Substitute new code, reusing the original inputs:
flyte.rerun("ul56wcvgqrb9vzhzz5l2", task_template=fixed_task)
```

**CLI** — `flyte run` (you have local code) and `flyte rerun` (fetch the
run's code) are complementary:

```bash
flyte rerun ul56wcvgqrb9vzhzz5l2                          # fetched code + prior inputs
flyte rerun ul56wcvgqrb9vzhzz5l2 --name retry --follow

flyte run main.py main --rerun-from ul56wcvgqrb9vzhzz5l2  # NEW local code + prior run's inputs
```

| command | code | inputs |
|---|---|---|
| `flyte run f t` | local | CLI |
| `flyte run f t --rerun-from <run>` | local | prior run's |
| `flyte rerun <run>` | fetched | prior run's |

## recover (coming soon)

`recover` (reuse a prior run's succeeded actions, re-run only what
failed/changed) is a run-context knob — `recover=True` recovers from the
run being rerun (rerun-only); a run-name string recovers a fresh `run()`
from a named prior run; it's remote-only and `recover=True` on a plain
`run()` raises. It's **gated** until the backend ships `flyteidl2
RunSpec.recover` (raises a clear `NotImplementedError`; one-line enable
then).

The matching CLI flags — **`flyte rerun --recover`** and **`flyte run
--recover-from <run>`** — are **coming soon**: omitted from the CLI for
now (left as TODOs) until the backend lands, so they don't surface in
the generated CLI docs. The Python `with_runcontext(recover=...)` field
exists today (gated).

`flyte.replay` is removed — `flyte.rerun` is the verb.

## What changed

- `_run_remote`'s back half is extracted into reusable `_Runner`
helpers: `_build_task_spec_from_template`, `_submit_remote` (the only
network call site), and `_apply_overrides` (the single place run-context
maps onto a `RunSpec` — fresh build, or deep-copy-and-merge for rerun).
- New `_Runner.rerun` + `flyte.rerun`; new `flyte rerun` command and
`flyte run --rerun-from`.
- Behavior-preserving: a characterization safety net
(`test_run_runspec_chars.py`) pins the exact
`CreateRunRequest`/`RunSpec` and passes unchanged across the refactor.
Lazy imports kept (no `import flyte` startup regression).

## Verification

~150 run-path unit tests green (mypy + ruff + codespell clean). **E2E on
demo** (local SDK baked into the image via `make dist`): `rerun`
reproduces a baseline exactly, changed-inputs takes effect, `flyte run
--rerun-from` reuses prior inputs with local code.

fix: report a rejected PKCE token exchange as an auth error (FLYTE-SDK-7D)

The authorization-code -> access-token exchange raised a bare RuntimeError
carrying the raw response bytes whenever the identity provider answered with
anything other than 200:

    RuntimeError: Failed to request access token with response: [400]
    b'{\n  "error": "invalid_request",\n  "error_description":
    "client_secret is missing."\n}'

That is a deployment configuration problem -- the OAuth2 application backing
browser login requires a client secret that the PKCE flow does not send -- but
RuntimeError is unclassified, so it escaped to Sentry as an SDK crash and the
user got a Python bytes repr instead of an explanation.

`_token_client.get_token` already raises `AuthenticationError` for exactly this
condition (_token_client.py:157); the PKCE authorization client just never got
the same treatment. `AuthenticationError` is on `_sentry._is_user_error`'s
allow-list and still subclasses RuntimeError, so no caller changes.

Also decode the RFC 6749 section 5.2 error body -- `error`, `error_description`,
`error_uri` -- rather than dumping the raw bytes. The description is the only
part of the exchange that says why the login was rejected. Non-JSON bodies (an
HTML page from a proxy answering the token endpoint) are quoted and truncated.

The sibling `Expected "access_token" in response` ValueError becomes an
AuthenticationError for the same reason. The state-parameter mismatch check is
deliberately left as a ValueError: it guards against a forged callback, and a
genuine SDK bug could also trip it, so it should keep reporting.

fixes FLYTE-SDK-7D

Enhance docstrings with detailed parameter documentation (#810)

## Summary

- Enhance docstrings for 12 classes/protocols with detailed parameter
documentation, format examples, and usage patterns
- Content transferred from the unionai-docs user guide as part of an
information architecture effort to keep procedural content in the user
guide and reference content in the SDK source

## Classes enhanced

| Class | File | Key additions |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `Resources` | `_resources.py` | CPU/memory/GPU/disk/shm format
examples, Kubernetes unit conventions |
| `ReusePolicy` | `_reusable_environment.py` | Capacity math, idle_ttl
vs scaledown_ttl distinction, scaling semantics |
| `Trigger` | `_trigger.py` | Grouped params (core, config, runtime
overrides, metadata), predefined methods note |
| `Cron` | `_trigger.py` | Cron expression quick-reference, common
patterns, timezone notes |
| `FixedRate` | `_trigger.py` | start_time behavior, interval examples |
| `Image` | `_image.py` | Fluent pattern overview, from_*/with_* method
listing with descriptions |
| `TaskEnvironment` | `_task_environment.py` | Three-level configuration
model, per-param override level documentation |
| `Cache` | `_cache/cache.py` | Three behavior modes explained, policy
defaults |
| `CachePolicy` | `_cache/cache.py` | Protocol docstring with custom
implementation example |
| `FunctionBodyPolicy` | `_cache/policy_function_body.py` | Default
policy role, cache invalidation behavior |
| `AppEnvironment` | `app/_app_environment.py` | App-specific params
with accepted values and constraints |
| `Scaling` | `app/_types.py` | Class docstring with common scaling
patterns |

## Motivation

The auto-generated API reference pages derive their content from these
docstrings. Richer docstrings mean richer API docs, allowing the user
guide to link to API reference instead of duplicating parameter
documentation inline. A companion PR in unionai-docs
([unionai/unionai-docs#854](https://github.com/unionai/unionai-docs/pull/854))
trims the duplicated content.

Use non-root flyte user by default in built images (#1016)

## Summary
- Default base image now creates a non-root `flyte` user, chowns
`/home/flyte`, `/root`, and `/opt/venv` to it, sets `WORKDIR
/home/flyte`, and switches `USER flyte` at the end of the local Docker
build.
- Files added via `with_source_folder`, `with_source_file`, and
`with_code_bundle` are copied with `--chown=flyte:flyte` so the runtime
user can read them.
- Refactored the user-creation layer from internal `_DockerLines` to
`Commands` + `WorkDir` so the remote builder (whose protobuf IDL only
understands proto-backed Layer types) also applies the user setup.

## Behavior notes
- **Local builds** (including the published default base built via
`maint_tools/build_default_image.py --builder=local`): runtime user is
`flyte`.
- **Remote builds**: the Union remote image builder backend currently
hardcodes its own non-root user (`union`, uid 65532) and ignores
SDK-side `USER` directives — the Layer IDL has no `USER` field. Verified
by running a probe task on `dogfood.cloud-staging.union.ai`:
    ```
    user=union uid=65532 gid=65532
    home=/home/union cwd=/home/flyte
    /opt/venv owner=root:root
    ```
Making the remote builder also default to `flyte` will require a
backend-side change (either adding a `USER` Layer to the IDL or aligning
the backend's hardcoded user).

## Test plan
```python
import getpass
import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import flyte

image = (
    flyte.Image.from_debian_base()
    .with_source_file(Path("README.md"))
)

env = flyte.TaskEnvironment(name="check_user_env", image=image)


@env.task
async def check_user() -> str:
    user = getpass.getuser()
    uid = os.getuid()
    gid = os.getgid()
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    cwd = os.getcwd()
    try:
        venv_owner = subprocess.check_output(["stat", "-c", "%U:%G", "/opt/venv"]).decode().strip()
    except Exception as e:
        venv_owner = f"<error: {e}>"

    readme = "/home/flyte/README.md"
    try:
        readme_owner = subprocess.check_output(["stat", "-c", "%U:%G", readme]).decode().strip()
    except Exception as e:
        readme_owner = f"<error: {e}>"

    try:
        with open(readme, "a") as f:
            f.write("\n# appended by check_user task\n")
        with open(readme) as f:
            tail = f.readlines()[-1].strip()
        modify_result = f"OK (last line: {tail!r})"
    except Exception as e:
        modify_result = f"FAILED: {e}"

    msg = (
        f"user={user} uid={uid} gid={gid}\n"
        f"home={home} cwd={cwd}\n"
        f"/opt/venv owner={venv_owner}\n"
        f"{readme} owner={readme_owner}\n"
        f"modify {readme}: {modify_result}"
    )
    print(msg)
    return msg


if __name__ == "__main__":
    flyte.init_from_config(".flyte/config.yaml")
    run = flyte.run(check_user)
    print(f"Run URL: {run.url}")
    run.wait(quiet=False)
    print(run.outputs())

```

fix: flyte.run always returns a Run; drop isinstance narrowing asserts from examples

Runner.run was typed `-> Union[R, Run]` because hybrid mode returned the
task's raw outputs while remote/local modes returned a Run handle. That
union forced `assert isinstance(run, Run)` narrowing at ~75 example call
sites to access `.url` / `.wait()` / `.outputs()`.

Make the runtime match the intended contract instead: hybrid mode now wraps
its natively-computed outputs in the same inline Run wrapper local mode uses
(extracted to module-level `_wrap_inline_run`), so `Runner.run` is honestly
typed `-> Run` in every mode. `wait()` on the wrapper is an immediate no-op
and `outputs()` serves the captured values, as before for local runs.

Remove the now-redundant asserts (and their `from flyte.remote import Run`
imports where unused) from 70 example files, and update the hybrid example
to read results via `run.outputs()`.

Hybrid mode is documented as test-only; the only consumer reading its return
value was examples/advanced/hybrid_mode.py, updated here.

cli: add --custom-context and --custom-context-from-env to flyte run (#1713)

## Summary

Adds two repeatable options to `flyte run` so custom context can be set
without a Python launcher:

- `--custom-context KEY=VALUE`
- `--custom-context-from-env VAR` (key is `VAR`) or
`--custom-context-from-env KEY=VAR`. Errors if `VAR` is unset.

```
flyte run \
  --custom-context experiment=calibration \
  --custom-context-from-env API_BASE_URL \
  deployed-task my_env.my_task:v1
```

Values are merged and passed to
`flyte.with_runcontext(custom_context=...)` for file tasks,
`--local`/`--tui`, and `deployed-task`. `--custom-context` wins when
both flags set the same key. Reserved context keys (kickoff time,
produced artifacts) are rejected. The help text notes that custom
context is stored as run metadata and should not hold secrets.

Requested by a user whose agents launch deployed tasks from the CLI.

## Test plan

- Unit tests for parsing (env lookup, `KEY=VAR` rename, precedence, `=`
in values, invalid input, reserved keys) and for wiring into
`with_runcontext` for both a file task and `deployed-task`.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_run.py tests/cli/test_run_remote_defaults.py`:
104 passed.
- Local end to end: `FOO_TOKEN=x flyte run --local --custom-context
experiment=calibration --custom-context-from-env FOO_TOKEN ctx_task.py
main`. A child task's `flyte.get_custom_context()` returned both keys.

fix(deploy): propagate --image to tasks in every environment, not just the first (#1566)

## Problem

`flyte deploy --image <image> --recursive <module>` propagates the image
correctly when the module defines a single `TaskEnvironment`:

```python
env = flyte.TaskEnvironment(name="test-environment")

@env.task
async def example_task(x: int) -> int:
    return x

@env.task
async def another_example_task(y: int) -> list[int]:
    return list(await asyncio.gather(*[example_task(x=x) for x in range(y)]))
```

But as soon as a second environment is involved — either a `clone_with`
override or a plain second `TaskEnvironment` — the nested task runs on
`ghcr.io/flyteorg/flyte:py3.11-v2.7.1` instead of the `--image` value:

```python
env = flyte.TaskEnvironment(name="test-environment")
med = flyte.TaskEnvironment(name="medium-environment", resources=flyte.Resources(cpu="0.5"))

@med.task
async def example_task(x: int) -> int:      # <-- runs on the default image
    return x

@env.task
async def another_example_task(y: int) -> list[int]:
    return list(await asyncio.gather(*[example_task(x=x) for x in range(y)]))
```

There is no error — just the wrong image.

## Root cause

1. `plan_deploy` puts every environment not reachable through
`depends_on` into **its own `DeploymentPlan`**. Two independent envs →
two plans.
2. `apply` called `_build_images` per plan, so each plan got an
`ImageCache` containing **only its own env**.
3. That cache is serialized into the pod's `--image-cache` container arg
(`_task.py`), and at runtime a parent task resolves a *child* task's
container image from it via `lookup_image_in_cache(sc, child_env_name,
child_image)` (`task_serde.py`).
4. For a child in a sibling env the lookup misses. The fallback branch

   ```python
if image._ref_name is None and (not serialize_context.image_cache or
len(image._layers) == 0):
       return image.uri
   ```

returns `image.uri` — and on a released flyte wheel the default
`Image.from_debian_base()` has **zero layers**, so the miss silently
resolves to the unbuilt default image rather than raising
`MissingEnvironment`.

Reproduced locally: for the snippet above, `plan_deploy` yields 3 plans
whose caches are `{'test-environment': ...}`, `{'medium-environment':
...}`, `{'overrides': ...}` — each blind to the others.

## Fix

Build every plan's images up front in `deploy` and hand **all** plans
the merged cache, so any env deployed in the same invocation is
resolvable from any task's serialization context — with or without a
`depends_on` link.

- Extracted `_build_images_for_plans`, which is the merge `build_images`
already performed, and made it build plans **concurrently** (`deploy`
previously got that parallelism for free by gathering over per-plan
`apply` calls).
- `apply` takes an optional pre-built `image_cache`; when omitted it
builds for its plan alone, so standalone callers are unchanged.

Note the merged cache now feeds the deployment version hash. That is
correct rather than churn: the cache is part of the container args, so a
changed sibling image genuinely *is* a changed deployment. Version stays
stable while sibling image URIs do.

This does not remove the `depends_on` requirement for envs deployed in
*separate* invocations — that case still raises the existing actionable
`MissingEnvironment` error.

One behavior change worth calling out: `deploy` now reads
`get_init_config()` itself, so `flyte.deploy(...)` on an uninitialized
client raises `InitializationError` from `deploy` rather than from the
`apply` call it delegates to. Same exception type, same guidance,
marginally earlier.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `tests/flyte/test_deploy_image_cache.py`:

- `test_build_images_for_plans_merges_cli_image_across_independent_envs`
— asserts three independently-planned envs (including a `clone_with`
one) all land in one cache carrying the `--image` override.
- `test_deploy_gives_every_plan_the_merged_image_cache` — drives
`flyte.deploy(...)` end to end and asserts every deployed env's
`SerializationContext` sees all envs, and that the parent's context
resolves the sibling task's image to the `--image` override instead of
the default.

Rebased onto `main` to pick up #1573 (`dry_run`, with the deprecated
`dryrun` alias). The two `test_deploy.py` dry-run tests isolate `deploy`
by patching `plan_deploy`/`apply`; they now also patch `get_init_config`
and `_build_images_for_plans`, since `deploy` gained that collaborator.

Verified: full `tests/flyte` + `tests/cli` suite passes (4363 passed, 9
skipped), plus `make mypy`, `make ty`, `make fmt`. The two failures in
that run —
`test_keyring_store::test_retrieve_degrades_when_keyring_not_installed`
and `test_int_image_builder::test_real_build` — are pre-existing and
environmental (keyring installed locally; no container registry
configured); both fail identically on `origin/main`.

task.override() with a `PodTemplate.with_termination_grace_period(int | timedelta)`
builder method, matching the existing `allow_fuse()` / `allow_nested_sandboxing()`

knob lives on the pod-template abstraction it belongs to (room for more helpers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Deliver known_hosts_data to the connector instead of dropping it

`known_hosts_secret` was plumbed the whole way -- validated on the config,
serialized into `secrets`, resolved by the backend, delivered to the connector --
and then thrown away. Only `get_logs` even declared the kwarg, and it passed
`_transport_for_meta(meta, ssh_private_key)` anyway; `create`, `get` and `delete`
let it fall into **kwargs. `_transport` had no parameter for it at all, so the
branch in SSHTransport that parses inline entries was dead code.

The effect is the worst kind: a task asking for host-key verification by secret
silently got none of its entries, and nothing about the connection looks
different when that happens.

All four methods now declare it and thread it through. The transport cache keys
on a digest of the entries as well as the key, so two tasks with different
known_hosts cannot share a connection -- without that the first one to connect
would decide host-key policy for the rest.

The path form (`known_hosts` / FLYTE_SLURM_KNOWN_HOSTS) was never affected, and I
verified that against a real login node: with the correct file the connection
succeeds, and with a valid-but-wrong host key asyncssh refuses with
HostKeyNotVerifiable. That path was working as documented.

Mitigate cross device issue (#960)

### Problem

`ObstoreParallelReader.download_files` downloads chunks into a
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (defaults to `/tmp`)
then moves each completed file to the target directory via
`aiofiles.os.replace` (which calls `os.rename` under the
hood). When the container has `/tmp` on a separate filesystem from the
destination (e.g. a tmpfs mount), `os.rename`
  fails with:

`OSError: [Errno 18] Invalid cross-device link:
'/tmp/tmpcdwfp9ad/fast<...>.tar.gz' -> '/root/fast<...>.tar.gz'`

This was observed in production at MyHeritage after they bumped to a new
base image that mounted /tmp as
tmpfs. The error was hidden inside a Python 3.11+ ExceptionGroup which
made the surface-level error appear
  unrelated.

 ### Tests

  Three new unit tests are added (no sandbox / real S3 required):

  - test_download_files_single_file — happy path with a mocked store
  - test_download_files_multipart — verifies multi-chunk reassembly
- test_download_files_no_cross_device_error — regression test: wraps
aiofiles.os.replace to raise EXDEV when the
source is outside target_prefix, confirming the fix keeps the staging
file on the same device

fix(config): parse list-valued config entries read from env vars

Every config entry doubles as an env var (`admin.command` -> FLYTE_ADMIN_COMMAND),
but `ConfigEntry` applied no transform to the value it read, so a list-typed entry
came back as the raw string. `FLYTE_ADMIN_COMMAND="mint-token --audience flyte"`
reached the external-command authenticator as a str, and

    asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*self._cmd)

spread it one argument per *character*. Same shape for the proxy command and for
scopes.

Add transforms so an env-supplied value is normalized to a list: a JSON array for
arguments that contain spaces, otherwise shlex.split for a command line and a
comma/whitespace split for a value list. YAML already yields a list and passes
through untouched, so the transforms are idempotent on the file path.

Also correct the AUTH_MODE docstring, which listed flytekit-1 spellings
('standard', 'basic', 'client_credentials') that the authenticator factory does
not match on, and omitted ExternalCommand and Passthrough entirely.
