fix: normalize the Image DSL's path arguments consistently

fixes FLYTE-SDK-8A

The image builder's path arguments normalize inconsistently, so whether a `str` or a `Path`
works depends on which argument you are filling. Both directions fail late, far from the call
that introduced the value.

1. `CopyConfig.__post_init__` normalizes `src` into a `Path` but left `dst` as passed, so a
   `Path` dst surfaced only in `_get_hash_digest` -> `CopyConfig.update_hash`:

       hasher.update(self.dst.encode("utf-8"))
       AttributeError: 'PosixPath' object has no attribute 'encode'

   which aborts `flyte deploy` during the image-existence check. That is FLYTE-SDK-8A, whose
   crashing frame reads `CopyConfig(1, PosixPath('../../dbt_utsikt'), PosixPath('.'))`.

   The same `Path` also defeats the `dst == "."` test in `with_source_folder`, so `dst=Path(".")`
   silently took the `copy_contents_only=True` path -- copying the folder's contents instead of
   the folder. That one never raises.

2. `with_uv_project`, `with_poetry_project` and `with_pixi_project` each coerce their first path
   argument from a `str` and leave the second untouched, so `uvlock=`/`poetry_lock=`/`pixi_lock=`
   as a `str` reach `validate()` as `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'exists'` --
   three for three, while the sibling argument in the same signature accepts a str fine.

Normalizing is what the rest of the codebase already assumes: `remote_builder` compensates with
`dst=str(layer.dst)` at both call sites, and `with_dockerignore` coerces with
`DockerIgnore(path=str(path))`. `WorkDir.workdir` is the same shape as `CopyConfig.dst` -- a
str-annotated path field with a bare `.encode()` -- and is normalized too.

Signatures widen to state what was already accepted. Coercion happens at the boundary, so the
narrow dataclass annotations stay true and both mypy and ty verify the result with no suppression.

Reachability: the FLYTE-SDK-8A crash is under `cli/_deploy.py`'s `@capture_errors` and
`AttributeError` is not filtered by `_is_user_error`, which is why it reached Sentry as an SDK crash.

We will store flyte task git repo host url in the backend when sending a
deploy request request to the run service. The url will be respond in
the GetTaskDetails api.

1. If task code file is under git repo and the git tree is clean, the
url will be suffixed with line number.

the url will only points to the code file in remote repo.
3. If task code file is not under git repo, the url will not be sent to
the backend.
4. The SDK will choose origin as default remote. If origin remote does
not exist, the SDK will sort remotes alphabetically and choose the first
one.

fix: raise InitializationError for missing project/domain (#1081)

## Summary

`require_project_and_domain` raised a plain `ValueError` when
`cfg.project` or `cfg.domain` was unset. The error message itself is
already actionable (`"Project must be provided to initialize the client.
Please set 'project' in the 'task' section of your config file, or pass
it directly to flyte.init(project='your-project-name')."`), but
`ValueError` is not in `_is_user_error`'s filter set, so every
occurrence lands in Sentry as an unhandled SDK crash — purely
user-config feedback being logged as if the SDK had bugged out.

filtered from Sentry via `_is_user_error` (#1056), so this stops logging

refactor(deepinfer)!: simplify the API to DeepInfer, deepinfer_image, clustered env

Addresses review feedback on #1701: the exposed methods were hard to follow and
the image hard-coded a distro- and arch-specific CUDA keyring URL.

API: 17 exports become 3. `DeepInfer` owns a lazily started pool of engine
processes (one per GPU by default) that stays warm for the life of the task
process, so a reusable container reloads nothing between invocations.
`generate` shards the prompts, applies sampling/structured-output options,
decodes, and returns results in input order (`llm.generate(...)` in sync code,
`await llm.generate.aio(...)` in async tasks). Structured output takes a
Pydantic model, dict or JSON string via `json_schema=`, or `regex=`/`grammar=`,
and parses the result. Callers no longer write module-level worker functions,
partials, `SamplingParams`, `setup_common_env`, or token decoding.

The accelerator constants and `accelerator_kind` are no longer public: they
clashed with Flyte's own accelerator strings (`gpu="B200:8"`) and were only
ever needed internally. `_launch.py` is gone; `_bootstrapping.py` is internal.

Image: `default_deepinfer_image`/`deepinfer_image_from_source` collapse into
`deepinfer_image()`. It builds on NVIDIA's official
`nvidia/cuda:<version>-devel-ubuntu24.04`, which ships the CUDA toolkit for
both amd64 and arm64, instead of installing a keyring pinned to
debian12/x86_64 — that URL broke every arm64 host (GB200 Grace) and any base
past bookworm. Upstream has no tags, so the source build pins a commit
(`commit=` to move it). `deepinfer_image(base=...)` layers the plugin onto a
prebuilt image, with `python=` for one whose DeepInfer lives in its own env.

Tests: a stand-in DeepInfer package (tests/stub) lets the engine pool run in
real spawned processes without a GPU, covering sharding, device pinning,
process reuse, multi-node rank splitting, structured parsing, and load failures.

feat(logging): log Python warnings through the root logger Flyte sets up

With reset_root_logger, Flyte gives the root logger its own handler, so
lines from libraries are formatted like Flyte's, as JSON under
LOG_FORMAT=json. Python warnings don't go through logging, though. They
are still printed to stderr as plain text, where a log collector that
reads severity from structured lines finds none, and GKE's Cloud
Logging marks every such line ERROR.

_setup_root_logger now calls logging.captureWarnings(True), so warnings
go to the "py.warnings" logger and propagate to the root handler it
just added, at WARNING and in the same format as other lines. It does
this only when it resets the root logger: without a root handler, the
standard library gives "py.warnings" a NullHandler and captured
warnings are dropped instead of printed.

fix: wrap docker buildx ls/create failures as ImageBuildError

`docker buildx create --name flytex ...` (and `docker buildx ls`) run with
`check=True`, so a CalledProcessError bubbled out of `_ensure_buildx_builder`
raw and was reported to Sentry as an SDK crash (FLYTE-SDK-4R / FLYTE-SDK-5J)
even though the failure is a local Docker environment problem (daemon down,
driver missing, or a leftover/locked builder), not an SDK bug.

Wrap both subprocess calls in `ImageBuildError` (a `RuntimeUserError`, filtered
from Sentry) with an actionable message that includes the captured stderr and
points at `docker buildx rm flytex` / the remote image builder. If the create
fails because the builder already exists (concurrent build), reuse it instead
of failing.

fixes FLYTE-SDK-4R
fixes FLYTE-SDK-5J

fix: validate a bare `cache=` the way a `Cache(behavior=...)` is validated

`TaskTemplate.__post_init__` normalized the bare `cache=` spelling with a
three-case `match` that has no `case _`:

    if isinstance(self.cache, str):
        match self.cache:
            case "auto":     self.cache = Cache(behavior="auto")
            case "override": self.cache = Cache(behavior="override")
            case "disable":  self.cache = Cache(behavior="disable")

Anything else fell through and stayed on the task as the raw value the user
typed. `@env.task(cache="always")` was accepted and stored as the string
`'always'`, while `Cache(behavior="always")` raises a clean ValueError naming the
valid set -- the same value, two spellings, opposite treatment.

The alias table is the sharper half. `_CACHE_BEHAVIOR_ALIASES` maps "enable",
"on", "off", "no" and five more onto canonical behaviors, and its comment says it
exists to keep `cache="enable"` working "instead of crashing with a ValueError
that ends up in Sentry as an SDK error". The decorator is where that spelling is
typed, and it is the one place the table never ran: `@env.task(cache="enable")`
left `task.cache == "enable"`, a str. `app/extras/_webhook_app.py` and
`ai/mcp/_tools.py` both read `<task>.cache.behavior`, which against a str is
`AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'behavior'`.

`cache_from_request` is the same coercion `task_serde` already applies, and it is
the only path that runs `Cache.__post_init__` -- where the alias table and the
error message both live. The `match` was a subset re-implementation of it that
drifted; calling the helper deletes the duplicate rather than extending it.

Sibling evidence that the unchecked field was the exception, not the rule: in the
same `__post_init__`, `service_account` raises a clean TypeError and `retries`
raises a clean ValueError as of #1594. `cache` was the one left silent.

fix: treat Resources(gpu=0) as no accelerator instead of raising

`Resources.__post_init__` accepts any GPU count `>= 0`, and the suite pins that
boundary -- `test_resources_gpu_with_negative_int` asserts `-1` is rejected with
exactly "gpu must be greater than or equal to 0", which makes `0` the intended
valid edge. `get_device()` then passed the count straight to `Device`, which
requires `quantity >= 1`, so the two validators contradicted each other.

The failure is not confined to a direct `get_device()` call. The serialization
path guards on `is not None`, and `0 is not None`, so every task carrying
`gpu=0` raised on the way to the backend:

    get_proto_resources(Resources(cpu=1, gpu=0))
    ValueError: GPU quantity must be at least 1

That makes a computed count a trap -- `Resources(cpu=1, gpu=num_gpus)` builds
cleanly when `num_gpus` is 0 and then fails at registration with a message
naming neither the field the user set nor the value behind it.

Return `None` from `get_device()` for `gpu == 0`, which is what "no
accelerator" already means downstream: both `resources_serde` call sites
already handle a `None` device, so no GPU entry is emitted and nothing else
changes.

Fixes flyteorg/flyte#7995

mount() now accepts max_uploads, attr_cache, entry_cache, and
dir_entry_cache. Defaults preserve safe behaviour (no caching beyond

fix: filter pyqwest transport errors from Sentry (FLYTE-SDK-6H)

connectrpc's HTTP transport is pyqwest, so control-plane RPCs
(SelectCluster, CreateRun, ...) surface transport failures as
pyqwest.ReadError / WriteError / StreamError rather than the httpx
equivalents the Sentry filter already covers.

FLYTE-SDK-6H is an HTTP/2 stream reset mid-body ("Error reading
content") that reaches the user as
ConnectError <- pyqwest.StreamError. A stream reset is a
connection/protocol condition between client and server -- every
StreamErrorCode describes one -- so it is a transient network failure,
not an SDK bug, and should not be reported as a crash.

These are plain Exception subclasses (not OSError), so they need an
explicit isinstance check. pyqwest is a transitive dependency, so the
import is guarded like the existing httpx one.

fixes FLYTE-SDK-6H

fix: report a non-string memory/disk/shm against the field that was wrong (#1581)

## What

`Resources.memory`, `.disk` and `.shm` are declared as Kubernetes
quantity **strings** and are handed to protobuf string fields untouched,
so nothing ever checked them. A non-string survived `__post_init__` and
only failed much later, during serialization:

```
TypeError: bad argument type for built-in operation
```

raised inside `resources_serde` — SDK frames, naming neither the field
that was wrong nor the task it came from.

`cpu` never had the problem, because `_get_cpu_resource_entry` does
`str(cpu)` (it legitimately accepts an int or float core count). The
other three quantities have no such coercion, and that asymmetry is what
hid the gap:

```python
def _get_cpu_resource_entry(cpu: CPUBaseType) -> ...:
    return tasks_pb2.Resources.ResourceEntry(..., value=str(cpu))   # coerced

def _get_memory_resource_entry(memory: str) -> ...:
    return tasks_pb2.Resources.ResourceEntry(..., value=memory)     # not coerced
```

Reproduced on `main`, 4 for 4 — every one dies in serde, `cpu` is the
control:

| `Resources(...)` | before |
|---|---|
| `memory=1024` | `TypeError: bad argument type for built-in operation`
|
| `memory=(1024, 2048)` | `TypeError: bad argument type for built-in
operation` |
| `disk=10` | `TypeError: bad argument type for built-in operation` |
| `shm=1024` | `TypeError: bad argument type for built-in operation` |
| `cpu=2` *(control)* | serializes fine |

## Fix

Validate the three quantity fields in `__post_init__`, exactly the way
#1560 did for `gpu`, so the mistake is reported against the task
definition that caused it rather than surfacing as an opaque crash at
deploy time.

**Reject rather than coerce.** `memory=1024` is a plausible mistake, and
`str(1024)` is a *valid* Kubernetes quantity meaning 1024 **bytes** —
coercing would quietly deploy a task with a thousandth of the memory the
user asked for.

The guard deliberately does not narrow the accepted surface: `cpu` stays
untouched (it is not a quantity string), `shm="auto"`, the `(request,
limit)` pairs and every unset field all still work. It runs *after* the
existing pair-length check, so a 3-tuple keeps its own more specific
message.

## How this was found

Technique: audit the *fix sites* of a merged fix rather than the Sentry
corpus. #1560 added a guard for `gpu`, a field typed as a Union whose
unchecked arms only failed later in serialization. `memory`/`disk`/`shm`
are its siblings in the same dataclass with the same shape of gap.

## Notes

- **No Sentry issue and no GitHub issue to close.** This is a code-audit
finding, like #1537 / #1546 / #1549 / #1559 — there is no `fixes
FLYTE-SDK-XX` trailer because nothing in the corpus has fired for it. It
is capture-reachable, though: `cli/_deploy.py`'s `@capture_errors`
covers serialization, so this *would* be filed as an SDK crash if a user
hit it.
- Distinct from flyteorg/flyte#7991 (the `pod_spec_from_resources` key
map), which is closed and fixed by #1545.

## Test plan

- 5 new tests reproduce the crash for each affected field/shape;
verified they fail on `main` with `DID NOT RAISE` and pass with the fix.
- 9 new tests pin the accepted surface so the guard cannot narrow it,
plus one that the pair-length message still wins and one end-to-end
serialization check.
- `tests/user_api/test_resources.py` +
`tests/internal/runtime/test_resources_serde.py`: **135 passed**.
- Broader sweep (`-k "resource or serde or pod_spec or deploy"`): **442
passed**.
- `make fmt`, `ruff check`, `mypy`, `ty`, `check-docstrings` all clean.

Claim new flyteplugins PyPI names at merge time, not release time

PyPI limits each account to creating 4 new projects per 24h
(pypi/support#10572), which broke the v2.7.0 release for the new
flyteplugins-github and flyteplugins-llamacpp packages (429), and an
unpublished name is squattable by anyone -- four flyteplugins names
were lost exactly that way and are now quarantined.

Add a claim-plugin-names workflow that:
- fails a PR early (with the rate-limit rationale) when it adds more
  than 4 new flyteplugins distributions, so it gets split before merge;
- publishes a 0.0.0a0 claim wheel for every still-unregistered name as
  soon as a plugin lands on main;
- drains any backlog at 4/day on a daily schedule (e.g. names PyPI
  frees from quarantine later).

Release runs of publish.yml then only ever upload to existing projects
and never hit the new-project creation limit.

Record serving facts when prefetching a HuggingFace model

The deploy path reads `flyte.io/serving` off a model artifact to decide which
GPUs it fits on and which engines can load it. Nothing wrote that key, so every
model published through the SDK arrived without it and could not be deployed --
the consumer has existed for a while against a producer that did not.

Prefetch is the right place for it: it already downloads config.json, and it
already receives per-file sizes from the Hub that it was throwing away.

Everything here is read from the Hub's metadata rather than from the weights,
so the same derivation works before a byte is downloaded -- which is what will
let a caller size a model it has not fetched yet.

Two details worth knowing:

  - architectures is written as a list. It was being comma-joined into a
    scalar, which would deserialize as one bogus architecture name and fail
    every engine-support lookup.
  - GPT-2-family configs spell their geometry n_layer/n_head/n_embd, which
    transformers reconciles through each config class's attribute_map. Reading
    the raw JSON sees the original names, so a missed alias silently zeroes the
    KV-cache term -- and that under-estimates VRAM, the direction that OOMs a
    deploy rather than merely wasting a GPU.

Deriving the facts is best-effort: a model that cannot be measured is still a
perfectly good artifact, so a failure publishes without facts rather than
failing a download that may have taken an hour.

Verified against the live Hub: Qwen3-0.6B (751M params, 1.5GB bf16, GQA at 8 KV
heads), Qwen3-32B (65.5GB across shards), gpt2 (legacy config names, and ships
both .bin and .safetensors without double-counting), and bert-base (no head_dim
or kv_heads, absorbed by the consumer's fallbacks).

extras: public model streamer; vLLM flyte-streaming load format (#1667)

## Summary

The safetensors streamer
(`flyte.app.extras._model_loader.SafeTensorsStreamer`) is reachable only
through `VLLMAppEnvironment` / `SGLangAppEnvironment`, configured by env
vars read at import. Its one public method, `get_tensors()`, runs an
`asyncio.Runner`, so it raises inside a running event loop. Every async
task body runs in one, so a reusable task can't use it to load a model
in an `alru_cache`d bootstrap (the `batch_inference_saturate.py`
pattern).

This PR exposes it publicly. Weights stream from object storage as
parallel byte ranges, and each tensor is handed over as soon as it
lands. Nothing is written to local disk, and host memory holds only the
tensors still in flight.

**`flyte.extras.model_streamer`** (core; torch stays a lazy import, so
`flyte.extras` and the import profile are unchanged)
- `ModelStreamer`:
  - async `stream()`
- thread-backed `stream_sync()` that works from any thread: bounded
hand-off, errors re-raised, clean early stop
  - `state_dict()`
- `load_into(module)` for any `nn.Module` built on `meta` with
`empty_weights()`: assign semantics, re-ties HF tied weights, strict
check
  - `download_metadata()` for config and tokenizer files
- `load_hf_model(path, device="cuda")`: a `transformers` model built on
`meta`, with weights streamed onto the device. `base_model_prefix` is
reconciled the way `from_pretrained` does it.

**`flyteplugins.vllm.model_streamer`** (flyteplugins-vllm)
- `load_format="flyte-streaming"`, registered through the
`vllm.general_plugins` entry point, which vLLM runs in every process it
starts (engine core and TP workers included). It is configured through
`model_loader_extra_config` rather than env vars.
- `engine_args(path)` downloads only config and tokenizer, then returns
the `LLM(...)` kwargs: `LLM(**await engine_args("s3://…"),
max_model_len=4096)`.
- It is vLLM's `DefaultModelLoader` with the primary weights iterator
swapped, so vLLM's weight loaders still handle placement, TP sharding
and quantization.

**Examples** (each prefetches its model with `flyte.prefetch.hf_model()`
and binds the model artifact to a `Dir` input)
- `examples/genai/vllm/vllm_task_streamed.py`: minimal offline
`vllm.LLM` in a reusable GPU task, engine built once in an `alru_cache`d
bootstrap with `engine_args()`. Uses SmolLM2-135M.
- `examples/ml/batch_inference_streamed.py`: the
`batch_inference_saturate.py` pattern (reusable GPU workers,
`alru_cache` bootstrap, `TokenBatcher`), with the model streamed into
the GPU. Built on `DEFAULT_VLLM_IMAGE`.
- `examples/ml/embed_streamed.py`: `load_hf_model` on reusable GPU
workers.
- `plugins/vllm/README.md`: new section, "Streaming weights into vLLM
inside a task".

The existing private loader used by `VLLMAppEnvironment` /
`SGLangAppEnvironment` is unchanged.

## Test plan

- `tests/flyte/extras/test_model_streamer.py` (11 tests, skipped without
torch) runs against a sharded tiny Llama checkpoint in an obstore
`LocalStore`:
- every tensor matches, both inside a running loop and from
`stream_sync`
  - dtype casting
  - error propagation and early close
- `load_into` on a meta model: buffers kept, tied weights re-tied,
strict mismatch reported
  - `load_hf_model` logits match `from_pretrained`
  - loading a bare `LlamaModel` from a `ForCausalLM` checkpoint
- `plugins/vllm/tests/test_model_streamer.py` ran against real vLLM
0.26.0 on CPU:
- `load_general_plugins()` registers `flyte-streaming` from the entry
point (confirmed independently of the test's own `register()` call)
  - the default loader's extra-config validation sees only its own keys
- `get_all_weights` streams every tensor correctly from a thread with a
running loop
  - a missing path gives a clear error
  - The full plugin suite passes: 41 passed.
- `tests/flyte/extras`: 247 passed, 1 skipped (the new file, without
torch).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, mypy (src/flyte/extras, the
plugin module, the examples), `check_docstring_style.py` and
`check-import-profile` are clean. `ty check` reports 3 diagnostics, all
pre-existing in untouched files (`_pod.py`, `remote/_progress.py`).

**Not yet verified on a GPU.** The full `LLM()` load into GPU memory and
the examples on a cluster are still to run.

## Summary

Fix `ContainerTask` deployment when it declares required inputs.

`ContainerTask` was constructing its `NativeInterface` with `None` as

matching required inputs on function-backed tasks.

  - their interface defaults use the required-parameter sentinel; and

Fix stale auth header accumulation on ConnectRPC retry

The old gRPC interceptor rebuilt ClientCallDetails from scratch on each
attempt, so stale auth headers could never persist across retries. The
ConnectRPC interceptor mutates a shared RequestContext via update(),
which only adds/overwrites keys but never removes old ones. When the
auth header key changes after credential refresh (e.g. "authorization"
→ "flyte-authorization"), both headers coexist on the retry. The
backend's connect headerInterceptor maps both into the "authorization"
gRPC metadata key, and if the expired token appears first, auth fails.

Fix: track injected auth headers and remove them before reinjecting
on retry, restoring the gRPC-era "fresh metadata per attempt" property.

feat: export Documentation from flyte (#1574)

## What

Exports `Documentation` from `flyte` and adds it to `__all__`.

`@env.task(docs=...)` (`TaskEnvironment.task`) and `TaskTemplate.docs`
are typed `Optional[Documentation]`, but the class lives in the private
module `flyte._doc` and has never been exported. Users can only reach it
with `from flyte._doc import Documentation`, which goes against
CONTRIBUTING's rule that users should never need to import an underscore
module. The Union docs had written `from flyte import Documentation`,
which fails with `ImportError` on 2.7.2.

## Changes

- `src/flyte/__init__.py`: `from ._doc import Documentation`, and
`"Documentation"` in `__all__`, in the existing order.
- `tests/flyte/test_doc.py`: the export is the same class as
`flyte._doc.Documentation` and is listed in `__all__`. Also tests
`extract_docstring`.

## Checks

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: pass.
- `pytest tests/flyte/test_doc.py`: 2 passed.
- `make check-import-profile` fails, **but it fails identically on
unmodified `main` (1e949304)**: the only difference is `flyte._observe`,
so the recorded baseline in `import_profiles/` looks stale. This change
adds no module to the import set, because `flyte._doc` is already
imported through `flyte._task`. I haven't regenerated the baseline here,
since that's unrelated to this PR.

## Worth knowing: `docs` does not reach the deployed description

While checking this, I found that `docs=` has no effect on the
description a deployed task shows in the UI:

- `_deploy._get_documentation_entity` builds the `DocumentationEntity`
from `task_template.interface.docstring` only.
- The one place that reads `task.docs` is the CLI: `cli/_run.py:604`
uses it as the `flyte run ... --help` text.

Reproduced on flyte 2.7.2:

| Task | `_get_documentation_entity(task).short_description` |
|---|---|
| docstring only | the docstring |
| `docs=Documentation("Explicit…")` + docstring | the docstring (`docs`
ignored) |
| `docs=Documentation("Explicit…")`, no docstring | `''` |

The parameter's own docstring ("The documentation for the task, if not
provided the function docstring will be used") implies `docs` should
take precedence. If that's the intent, `_get_documentation_entity` could
prefer `task_template.docs.description` when it's set. I've left
behaviour unchanged here, so this PR stays a pure export. Happy to
follow up if you want it wired through.

fix: give `flyte deploy` a CLI config when the context has none (FLYTE-SDK-8N) (#1589)

## Problem

[FLYTE-SDK-8N](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/?query=FLYTE-SDK-8N) —
firing at release **2.8.0**, the current release:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'output_format'
  flyte/cli/_deploy.py:242 in invoke
```

`DeployEnvRecursiveCommand.invoke` reads `ctx.obj` into a local
**before** calling `common.initialize_config(ctx=ctx, ...)`, and then
throws that call's return value away:

```python
obj: CLIConfig = ctx.obj          # None when nothing put a config on the context
common.initialize_config(         # <- builds one, returns it, return value discarded
    ctx=ctx, project=..., domain=..., ...
)
...
common.format("Loaded Environments", ..., obj.output_format)   # boom
```

`initialize_config` already handles this exact state — it has an `if obj
is None:` branch that builds a `CLIConfig` and hands it back. The repair
it performs simply never reached the caller.

`DeployEnvCommand.invoke` has the same root cause one step earlier. It
calls `ctx.obj.init(...)` directly, with no `initialize_config` call at
all, so the same context state gives:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'init'
```

**A context arriving without a config is expected, not hypothetical.**
Two independent compensations for it already exist in the codebase —
`initialize_config`'s own `is None` branch, and
`_hello.py:_ensure_cli_config`, whose docstring states the case
outright:

> Give the context a CLIConfig when `run`/`serve` was invoked without
going through main.

`_deploy.py` was the caller of that shape benefiting from neither.

## Fix

- `DeployEnvRecursiveCommand.invoke` takes the config
`initialize_config` returns instead of the pre-call `ctx.obj`.
- `DeployEnvCommand.invoke` routes through `initialize_config`. The five
arguments it passed to `ctx.obj.init(...)` are exactly the five
`initialize_config` forwards to `CLIConfig.init`, so this is
behaviour-preserving when a config is present, and a repair when it is
not.
- `initialize_config` now also stores the config it builds on the
context rather than only returning it. The remaining callers invoke it
purely for its side effect (`list_commands`/`get_command` in `_deploy`,
`_serve` and `_run`); this leaves the context in a state where a later
`ctx.obj` read succeeds instead of silently building and discarding a
config.

## Verification

Both crash sites reproduce on `main` with the exact Sentry exception,
and pass after the change. 3 of the 4 new tests fail without the
production diff (the fourth is a guard that a context which *already*
carries a config keeps that exact object, and passes either way).

`tests/cli/` + `tests/flyte/cli/`: **537 passed**, no regressions. `make
fmt`, `make mypy`, `make ty` and `make check-docstrings` all clean.

artifacts: parent lineage, duck-typed declaration protocol, content-hash versions (#1527)

Core plumbing so plugin-provided offloaded assets (Union Volumes first)
can publish as artifacts, and so any artifact can carry git-style parent
lineage. Pairs with unionai/flyteplugins-union (volume wiring) and rides
flyteidl2 2.0.48's `repeated parent_artifacts` (flyteorg/flyte#7972).

## What changed

- **`Metadata.parents`** — ordered parent edges (`ArtifactParent` or a
bare version string = same-name parent), serialized onto
`ProducedArtifact.parent_artifacts` (declarative path) via
`to_produced_artifact`. A bare entry stays keyless on the wire so the
service inherits the child's name/scope; `ArtifactParent` carries a key
only when overriding.
- **`Metadata.version_from_content`** — opt-in: an empty version
resolves to the literal's content hash (`Literal.hash`) at
conversion/create time, so republishing identical content is idempotent.
Opt-in on purpose: File/Dir defaults are unchanged.
- **Duck-typed declaration protocol** — output conversion now recognizes
any top-level output exposing `get_flyte_metadata() -> Metadata | None`,
not just `ArtifactWrapper`. A new `current_output_declares_artifact()`
contextvar (set only for the output actually being declared, never for
nested values) lets the value's transformer stamp registry knowledge
into the serialized value.
- **`Artifact.create(parents=...)`** — imperative path parity: fills
`ArtifactSpec.parent_artifacts`; duck metadata seeds
name/version/description/attrs/card/parents exactly like the wrapper
does; `ensure_artifactable` accepts protocol-carrying values.
- **flyteidl2 pinned to 2.0.48** (incl. `rs_controller` pyproject/Cargo
pins + lock checksums).

## Usage

**Declare an artifact on a returned value.** `artifacts.new` wraps an
offloaded asset (`File`, `Dir`, `DataFrame`) zero-copy; it still behaves
exactly like the underlying object.

```python
import flyte.artifacts as artifacts
from flyte.io import File

@env.task
async def train() -> File:
    f = await File.from_local("model.pt")
    return artifacts.new(f, artifacts.Metadata(name="model"))
```

**Content-hash versions** — republishing unchanged content is
idempotent, and an explicit `version` still wins:

```python
artifacts.new(f, artifacts.Metadata(name="model", version_from_content=True))
```

**Multi-parent lineage.** A bare string is shorthand for a same-name
parent (an earlier version of this artifact); `ArtifactParent` carries
`name`/`project`/`domain`/`org` when the parent lives elsewhere. Order
is preserved, so a merge records which side came first:

```python
artifacts.new(
    merged,
    artifacts.Metadata(
        name="dataset",
        parents=("v3", artifacts.ArtifactParent(version="v7", name="dataset-b")),
    ),
)
```

Parents are stored as given and never resolved — a parent that was never
published is legal, like a git remote missing commits nobody pushed.
Only a direct self-reference is rejected.

**Duck-typed declaration.** Any value exposing `get_flyte_metadata() ->
Metadata` participates without importing the wrapper, which is how
`flyteplugins-union` volumes publish themselves
(unionai/flyteplugins-union#106):

```python
class WarmVenv:
    def get_flyte_metadata(self) -> artifacts.Metadata:
        return artifacts.Metadata(name="warm-venv", version_from_content=True)

@env.task
async def prepare() -> WarmVenv:   # declared on the Outputs envelope; no RPC from the task
    ...
```

**Imperative parity** for code that registers directly:

```python
await Artifact.create(name="dataset", version="v8", parents=("v7",))
```

## Testing

- `tests/flyte/test_produces_artifacts.py`: parent serialization shapes,
ordered multi-parents, duck-typed declaration + contextvar behavior,
content-hash version precedence (explicit > hash > empty).
- `tests/flyte/remote/test_artifact.py`: `create(parents=...)` wire
shapes, duck seeding, hash-defaulted versions.
- Full artifact/convert suites green locally (205 passed).

feat(cli): flyte proxy app keeps a Union LLM gateway key sent as the bearer

`flyte proxy app` drops the client's `Authorization` header and injects the
Union bearer the app's auth edge needs. That silently discards a Union LLM
gateway virtual key sent the OpenAI way (`Authorization: Bearer sk-un-...`),
so every OpenAI-compatible client got 401 "virtual key is required" through
the proxy and had to send the key in the gateway's `x-bf-vk` header instead.

A client bearer that is a gateway virtual key (`sk-un-` prefix) now moves to
`x-bf-vk`; the Union bearer is injected as before. An explicit `x-bf-vk` wins,
and any other client `Authorization` is still dropped.

feat: Add retry logic to file upload function (#415)

This pull request introduces a robust retry mechanism for file uploads
in the `src/flyte/remote/_data.py` module. The main improvement is the
addition of an exponential backoff strategy for handling transient
network and server errors during file uploads, replacing the previous
single-attempt upload logic. This enhances reliability, especially in
unstable network conditions.

**Resilience improvements for file uploads:**

* Added a new `_upload_with_retry` async function that uploads files
using exponential backoff and retries on transient network errors and
retryable HTTP status codes (408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504). This
function logs retries and raises a `RuntimeSystemError` if all attempts
fail.
* Introduced a custom `_RetryableUploadError` exception and a helper
function `_is_retryable_status_code` to distinguish between retryable
and non-retryable HTTP errors.

**Integration with file upload flow:**

* Updated the `_upload_single_file` function to use `_upload_with_retry`
instead of directly uploading the file in a single attempt, ensuring all
uploads benefit from the new retry logic.
* Refactored header preparation and removed redundant file open/close
logic in `_upload_single_file`, delegating the upload responsibility to
the new retry-enabled function.

Replace _is_flyte_default with _is_cloned on Image (#957)

## Summary

Replace the `_is_flyte_default` flag on `Image` with `_is_cloned`
(inverted semantics): the SDK only builds an image when the user has
modified it via `clone()` or a `with_*` method. Unmodified default
images short-circuit the existence check and their URI is taken directly
from their `base_image`.

### Core changes in `src/flyte/_image.py`
- **Field rename with flipped default.** `_is_flyte_default: bool =
False` → `_is_cloned: bool = False`. A fresh image is treated as
"already exists in a registry" until something mutates it.
- **Early return for released default images.** `_get_default_image_for`
now returns a bare-URI image
(`base_image=ghcr.io/flyteorg/flyte:<preset_tag>`,
`registry=_get_base_registry()`, `name=_DEFAULT_IMAGE_NAME`,
`extendable=True`) for released (non-dev) Flyte versions, instead of
rebuilding the layer stack. The `packaging.version.Version` import and
the devrelease/prerelease gating are gone.
- **`uri` property rewritten.** Non-cloned images return their
`base_image` directly. Cloned images compose `{registry}/{name}:{tag}`
(with `name` now required). No more fall-throughs for partially-defined
images.
- **`clone()` and `from_dockerfile` mark the produced image as cloned.**
Every `with_*` helper flows through `clone()`, so any user-facing
mutation automatically flips `_is_cloned=True`.
- **`resolve_code_bundle_layer` preserves `_is_cloned`** in both the
strip and resolve-to-CopyConfig reconstruction paths, so hash stability
holds for default (non-cloned) images.

### Builder / tooling
- `src/flyte/_internal/imagebuild/image_builder.py`: `image_exists`
short-circuits on `not image._is_cloned` instead of `_is_flyte_default`.
- `maint_tools/build_default_image.py`: dropped the redundant
`object.__setattr__(default_image, "_is_flyte_default", False)`
override. `from_debian_base(registry=..., name=...)` now naturally goes
through `clone()`, which flips `_is_cloned=True`, so the build proceeds
without help.

### Tests
- `tests/flyte/test_image.py`: 8 new tests covering released default,
dev default, `with_pip_packages`, explicit `clone()`, `from_base`,
`from_ref_name`, `from_debian_base` with a registry override, and
`from_base` + layers.
- `tests/flyte/test_image_builder.py`: 3 new tests confirming
`ImageBuildEngine.image_exists` short-circuits (no backend calls) for
unmodified default / `from_base` images, and that it *does* query the
backend once a layer is added.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/flyte/test_image.py
tests/flyte/test_image_builder.py` — all passing (pre-existing
`test_default_base_image` failure is unrelated)
- [ ] Released SDK pointed at a demo cluster: default
`from_debian_base()` is not rebuilt; `with_pip_packages(...)` triggers a
build
- [ ] `from_base("ghcr.io/...")` does not attempt a build unless
modified

fix: surface missing src path as ImageBuildError in copy_files_to_context (#1075)

## Summary
- `copy_files_to_context` is called for every image layer that needs a
file or directory inside the Docker build context (requirements files,
pyproject/uv.lock, source folders, etc.). It used to delegate the
existence check to `shutil.copy` / `shutil.copy2` and let
`FileNotFoundError` bubble all the way up. When the user pointed a layer
at a path that didn't exist, the raw traceback ended up in Sentry as an
unhandled SDK crash even though it's purely a configuration mistake on
the user side.

Two changes:
1. Guard the entrypoint with `src.exists()` and raise `ImageBuildError`
with an actionable message naming the missing path and the most likely
culprits (`with_requirements`, `with_source_folder`, `with_pyproject`).
`ImageBuildError` is already filtered from Sentry via `_is_user_error`
(#1052), so we stop logging this as an SDK crash.
2. Inside the directory branch, defensively catch `FileNotFoundError`
from `shutil.copy2` so that a file that disappears between enumeration
(`pm.walk`) and the copy (e.g. a transient venv entry, a broken symlink,
or a file removed mid-build) only generates a warning rather than
aborting the entire image build.

## Sentry issues
Fixes [FLYTE-SDK-2X](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/7481752765/)
(`FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'/Users/.../flyte-sdk/.venv/lib/python3.13/dist'` from `shutil.copyfile`
inside `copy_files_to_context`)

`test_copy_files_to_context_missing_src_raises_image_build_error` covers
the missing-src branch
- [x] New regression test
`test_copy_files_to_context_skips_files_that_vanish_mid_walk` covers the
vanish-mid-walk branch

Fallback to constant start time and add lock around submit_sync (#1130)

Child actions weren't deduping across parent retries — a `retries=2`
parent with 3 children spawned 9 child actions instead of 3.

Cause: the sub-action ID hash includes the task spec, which bakes in
`run_start_time`. When the backend doesn't substitute
`{{.runStartTime}}`, we fell back to `datetime.now()`, so each retry
attempt of the parent hashed to a different child name.

Fix: fall back to a constant epoch (1970) instead of `now()`, so the
hash is stable across attempts.

feat: add disable_keyring config option to skip token caching (#971)

## Summary
- Adds `admin.disableKeyring` YAML config option (and corresponding
`FLYTE_ADMIN_DISABLEKEYRING` env var) to disable system keyring use for
auth tokens
- Plumbs the flag through `PlatformConfig` → `init_from_config` → `init`
→ `_initialize_client` → `ClientSet` → `Authenticator` →
`KeyringStore.retrieve/store/delete`
- When disabled, `KeyringStore` skips all store/retrieve/delete
operations so tokens are never persisted to the system keyring

## Why
Useful for environments where the system keyring is unavailable
(headless/CI), misconfigured, or undesirable for security reasons. Users
can now opt out of token caching via config or env var without having to
rely on side-channel hacks.

## Usage
YAML config:
```yaml
admin:
  endpoint: dns:///your-endpoint
  authType: Pkce
  disableKeyring: true
```

Env var:
```
export FLYTE_ADMIN_DISABLEKEYRING=true
```

## Test plan
- [x] Added unit tests in `tests/flyte/keyring/test_keyring_store.py`
covering `store`/`retrieve`/`delete` with `disable=True` and
`disable=False`
- [x] Existing keyring tests still pass
- [ ] Manually verify with a real endpoint that no tokens are written to
the keyring when `disableKeyring: true` is set

docs(hitl): add deprecation notice pointing to flyte-native conditions (#1307)

## Summary

Adds a deprecation warning banner to `plugins/hitl/README.md`: the
`flyteplugins-hitl` event API is superseded by flyte-native conditions
(`flyte.new_condition`), which are built into the SDK and require no
extra dependency, no `depends_on=[hitl.env]` app infrastructure, and no
web-form serving.

The banner includes:
- A one-to-one migration snippet (`hitl.new_event` →
`flyte.new_condition`). The plugin's `scope="run"` argument has no
`new_condition` equivalent since conditions are inherently run-scoped,
so it's simply dropped.
- The three ways to signal a condition: the Flyte UI, the CLI (`flyte
signal condition <run> <action> <value>`), and
`flyte.remote.Condition.signal`.
- A pointer to `examples/advanced/conditions.py` for markdown prompts,
timeouts, webhook notifications, and programmatic signaling.

Follow-up to #1306, which migrated the `flyte.ai.agents` HITL approval
flow off this plugin.

## Test plan

- [x] Docs-only change; verified the `> [!WARNING]` admonition renders
as GitHub-flavored markdown.

Announcements

Security

  • CVE-2026-25645 requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths now extracts contents to a non-deterministic location to prevent malicious file replacement. This does not affect default usage of Requests, only applications calling the utility function directly.

Bugfixes

feat(auth): FLYTE_USE_FILE_KEYRING opt-out of macOS keychain prompts

macOS keychain ACLs are tied to the exact interpreter binary. Two
consequences for flyte auth:

- python-keyring's macOS backend implements set_password as delete +
  SecItemAdd, so every token refresh recreates the keychain item with a
  fresh ACL — "Always Allow" never sticks.
- uv / python-build-standalone interpreters are ad-hoc signed with no
  code-signing identity, so every new venv is a "different app" to the
  keychain and re-prompts for the login password even though the token
  is already cached.

escape hatch: FLYTE_USE_FILE_KEYRING=1 raises the priority of the
existing SimplePlainTextKeyring backend (already used in notebooks)
above the macOS backend, storing tokens in ~/.flyte/keyring.cfg (0600)
with no prompts. Default behavior is unchanged.

fix: resume checkpoints across JobSet whole-set restarts in clustered tasks (#1499)

## Problem
  
In `ClusteredTaskEnvironment` tasks, checkpoint saving works but a
JobSet whole-set restart never loads
the checkpoint saved by the previous attempt — `ctx.checkpoint.load()`
returns None and training
  silently restarts from step 0, losing all progress.

  ## Root cause
  
The backend templates `--checkpoint-path` / `--prev-checkpoint` into the
container args once, per Flyte
attempt (`prevCheckpointPrefix` is only populated from Flyte attempt ≥
2, pointing at the previous
Flyte attempt). JobSet whole-set restarts happen entirely at the K8s
layer: the JobSet controller
recreates pods from the same pod template, so the backend never gets a
chance to re-template
`--prev-checkpoint`. Every restart attempt within a Flyte attempt
therefore ships with
  `--prev-checkpoint '""'` while sharing one `--checkpoint-path`
  `(.../<action>/<attempt>/_flytecheckpoints)`.

Verified on a live reproduction
`(examples/clustered/failure_cascade.py)`: the restarted pod's args
carried the empty prev path while the checkpoint blob from the previous
attempt sat at the exact
`--checkpoint-path` URI the pod was given — the SDK just never looked
there.

This can only be fixed in the SDK: the sole signal that a pod is a
restarted set is the
`JOBSET_RESTART_ATTEMPT` env var (downward-API projection of the
`jobset.sigs.k8s.io/restart-attempt` annotation), which exists only
inside the pod at runtime.

  ## Fix

In `TaskContext.checkpoint` (`src/flyte/models.py`): when
`restart_attempt > 0`, use the task's own
`checkpoint_path` as the load source — the previous restart attempt
saved there. Otherwise keep the
  backend-templated prev path exactly as before.

- Scoped strictly to jobsets: `JOBSET_RESTART_ATTEMPT` is only ever set
on jobset pods, so regular
tasks hit the identical code path as today.
`flyte._checkpoint.Checkpoint` is untouched.
- `restart == 0` keeps prev, preserving cross-Flyte-attempt resume
(backend templates that correctly).
- A set that restarts before its first save finds nothing at its own
path; `Checkpoint.load()` already
treats a missing object as "no checkpoint" and returns None gracefully.

  ## Testing
  
- Unit (`tests/flyte/test_checkpoint.py`, +3 tests): restarted set loads
from its own path (including
the literal `'""'` prev the backend templates); restart before first
save returns None; env unset / 0
    keeps prev — regular-task behavior pinned unchanged.
- E2E before: `failure_cascade.py` on a local devbox (JobSet controller
v0.8.1) — attempt 1 logged
`restart_attempt=1`, no resume, reran all 40 steps; checkpoint blob
confirmed present in the object
    store.
- E2E after: same example on local devbox and`demo.hosted.unionai.cloud`
(run `uvmmvthbbdnmh4gmklw2`, SUCCEEDED) — attempt 1 logged resumed from
checkpoint at step 25 and completed only the remaining steps.

fix(auth): harden security-CLI keyring per security review

- Replace 'security -i' with plain argv: the interactive mode is a
  command interpreter that executes embedded newlines as further
  commands and truncates input at 4096 bytes, which could corrupt or
  disclose long tokens. execve passes the secret verbatim with no
  parsing and no length limit. argv is briefly visible to same-user
  ps, which adds no exposure given the item's ACL already trusts
  /usr/bin/security for any same-user process.
- Remove the global keyring.backends entry point: entry points are
  process-global, so installing flyte would have changed credential
  storage for unrelated packages. KeyringStore now instantiates
  SecurityCliKeyring directly on Darwin only.
- get_password returns None only for errSecItemNotFound (44); locked
  keychain / denied access now raise KeyringError instead of
  masquerading as 'no password stored'.
- set_password recreates the item (delete + add) instead of -U: an
  in-place update preserves the old ACL, so legacy interpreter-owned
  items would have kept prompting.
- Typed keyring exceptions, subprocess timeouts, corrected
  login-keychain wording, documented the same-user ACL tradeoff.

feat: add with_code_bundle to Image (#741)

```python
from dep import foo

import flyte

env = flyte.TaskEnvironment(
    name="full_build",
    # with_code_bundle() automatically copies source code from root_dir into the image
    # when copy_style="none" is set in with_runcontext() or flyte deploy. When copy_style
    # is "loaded_modules" or "all", it's a no-op since the code is bundled separately.
    image=flyte.Image.from_debian_base().with_code_bundle(),
)


@env.task
def square(x) -> int:
    return x ** foo()


@env.task
def main(n: int) -> list[int]:
    return list(flyte.map(square, range(n)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    flyte.init_from_config()
    run = flyte.with_runcontext(copy_style="none", version="x").run(main, n=10)
    print(run.url)
```

- Add `Image.with_code_bundle()` method that configures automatic source
code baking into Docker images when `copy_style="none"` is set in
`with_runcontext()` or `flyte deploy`
- When `copy_style` is `"loaded_modules"` or `"all"`, the layer is a
no-op since code is bundled separately
- Supports two copy styles: `"loaded_modules"` (only imported Python
modules) and `"all"` (entire root_dir)
- Adds `resolve_code_bundle_layer()` integration in `_run_remote()`,
`_run_hybrid()`, and `deploy.apply()` before image builds
- Includes safety-net `RuntimeError` in `docker_builder` if a

Sessions: child actions that are ready when they publish an address

flyte._session (private, like flyte._condition) starts a child action of the
running task and waits for the ActionAddress its worker publishes while it
runs (ActionUpdate.address, flyteorg/flyte#8201). The sandbox plugin uses it
to start interactive sandbox sessions over the task's own watch.

- Controller protocol: register_action / wait_for_registered_action /
  abort_registered_action, for conditions and sessions; register_condition
  and wait_for_condition are unchanged.
- Both remote controllers keep the latest address on each cached action and
  fire a ready event on the first one, or on terminal; the action stays
  cached while the session runs.
- Sessions never retry (user retries are cleared) and get a name unique per
  session, so a retried parent never reattaches to an old session.
- The Python informer only warns about a missing output URI on terminal
  updates, now that the server sends non-terminal ones.

fix: preserve image build run link on image cache hits (#1481)

## Motivation

When an image already exists in the registry, no build runs, so
TaskMetadata.image_build_run was never stamped and the console lost its
link from a task's image to the build that produced it. The image
service now reports the originating build run on a GetImage hit, so the
SDK can stamp it without a build.

 ## Summary

- Add ImageBuild.build_run, carrying the run that originally produced an
image when no build was launched in this process.
- RemoteImageChecker.image_exists records Image.build_run from the
GetImage response into a process-local side channel (_image_build_runs),
which ImageBuildEngine.build attaches to cache-hit results. Needed
because the public ImageChecker protocol (flyte.extend) returns only a
URI.
- _build_image_bg falls back to build_run when remote_run is absent; a
build launched in-process still takes precedence.
- _build_images now propagates build_run_ids from seed_cache, so nested
runs don't drop the link.

##  Test Plan

  - uv run pytest tests/flyte/imagebuild/ tests/flyte/test_deploy.py
- New tests/flyte/imagebuild/test_remote_image_checker.py covers: build
run recorded on hit, unset build_run, partial identifier rejected, bare
{id, fqin} response, and recording failures swallowed. The three tests
needing the new field skip on flyteidl2==2.0.42.

opentelemetry tracing and grafana agent observability for agents (#1355) Adds distributed tracing to Flyte plus a bridge that sends agent generations to Grafana Agent Observability. Two new plugins and one small hook in core. ## The problem A durable run is not one process. It crashes, resumes, retries and each attempt starts a fresh OpenTelemetry SDK that knows nothing of the earlier ones. Point a normal OTel setup at a durable agent and two things go wrong: every attempt mints its own trace id, so one agent run arrives as several unrelated traces; and every step the resumed run replayed out of its durable log is missing entirely because replayed steps never execute and nothing instruments them. The trace ends up with holes exactly where durability did its job. ## What is here `flyte._observe` (core): a dependency-free hook exposing two moments: a task starting and a `flyte.trace` step running. Context-manager based so an observer's span is active while user code runs and any instrumentation library's spans nest inside it. Core never imports an observability SDK. Called from `_trace.py` (all four wrappers) and `taskrunner.run_task`; when nothing is registered the path is a dict lookup and no allocation. `flyteplugins-otel`: turns those callbacks into spans. Ordinary distributed tracing for ordinary tasks plus two durability-specific behaviours. When no trace context arrives from outside, the trace id is derived from the run identity, so every process computes the same value and a crashed-and-resumed run is one trace with no coordination. Steps served from the durable log are recorded as spans marked `flyte.replayed` so a resumed trace has no holes. `flyteplugins-agento11y`: sends generations, tool calls, token usage and cost to Grafana, nested inside the Flyte task span and grouped by Flyte run. Binds Flyte identity onto agento11y's own context: run name to conversation id, task name to agent name, task version to agent version. Both bindings are switchable since a task driving several agents should keep each framework's own names. `flyteplugins-agents-core`: two registries so an out-of-tree package can instrument frameworks the adapters drive. Agent instrumentation libraries attach at the call site and the adapter owns that call, so a user going through `run_agent` has nowhere to put a handler. Adapters offer their framework-native payload on the way past and separately can have their call substituted. Both know nothing about any vendor. Six adapters wired: langchain, langgraph, openai, claude, google, pydantic_ai. Grafana links for the Flyte UI. `GrafanaTrace` queries on `flyte.run_name` rather than addressing a trace by id so it works whatever the trace ids turn out to be. `GrafanaAgentObservability` opens the run's conversation. 1. ## What

Exports `Documentation` from `flyte` and adds it to `__all__`.

`@env.task(docs=...)` (`TaskEnvironment.task`) and `TaskTemplate.docs`
are typed `Optional[Documentation]`, but the class lives in the private
module `flyte._doc` and has never been exported. Users can only reach it
with `from flyte._doc import Documentation`, which goes against
CONTRIBUTING's rule that users should never need to import an underscore
module. The Union docs had written `from flyte import Documentation`,
which fails with `ImportError` on 2.7.2.

## Changes

- `src/flyte/__init__.py`: `from ._doc import Documentation`, and
`"Documentation"` in `__all__`, in the existing order.
- `tests/flyte/test_doc.py`: the export is the same class as
`flyte._doc.Documentation` and is listed in `__all__`. Also tests
`extract_docstring`.

## Checks

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: pass.
- `pytest tests/flyte/test_doc.py`: 2 passed.
- `make check-import-profile` fails, **but it fails identically on
unmodified `main` (1e949304)**: the only difference is `flyte._observe`,
so the recorded baseline in `import_profiles/` looks stale. This change
adds no module to the import set, because `flyte._doc` is already
imported through `flyte._task`. I haven't regenerated the baseline here,
since that's unrelated to this PR.

## Worth knowing: `docs` does not reach the deployed description

While checking this, I found that `docs=` has no effect on the
description a deployed task shows in the UI:

- `_deploy._get_documentation_entity` builds the `DocumentationEntity`
from `task_template.interface.docstring` only.
- The one place that reads `task.docs` is the CLI: `cli/_run.py:604`
uses it as the `flyte run ... --help` text.

Reproduced on flyte 2.7.2:

| Task | `_get_documentation_entity(task).short_description` |
|---|---|
| docstring only | the docstring |
| `docs=Documentation("Explicit…")` + docstring | the docstring (`docs`
ignored) |
| `docs=Documentation("Explicit…")`, no docstring | `''` |

The parameter's own docstring ("The documentation for the task, if not
provided the function docstring will be used") implies `docs` should
take precedence. If that's the intent, `_get_documentation_entity` could
prefer `task_template.docs.description` when it's set. I've left
behaviour unchanged here, so this PR stays a pure export. Happy to
follow up if you want it wired through.

feat(init): env-var control of the in-cluster auth mode

`init_in_cluster` resolved credentials from an explicit api_key, then a mounted
config file (UCTL_CONFIG / FLYTECTL_CONFIG), then the injected _UNION_EAGER_API_KEY
/ EAGER_API_KEY. A deployment that mints its own scoped tokens could only opt out
of the injected key by mounting a config file; there was no env-var-only route,
even though every credentials config entry already has an env var.

Read the auth entries from the environment and thread them through. A pod can now
carry:

    FLYTE_ADMIN_AUTHTYPE=ExternalCommand
    FLYTE_ADMIN_COMMAND="/usr/local/bin/mint-token --audience flyte"

and authenticate by running that command, with no api key issued to it at all.
Setting an auth type disables the injected-key fallback outright rather than
layering on top of it, so a cluster still injecting a key during migration cannot
have the two silently disagree. The endpoint keeps coming from the injected
_U_EP_OVERRIDE and also accepts FLYTE_ADMIN_ENDPOINT, since dropping the api key
drops the endpoint it used to decode to. FLYTE_ADMIN_PROXYCOMMAND is picked up
independently of the auth type.

An explicit api_key argument still wins, and says so in the log rather than
quietly ignoring the env vars. ExternalCommand with no command raises at init
instead of deferring to an AuthenticationError on the first RPC that names neither
env var.

The entries are read with `ConfigEntry.read()` and no config file, which consults
only the environment - this keeps the pod off `resolve_config_path`, whose
`git rev-parse` subprocess is wasted work in a task pod.

Known gap: the opt-in Rust controller (_F_USE_RUST_CONTROLLER=1) reads the injected
api key directly and does not honor these vars.

fix: validate a `cpu` request/limit pair the way a `memory` pair is validated (#1590)

## Problem

`Resources.cpu` is exempt from `_check_quantity_string` (added in #1581)
because, unlike `memory`, `disk` and `shm`, it legitimately accepts an
int or float core count as well as a Kubernetes quantity string —
`_get_cpu_resource_entry` calls `str()` on whatever it is handed. That
exemption left the field with two gaps.

**1. No type check at all.**

```python
Resources(cpu=[1])        # accepted -> CPU quantity '[1]'
Resources(cpu=(None, 2))  # accepted -> CPU quantity 'None'
```

Both reach the backend as those literal strings rather than being
rejected here, where the field name is still known.

**2. A sign check that only ever saw the bare spelling.**

```python
Resources(cpu=-1)       # ValueError: cpu must be greater than or equal to 0
Resources(cpu=(-1, 2))  # accepted -> serializes a request for -1 cores
```

The check is written as `if isinstance(self.cpu, (int, float))`, which a
tuple never satisfies.

**The sibling field in the same method proves the intent.** `memory`
validates *both* halves of its pair — `_check_quantity_string` recurses
when `allow_pair` is set — so before this change the same bad value was
treated one way as `memory=(...)` and the opposite way as `cpu=(...)`.

## A third instance, in the `memory` half

Checking that sibling turned up the same shape once more: `None` was
accepted as one half of a pair, not just as the field itself.

```python
Resources(memory=(None, "2Gi"))   # accepted -> serializes a request for ''
```

Protobuf takes `None` as the empty string, so this silently requested an
empty memory quantity rather than leaving the request unset. `None` now
means "unset" for the field only, for both fields.

## Fix

- New `_check_cpu_quantity`, a sibling of `_check_quantity_string` that
admits the core-count types `cpu` is declared to take, applied to the
bare and pair spellings alike.
- The negative-value check moves into it, so it sees both spellings. Its
message is unchanged, so existing callers and tests read the same.
- Both helpers take `allow_none`, set only for the field itself.

**Reject rather than coerce**, for the reason already recorded for
`memory`: `str()` of the wrong thing is usually a *valid* Kubernetes
quantity meaning something the user did not intend, so coercing would
quietly deploy the wrong resources.

## Verification

12 of the new parametrized cases fail on unpatched `src/` and pass with
the fix. The remainder are guards that every documented `cpu` spelling
(`1`, `0`, `0.5`, `"100m"`, `(1, 2)`, `("1", "2")`, `None`) and every
"unset" spelling still work — they pass either way, which is the point.

`tests/user_api/test_resources.py`: **137 passed**.
Resource/serde/deploy/pod/task sweep: **934 passed**, with one failure
(`test_files.py::test_task_write_file_local_then_upload`) confirmed
failing identically on clean `origin/main` and unrelated to this change.
`make fmt`, `make mypy`, `make ty` and `make check-docstrings` all
clean.

## Note

No Sentry trailer — this is a code-audit PR in the same family as #1560,
#1581 and #1582. The `cpu=(-1, 2)` and `memory=(None, …)` shapes do not
crash, so they cannot produce a Sentry issue; they deploy the wrong
resources silently, which is why they were worth finding.

fix(auth): route macOS keychain access through /usr/bin/security

The keychain authorizes clients by code signature. Python interpreters
from uv / python-build-standalone are ad-hoc signed with no identity, so
every venv is a different "app" to the keychain: tokens written by one
interpreter trigger a login-password prompt when read from a new venv,
and "Always Allow" grants never stick (keyring's native macOS backend
also recreates the item on every set_password, wiping the ACL).

Add a keyring backend that shells out to /usr/bin/security instead of
using the Security-framework bindings. The CLI is Apple-signed and
identical for every venv, so items it creates are readable by any venv
with zero prompts, while tokens stay in the encrypted login keychain.

- priority 6 on Darwin (native backend is 5), -1 elsewhere
- secrets passed via 'security -i' stdin, never in process argv
- legacy python-created items still readable through keyring's chainer
  fallback to the native backend, and are rewritten as CLI-owned items
  on the next token refresh

fix(app): resolve _caller_frame to user code in subclasses and factories

AppEnvResolver uses ``AppEnvironment._caller_frame.filename`` to locate the
module that holds the module-level ``app_env`` binding the deployed
``fserve`` container must import. Four subclasses
(``MCPAppEnvironment``, ``FastAPIAppEnvironment``,
``FlyteWebhookAppEnvironment``, ``AgentChatAppEnvironment``) were
overwriting the parent class's correctly-computed ``_caller_frame`` with
a 2-level ``frame.f_back.f_back`` walk that landed on the synthesized
dataclass ``__init__`` whose ``co_filename`` is ``"<string>"``. The
resolver then raised ``RuntimeError``, ``container_cmd`` silently dropped
``--resolver-args`` from the command line, and the deployed container
crashed at boot with ``ValueError: No command provided to execute``.

This change:

* Declares ``_caller_frame`` once on the parent ``AppEnvironment``
  (``field(init=False, default=None, repr=False, compare=False)``).
* Extracts a robust walker ``_find_user_caller_frame()`` that skips every
  frame whose source file lives inside the SDK source tree or has an
  angle-bracketed ``co_filename`` (``<string>``, ``<frozen ...>``), plus
  any ``__post_init__`` / ``__init__`` frames so a user subclass that
  chains ``super().__post_init__()`` still resolves to its caller.
* Deletes the broken 2-level overrides in the four subclasses.

Adds ``tests/flyte/app/test_caller_frame_resolution.py`` covering:

* Direct module-level instantiation lands on the user file.
* Factory helpers (single-level and nested) still land on the user file.
* Synthesized filenames are never reported.
* Every formerly-broken subclass now inherits the correct walker.
* ``container_cmd`` emits ``--resolver-args module:varname`` end-to-end.

All 378 existing ``tests/flyte/app/`` + ``tests/flyte/ai/`` tests pass.

fix: validate the int fields of RetryStrategy and ReusePolicy

`RetryStrategy.count`, `ReusePolicy.concurrency` and the elements of
`ReusePolicy.replicas` are all declared `int` and handed straight to protobuf
uint32 fields at serialization time, but none of them were validated.

A wrong type survived construction and died far from the mistake as
`TypeError: '<x>' object cannot be interpreted as an integer` -- raised in SDK
frames naming neither the field that was wrong nor the task it came from. A
value below the field's valid range was worse: `concurrency=-1`, a negative
`replicas`, and `replicas` min > max were all serialized *silently*, deploying
a pool that can never run a task.

`@env.task(retries="3")` is the sharpest case. `_task.py` only converts
`retries` when `isinstance(retries, int)`, so a string passes through untouched
to `get_proto_retry_strategy`'s `retries.count` -- and that attribute access
succeeds, because `str.count` is a real built-in method. The failure surfaces
one layer further on as `TypeError: 'builtin_function_or_method' object cannot
be interpreted as an integer`, naming nothing the user wrote.

Each is now rejected where the mistake was made, with the field named, matching
how `ReusePolicy` already validates `scope`, `idle_ttl` and `scaledown_ttl`, and
how `Timeout` and `Resources` validate their own fields. `reuse_policy_to_pb`'s
docstring already asserts the invariant this establishes -- that
`__post_init__` leaves its accessors "always well-defined" -- which was true of
`replicas`' shape but not of its elements, and not of `concurrency` at all.

Validate rather than coerce: `retries="3"` is a plausible typo, and silently
reading it as `3` would deploy a task with a retry budget the user never wrote.
Following the same family's precedent, `bool` is deliberately not narrowed.

`replicas=(0, 3)` stays legal -- a scale-to-zero minimum is meaningful.

feat(webhooks): action= kwarg on on_event for user-defined identifiers

Registering one Slack button or slash command meant a raw string --
"block_actions.approve_deploy", "command.deploy" -- because the suffix
is the app's own vocabulary (its action_id, its command name), which no
plugin constant can enumerate. The string form worked but hid the
structure and invited the "command./deploy" never-matches typo.

on_event now takes the user-defined half explicitly:

    @app_env.on_event(events.Interaction.BLOCK_ACTIONS, action="approve_deploy")
    @app_env.on_event(events.Command, action="/deploy")

The kwarg is named `action` because that is the WebhookEvent field it
matches, the name GitHub's payloads use on the wire, and the vocabulary
slack_bolt users know (@app.action / @app.command) -- one generic name
that scales across providers where action_id=/slack_command= would
multiply per-provider kwargs in a core API. A leading "/" is dropped so
slash commands read the way Slack displays them; an EventType class
means its ANY. Raw qualified strings still work unchanged.

Composition happens at registration, so matching, /api/status, and the
dashboard are untouched. Rejects action= on an already-qualified
pattern and on the match-everything empty pattern.

fix: raise ImageBuildError for missing image source folder (#1148)

## Problem

`CopyConfig.validate()` raised a bare `ValueError` when an image's
source path is missing or the wrong type (e.g. a stale `add_source(...)`
path pointing at a build dir that no longer exists). That escaped into
the SDK's Sentry project as an SDK crash, even though a bad source path
is a user mistake in the image spec.

## Fix

In `src/flyte/_image.py:CopyConfig.validate`, raise
`flyte.errors.ImageBuildError` (a `RuntimeUserError` already filtered by
`flyte/_sentry.py:_is_user_error`) for the three validation failures
(missing path, not-a-directory, not-a-file). Messages are unchanged. No
caller catches `ValueError` around this path (verified), and
`ImageBuildError` is still a `RuntimeError` subclass.

## Closes
- [FLYTE-SDK-4D](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/FLYTE-SDK-4D/) —
`ValueError: Source folder /.../deploy/build/release/sandbox-server does
not exist`.

`fixes FLYTE-SDK-4D`

## Tests

fix: wrap docker buildx CalledProcessError as ImageBuildError

`_build_from_dockerfile` ran `subprocess.run(..., check=True)` without any
try/except, so a non-zero `docker buildx build -f Dockerfile` exit
propagated the raw `subprocess.CalledProcessError` straight up to the
caller — and into Sentry as an unhandled SDK crash (FLYTE-SDK-34).

`_build_image` already had a try/except for the same case, but wrapped
the error as a plain `RuntimeError("Failed to build image: ...")`.
`RuntimeError` isn't in `_is_user_error`'s filter set, so even though
docker rejecting the user's Dockerfile is purely user-facing feedback,
each occurrence landed in Sentry as a crash (FLYTE-SDK-2R).

Wrap both call sites as `ImageBuildError`. `ImageBuildError` is already
filtered from Sentry via `_is_user_error` (#1052), so these are now
classified as user-facing image-build feedback. The underlying
`CalledProcessError` is preserved via `raise ... from e` so the chained
cause remains available for diagnostics.

implement intratask checkpointing in the sdk (#885)

This pull request introduces a comprehensive suite of example scripts
demonstrating how to implement checkpointing and failure recovery for
machine learning training workflows using Flyte's `AsyncCheckpoint`
mechanism. The examples cover a range of ML frameworks including
scikit-learn, PyTorch, PyTorch Lightning, and Hugging Face Transformers,
each showing how to persist and restore training state across task
retries. The scripts also illustrate best practices for simulating
failures and integrating checkpointing into iterative training
processes.

The most important changes are:

**Scikit-learn checkpointing:**
* Added `sklearn_partial_checkpoint.py` to demonstrate incremental
training with `SGDClassifier.partial_fit`, using checkpointing to
persist and restore model state and training progress across retries.

**PyTorch checkpointing:**
* Added `pytorch_task_checkpoint.py` to show checkpointing of a simple
PyTorch model's state dict and optimizer at each epoch, with failure
simulation and recovery.

**PyTorch Lightning checkpointing:**
* Added `pytorch_lightning_checkpoint.py` to illustrate checkpointing
for a LightningModule using `ModelCheckpoint` and custom callbacks,
including logic for resuming from the latest checkpoint and injecting
failures.

**Hugging Face Transformers checkpointing:**
* Added `huggingface_trainer_checkpoint.py` to provide an example of
checkpointing with `transformers.Trainer`, integrating Flyte
checkpointing with Hugging Face's checkpointing and recovery system, and
simulating failures at defined intervals.

**Generic byte checkpointing:**
* Added `generic_data_checkpoint.py` as a minimal example of
checkpointing arbitrary byte data, demonstrating the basic checkpoint
load/save/retry pattern.

fix(devbox): make `flyte start devbox` work on Windows

Three host-OS assumptions broke the devbox on Windows:

- `_KUBE_DIR = Path("/tmp/.kube")` renders as the driveless `\tmp\.kube`,
  which docker rejects as a `-v` host path. Use `tempfile.gettempdir()`

  splits a `C:\...` path in half. Use `os.pathsep`.
- The root-owned-kubeconfig retry calls `os.getuid()`, which does not exist
  on Windows, masking the real kubectl error with an `AttributeError`. The
  fallback only applies to Linux bind mounts, so re-raise there.

runners can't run Linux containers, so an end-to-end devbox test needs a
self-hosted machine; this covers the CLI-side host-OS assumptions.

Simplify cross-loop client caching to a threadsafe memo

Replace the loop_agnostic_async_cache decorator (per-instance state, per-loop
in-flight task tracking, WeakKeyDictionary, shielding) with a single small
ThreadSafeCache: a threading.Lock-guarded OrderedDict of resolved values. The
cluster-aware _resolve methods in controlplane.py now do a plain lookup-or-call
against this map, keyed per method and arguments.

The cached clients carry no event-loop state, so one threadsafe mapping serves
every event loop and thread in the process, which is all the original problem
needed — a task-based cache cleared itself and warned on a loop change. Failures
are still never cached (the next call retries), per-instance isolation and LRU
bounding are preserved, and the mapping guards lookups under a short lock while
the async factory runs outside it. Concurrent misses for the same key resolve
independently rather than being serialized, per review feedback.

Making every command output json (In the future yaml too) (#56)

### PR Description

#### Overview

This pull request introduces significant improvements to the Flyte CLI
and SDK around output formatting and JSON serialization. The goal is to
make CLI output more flexible, scriptable, and user-friendly, especially
for automation and integration with other tools.

---

#### Key Changes

**1. Output Format Option for CLI**
- Replaces the boolean --simple flag with a new --output-format (or -of)
option.
- Supports multiple formats: table (default), table-simple, and json.
- All CLI commands that previously used get_table now use the new format
function, allowing consistent output formatting based on user
preference.

**2. Common Formatting Utilities**
- Introduces a new format function in _common.py that handles table,
simple table, and JSON output for iterable objects.
- get_panel is updated to respect output format for consistency.

**3. ToJSONMixin for Models**
- Adds a new ToJSONMixin class (in remote/_common.py) that provides
to_dict and to_json methods.
- All major API model classes (Project, Run, Task, Secret, Action,
ActionDetails, ActionInputs, ActionOutputs, RunDetails, TaskDetails) now
inherit from ToJSONMixin.
- This enables easy and consistent JSON serialization for CLI output and
programmatic use.

**4. Improved List Commands**
- All list commands (e.g., flyte get projects, flyte get runs, flyte get
tasks, etc.) now respect the --output-format option.
- Limits for listing are more consistently handled (e.g., flyte get
run/task now have a --limit option).

**5. Codebase Modernization**
- Refactors all usages of simple argument to output_format.
- Updates type annotations using Literal and typing_extensions.get_args
for CLI option validation.

---

#### Motivation

- Provides a more scriptable CLI experience for users and automation by
supporting JSON output.
- Makes the CLI more flexible for different use cases (human-friendly
tables, simple for scripting, JSON for parsing).
- Unifies output formatting and serialization logic across the codebase
for maintainability and consistency.

---

#### Backward Compatibility

- The --simple flag is removed and replaced by --output-format. The
default remains a rich table, so most users will not notice a change
unless they used --simple (who can now use --output-format
table-simple).
- All API models are backward compatible, now with additional methods
for JSON serialization.

---

#### How to Use

- Human-readable table (default):  
  `flyte get projects`
- Simple table (for copy-pasting):  
  `flyte get projects --output-format table-simple`
- JSON output (for scripting/automation):  
  `flyte get projects --output-format json`

---

#### Example

```sh
flyte get tasks --output-format json --limit 10
```

---

#### Additional Notes

- All new output format logic is centralized, making future extensions

Changelog

Sourced from cryptography's changelog.

50.0.0 - 2026-07-31


* **SECURITY ISSUE**:

:func:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs7.pkcs7_decrypt_der`
and its PEM and S/MIME variants no longer expose distinguishable errors
or
timing when unwrapping a ``RecipientInfo``'s ``encryptedKey``, which
could
act as a Bleichenbacher oracle for callers that decrypt untrusted
messages.
A random key is now substituted on failure, as described in :rfc:`3218`.
  Credit to **@X1AOxiang** for reporting the issue. **CVE-2026-69247**
* Deprecated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over finite fields (FFDH).
  Everything FFDH is deprecated, including the types in
``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh`` and loading FFDH keys
or
  parameters with the key loading APIs. Users should migrate to a more
  modern key exchange algorithm.
* Added ``xof()`` class methods to
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE128` and
:class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE256` for
constructing
  algorithm instances configured for use with
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash`.
* The :mod:`X.509 verification <cryptography.x509.verification>`
APIs are now
  considered stable and are subject to our API stability policy.
* Added the :doc:`/cobblestone` recipe, an implementation of the
  Cobblestone-128 and Cobblestone-256 instantiations of the `C2SP
  chunked-encryption specification
<https://c2sp.org/chunked-encryption>`_ for streaming
authenticated
  encryption of large messages.
* Parsing a Signed Certificate Timestamp list now rejects encodings that
carry trailing bytes after the list or after an individual SCT, instead
of
  silently ignoring them.
* Added support for using :class:`~cryptography.x509.Name` as a field
type in
  the :doc:`/hazmat/asn1/index` module.
* Loading a public key or an EC private key now rejects DER where the
``subjectPublicKey`` (or EC ``publicKey``) ``BIT STRING`` declares a
non-zero
  number of unused bits, instead of silently ignoring it.
* Parsing a CRL entry's ``InvalidityDate`` extension now rejects a
``GeneralizedTime`` that carries fractional seconds or another non-DER
form,
matching the strict encoding already required for every other X.509 time
  field.
* :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_request` and
:func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_response` now reject a
request
or response whose ``version`` field is not ``v1``, the only version
defined
by RFC 6960, matching the version validation already performed when
loading
  certificates, CSRs and CRLs.
* :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash` is now
supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
* HMAC (and therefore PBKDF2-HMAC) with SHA-3 hashes is now supported
when
  building against AWS-LC.
* Diffie-Hellman (:doc:`/hazmat/primitives/asymmetric/dh`) is now
supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
</tr></table>

Changelog
