refactor(config): prefer FLYTE_AUTH_* over the derived FLYTE_ADMIN_* names

`admin.authType` and `admin.command` are auth settings, not "admin" ones. The
"admin" in their env vars is not a chosen name at all — `get_env_name()` derives
it mechanically from the yaml switch, so `admin.authType` becomes
FLYTE_ADMIN_AUTHTYPE. That spelling leaks flyte-1 `flyteadmin` naming into
something a customer now has to type into a pod spec, and `read_from_env`'s own
docstring already flagged the scheme as provisional.

Renaming outright would be worse than the wart. The scheme's one real virtue is
that the env var and the config key are derivable from each other in both
directions; changing two of the eleven `admin.*` entries would leave no rule, just
a lookup table with exceptions. And the derived names are public surface that
predates this feature — they are what the config-file path has always used.

So make the preferred name explicit instead of implicit. `YamlConfigEntry` takes
an `aliases` tuple of hand-written names that are checked before the derived one;
`get_env_name()` reports the preferred name (used in docs and error messages) and
`env_names()` gives the full precedence order. The auth entries declare
FLYTE_AUTH_TYPE, FLYTE_AUTH_COMMAND and FLYTE_AUTH_PROXY_COMMAND; everything that
worked before still works.

When two names for one setting disagree, the higher-precedence one wins and the
conflict is logged rather than silently dropped — that ambiguity is how a
migration goes wrong quietly. Identical values are not reported.

Scoped deliberately to the three auth entries this feature documents.
FLYTE_ADMIN_ENDPOINT keeps its derived name: the endpoint is a platform setting,
not an auth one. Renaming the rest of the `admin.*` family is the scheme-wide
change the code comment anticipates, and wants its own discussion.

one no longer declares -- asserted by a test, so it fails loudly rather than
publishing nothing.

quietly covering:

    `Artifact.create`, so a new-style implementer would not have been

    construction rather than by coincidence.
  * `tests/flyte/prefetch/test_hf_model.py` exercised the wrapper through the

the ones inside your own repo that you meant to update.

fix(docs): six RST literals the style check could not see

check-docstrings scans line by line, and DOUBLE_BACKTICK_RE is `` [^`\n]+ ``.
Docstrings wrap at the line limit, so an inline literal starting near the margin
has its closing delimiter on the next line and is invisible to it. Six were live
and the file reported clean.

One reached readers. flyte.PodTemplate's page rendered

    container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<primary>: unconfined

The ``...`` is not a code span to the API generator, so its angle brackets were
escaped as prose -- and then it formed a code span anyway at render time,
trapping the entities where nothing decodes them. A single-backtick span is
recognised and its angle brackets are left alone: the generated reference
already carries `[mcp_servers.<name>]` and `--from-file <path>` correctly.

So all six become single-backtick spans, and the check gains a pass over the
whole docstring rather than a line at a time, with fenced regions blanked first
so an example containing a wrapped literal is still left alone. Verified both
ways: a reintroduced wrapped literal is caught, and one inside a fence is not.

Three of the six needed their surrounding prose rewrapped rather than simply
unwrapped, to stay inside the line limit.

typed output/input API on ActionDetails/Run (#1247)

Fetching another action's output via ActionDetails.outputs() eagerly
reconstructs the whole interface and fails fast if any one type can't be
guessed; the result is also a synthetic schema-derived look-alike, and
there's no first-class way to ask
for an output as a known type. This adds an API addressing those gaps:

- output_literals() / input_literals(): raw {name: Literal} straight
from the data proxy, with no interface reconstruction.
- typed_outputs(types) / typed_inputs(types): re-hydrate only the
requested slots into caller-supplied types via
literal_map_to_kwargs(python_types=...), which skips guess_python_type.
Sibling types are never touched and the result is the caller's real
class with its validators/methods.
- deserializers={Type: loader}: optional hook handing the raw
pre-validation payload to a caller loader instead of the default decode,
for versioned-schema models that migrate historical payloads before
validating.

The data-proxy fetch is factored into a cached _fetch_action_data()
shared by _cache_data and the new methods. Wrappers are surfaced on
RunDetails (async) and Run (syncified).

Fixes
https://linear.app/unionai/issue/ENG26-759/first-class-typed-output-fetch-without-eager-interface-reconstruction,

fix: bind Artifact overrides when firing a trigger with flyte.run(trigger, ...) (#1543)

## Why

`flyte.run(trigger, model=<flyte.remote.Artifact>)` raises
`TypeTransformerFailedError: Expected value of type File but got
Artifact(...)`. `_run_trigger` converts keyword overrides with
`convert_from_native_to_inputs`, which does no artifact binding, while
`_run_remote` uses `convert_from_native_to_inputs_binding_artifacts`.

Firing an artifact trigger by hand is the main case: no new version is
being published, so the caller has to pass the `flyte.TriggeredArtifact`
input themselves, and the natural thing to pass is the `Artifact`
object. Found by the docsy review on unionai/unionai-docs#1578, which
documents exactly this flow.

## What

- `_run_trigger` now uses the same binding path as `_run_remote`, so an
`Artifact` override lands as its stored literal, coerced to the declared
input type, with its `artifact_id` provenance stamp intact.
- Regression test
`test_run_trigger_artifact_override_binds_stored_literal`. It fails on
`main` with the error above and passes with the fix.

The docs PR states this needs flyte 2.7.2.

fix(extras): upload Volume.fork snapshot eagerly via remote.upload_file

`File.from_local(snapshot_path)` inside a parent task pod takes a path that
the literal-marshaller later skips ("Remote context detected, skipping lazy
uploaders.") — the resulting File then carries the host's local
/tmp/vol-fork-*.db path, which the sub-action pod cannot read. The original
implementation also unlinked the snapshot before that lazy upload would
have had a chance to run, surfacing as
"upload arg must be a single file" at submit time.

Using `flyte.remote.upload_file` directly pushes the snapshot to object
storage and returns the remote URI, which we wrap in a File so the
sub-action receives a URL it can actually fetch. The local snapshot is
unlinked after the upload completes.

Exercised end-to-end via the cloud monorepo's `make buf_flyte` shim:
parent task forks its live JuiceFS volume → sub-action mounts the fork at
/workspace, runs the buf chain, commits the new index → parent mounts the
result, rsyncs the regenerated tree back, and the .proto change propagates
all the way to gen/pb-go / gen/pb_python / clients/ / clientsv2/.

Add control-plane reporting for tracked runs (flyte run --tracked) (#1356)

## Overview

Tracked runs: the SDK keeps orchestrating everything locally while
reporting run state — actions, attempts, inputs/outputs, HTML reports —
to the control plane, so local runs appear live in the console. Builds
on the IDL in flyteorg/flyte#7737 and the `TrackedRunService` rename
(released as flyteidl2 2.0.40, which this PR pins).

### How it works

- **RemoteRunReporter** — a third `RunRecorder` sink alongside the TUI
tracker and SQLite store. The recorder observer contract is synchronous
and fires from async controller code *and* the threads that run sync
tasks, so the sink is a sync enqueue facade over async I/O: `record_*`
calls capture a fully-computed event under a lock (per-attempt monotonic
versions; attempts start at 1 per the server contract) and a dedicated
background event loop batches `TrackedRunService.ReportActions` calls
and performs the signed-URL uploads (the same background-loop shape as
`flyte.syncify`). Terminal events trigger a bounded flush barrier at run
end. Reporting is best-effort and never fails or hangs the run (unless
strict mode is on).
- **Data path routes like everything else**: artifacts upload via
`DataProxyService.CreateUploadLocation` signed PUT URLs with the
`tracked-runs/<run>/<action>[/<attempt>]` filename_root scheme, routed
by `ClusterService.SelectCluster(OPERATION_TRACKED_RUN_DATA)` — an org
with a directly-reachable data plane cluster uploads straight to that
cluster's store; an org without one is served by the control plane's own
store. The reporter stamps the routing cluster onto reported attempt
events so reads later route to the same store. Inputs upload before
CreateRun (deterministic path, no URI on the event); outputs/report URIs
attach to the terminal event after their uploads complete. Reports also
flush live mid-run so the report tab updates while the run executes.
- **Opt-in surface** (one naming family, anchored on the flag):
  - `flyte run --local --tracked [--tracked-strict]`
- config: `local.tracked` / `local.tracked_strict` (section mirrors
`local.persistence`)
- `flyte.init(local_tracked=..., local_tracked_strict=...)`; `flyte
create config --local-tracked`
  - runcontext: `flyte.with_runcontext(mode="local", tracked=True)`
- Requires project/domain; degrades gracefully with one warning when no
client is initialized. `--tracked-strict` fails the run loudly on the
first reporting failure (for debugging reporting itself). SIGINT/SIGTERM
abort-flushes in-flight actions as ABORTED. `Run.url` points at the
console tracked-runs page. Falsy outputs (`0`, `""`, `[]`, `False`)
report correctly (presence, not truthiness). File/Dir raw data never
uploads — only the three metadata artifacts (inputs.pb / outputs.pb /
report.html) reach the dataproxy.

The deck feature (`@env.task(report=True)`, `flyte.report`) and the
`@trace` decorator are unrelated and untouched.

## Test Plan

- 688 unit tests green on the released flyteidl2 pin (reporter lifecycle
incl. retries/ordering/flush barrier/failure isolation/strict mode,
upload helper, client protocol, CLI flags, config plumbing).
- Live E2E against three environments running a backend that implements
`TrackedRunService`:
- a single-process development stack: full lifecycle, watches, replay
idempotency.
- a hosted control plane with a directly-reachable data plane cluster:
runs + inputs/outputs + reports render in the console; artifacts land in
the cluster's metadata store, with the routing cluster recorded on
attempts.
- a hosted control plane where artifacts are served by the control
plane's own store — the fallback leg of the routed data path, verified
end to end on the released flyteidl2 pin.

## Rollout Plan

The feature is opt-in per run/config and requires a control plane that
implements `TrackedRunService`; nothing changes for users who don't pass
`--tracked`.

## Rollback Plan

Revert; the feature is client-side and opt-in.

fix: load this attempt's own checkpoint before the previous attempt's (#1728)

## Motivation
flyteorg/flyte#8258 lets a clustered task wait out a Kueue preemption in
its current attempt. When Kueue readmits the gang, the pods are
recreated with the same `JOBSET_RESTART_ATTEMPT`.
`TaskContext.checkpoint` only reads the attempt's own checkpoint when
that counter is above 0, so a readmitted gang loads the previous
attempt's checkpoint (or none) and loses the progress it saved before
the preemption.

## Summary
- `Checkpoint.load` / `load_sync` try the attempt's own
`checkpoint_path` first and fall back to `prev_checkpoint_path`. They no
longer return early when there is no previous checkpoint.
- `TaskContext.checkpoint` drops the `JOBSET_RESTART_ATTEMPT > 0`
special case. Each attempt has its own checkpoint prefix, so the own
path is empty on a fresh attempt. It only holds data when the same
attempt runs again (JobSet restart, Kueue readmission), and that data is
the newest state.
- A JobSet restart that crashed before its first save now falls back to
the previous attempt's checkpoint instead of starting from scratch.
- Logs which checkpoint was loaded (this attempt's or the previous
attempt's).

## Test Plan
- `pytest tests/flyte/test_checkpoint.py tests/flyte/clustered`: a table
of cases run sync and async (readmission on first and later attempts,
JobSet restart, fresh attempt, restart before first save, nothing
saved), plus a check that `remote_source` is still the previous
attempt's path. `make unit_test` passes.
- Devbox end-to-end with a flyte-binary built from flyteorg/flyte#8258,
JobSet v0.13.0 and Kueue 0.19.8:
- Setup: a ClusterQueue with `withinClusterQueue: LowerPriority`, and a
2-worker low-priority clustered task with `retries=0` and
`resume_after_preemption: true`. Rank 0 saves `{"step": n}` every step.
  - Preempt it with a high-priority Job and let Kueue readmit it.
- With this branch: same attempt, `restart_attempt=0`, resumed at step 6
(the last saved step), completed on attempt 1.
  - Control on `main`: same attempt, resumed at step 0.

Related: flyteorg/flyte#8258, flyteorg/flyte#8223

feat(io): per-call multipart part size and concurrency on upload APIs (#1684)

## Motivation

A customer hit S3 503 SlowDown from `Dir.from_local()` with many tasks
uploading to the same bucket, and asked for the multipart part size to
be settable through the call. #1681 made it configurable through
`FLYTE_IO_UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE` / `FLYTE_IO_UPLOAD_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, which
apply to the whole process. This adds the same two knobs as arguments on
the user-facing upload APIs. The env vars stay the default.

## Summary

- New `chunk_size` (minimum part size in bytes) and `max_concurrency`
(parts in flight per file) arguments on:
- `Dir.from_local`, `Dir.from_local_sync` (which also gains
`batch_size`, missing until now)
- `File.from_local`, `File.from_local_sync`, on both the hashed
(`put_stream`) and unhashed (`put`) paths
- `storage.put`, `storage.put_stream` (`chunk_size` was an undocumented
kwarg on `put_stream` and is now a named argument)
- `File.open("wb")` documents `chunk_size` / `max_concurrency` kwargs.
It now also honors the env vars: its part size is the larger of the 10
MiB writer buffer and `FLYTE_IO_UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE`.
- `chunk_size` is a floor. Values below 5 MiB are raised to 5 MiB with a
warning, the same rule as the env var. Very large files still scale
above it to stay under the 10,000-part limit. `max_concurrency` is
clamped to at least 1.
- Non-obstore filesystems (`file://`, `flyte://`, fsspec plugins such as
redis) ignore both arguments and log at debug level. fsspec has no
standard part-size kwarg, so nothing is forwarded to them. `put_stream`
also stops passing the env-derived `chunk_size` to them.
- Defaults are unchanged.

Not covered: DataFrame encoding, code bundle, pickle, report and
inputs/outputs uploads have no per-call argument. The env vars still
apply to them.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests in `tests/internal/storage/test_storage.py`,
`tests/flyte/io_types/test_files.py` and
`tests/flyte/io_types/test_dirs.py` cover:
- per-call values reach `put_async` (single-file and recursive) and
override the env defaults
  - clamping of values below the minimums
  - scaling above an explicit floor for very large files
  - `put_stream` passes the values to the writer
  - `open_writer_async` receives the buffer size and concurrency
  - the arguments are a no-op on non-obstore filesystems
  - `Dir` and `File`, sync and async, forward the arguments
- The related test suites pass (343 passed, 2 skipped), and mypy is
clean on the changed modules.
- Remote check on the demo tenant (S3), using a wheel built from this
branch with no env vars set. A 200 MiB file was uploaded each way and
the ETag part count read back:

| Call | Parts |

| `Dir.from_local` (default) | 40 |

4 |

| `File.from_local(hash_method=sha256, chunk_size=64 MiB)` | 4 |

Example: add async training with periodic eval and early stopping exa… (#721)

…mple

Add examples/ml/async_train_eval.py demonstrating a common ML pattern
where a long-running training task runs concurrently with periodic
evaluation rounds that can trigger early stopping on convergence.

How it works:
- A training task runs in the background via asyncio.create_task,
writing JSON checkpoints (epoch + loss) to a shared File location after
each epoch, and returning the final checkpoint on completion.
- The orchestrator loops through evaluation rounds, using
flyte.durable.sleep.aio (crash-resilient) between each round. The sleep
is raced against the training task via asyncio.wait so that training
completion or failure is detected immediately.
- Each eval round reads the latest checkpoint and launches a batch
inference task that checks if loss is below a convergence threshold.
- On convergence: training is cancelled and the pipeline returns early.
- On training failure: any in-progress eval is cancelled and the
exception propagates.
- On training completion: a final eval is run against the checkpoint
returned by the training task.

All tuning knobs (epochs, epoch duration, convergence threshold, eval
interval, max eval rounds) are exposed as parameters with defaults.


To run it
```bash
flyte run examples/ml/async_train_eval.py main
```

Add a third benchmark arm to examples/typesafe_ai so "could System 2 fill that schema itself?" is measurable (#1611)

## The problem

The `examples/typesafe_ai` benchmark compared two arms — with Jev and
without — and could not answer its own strongest counter-argument, the
first thing a sceptical reader says out loud: *the System 2 model could
have filled that schema itself, you just never asked it to.*

That objection was correct. The pair varied three things at once, so a
win for Jev was unattributable between them:

1. **who answers** the atomic questions,
2. whether the verdict is **composed in code** or reasoned out in a
prompt,
3. whether the pipeline may **abstain**.

Several scoring choices also leaned the same way — all of them in Jev's
favour.

## The fix: a third arm

`system2_structured` pins (2) and (3) down and varies only (1). System 2
answers exactly the battery Jev answers, against exactly the criteria
Jev is given, and runs through the same `derive()`, the same confidence
gate, the same tools and the same prose prompt.

| Arm | Fills the battery | Composes the verdict | May abstain |
|---|---|---|---|
| `with_system1` | System 1 (Jev), one parallel call |
`TaskSpec.derive()` | yes |
| `system2_structured` | System 2, autoregressively |
`TaskSpec.derive()` | yes |
| `without_system1` | System 2, autoregressively | the prompt | no |

Both composed arms call one shared `_compose_and_finish` rather than two
copies, so nothing downstream of the battery can drift apart and quietly
confound the comparison. Two independent readings fall out:

- **with Jev vs structured** — who is the better schema-filler,
everything else identical.
- **structured vs without** — what moving composition out of the prompt
and into Python is worth, model held fixed. This delta costs no System 1
vendor at all, and may be the more broadly useful number.

## Levelling the specification and the scoring

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| Jev got `true`/`false` criteria, label descriptions and every severity
tier; System 2 got bare keys — it was graded against a rubric it had
never seen | Both System 2 arms get the identical specification via
`_battery_spec()` |
| System 2 sampled at the gateway default while Jev is deterministic |
`temperature=0`, so decision-stability measures the model, not the
sampler |
| A signal answered `"yes"` instead of `true` scored as a dropped field
| Lenient counting, with the strict count beside it as a reported
**format gap** |
| A battery truncated at `max_tokens` was indistinguishable from one the
model declined to answer | `max_tokens` 4096→8192 and
`finish_reason`/`stop_reason` captured as `truncated` |
| An arm that escalated everything scored 0% success while doing exactly
what it was designed to do | New **coverage** metric as the denominator
for selective accuracy |

Two asymmetries are kept **deliberately**, and both are flagged in the
report:

- The with-Jev arm spends a second Jev call verifying its own
generation, so the structured arm runs the same three checks through
System 2 and is billed for them — rather than looking cheaper for
skipping work.
- The two gates are not the same quantity. Jev's confidence is a
calibrated probability; the structured arm's is a number the model was
asked to state about itself. That makes their routing split a test of
**calibration** — a real difference between the approaches, not a flaw
in the setup — but it must be read as that and not as accuracy.

## Verification

`logic_check.py` gains a second offline proof alongside the existing
one: a *perfect* System 2 answer sheet derives the identical label, tool
and routing tier as a perfect Jev battery, across all 36 cases,
including deliberately mixed boolean spellings. Without it a lossy
adapter could handicap the challenger and the benchmark would confirm
its own hypothesis.

```
all composition rules reproduce ground truth
both composed arms derive identically from a perfect battery
```

Both run offline in under a second — no API key, no tokens. An
end-to-end smoke test with stubbed models also runs all three arms clean
and renders the full report; `ruff`, `mypy` and `ty` all pass.

fix: validate TorchRun.rdzv_backend and the clustered restart budgets

`ClusteredTaskEnvironment.__post_init__` validates `replicas`, `nproc_per_node`,
`runtime`'s type, the JaxRun process-count rule and `interconnect`'s membership
in `_INTERCONNECT_VALUES` -- but not `rdzv_backend`, the two `max_restarts`
fields, or `ttl_seconds_after_finished`.

`rdzv_backend` is the sharpest of the four, because `to_custom_dict` resolves it
the same way it resolves `interconnect`, ten lines apart:

    interconnect=_interconnect_map[self.interconnect]   # guarded at construction
    rdzv_backend=_rdzv_map[self.runtime.rdzv_backend]   # not guarded

So `TorchRun(rdzv_backend="C10D")` -- a case typo on a documented value -- is
accepted and then dies as a bare `KeyError: 'C10D'`, naming neither the field
nor the class. A `Literal` is not enforced at runtime, which is precisely why
`interconnect` has an explicit check.

The restart budgets fail the other way. Both `max_restarts` fields reach a
*signed* int32 proto field, so a negative serializes silently:

    TorchRun(max_restarts=-1)  ->  {"runtime": {"torchrun": {"maxRestarts": -1}}}
    ClusterFailurePolicy(max_restarts=-2)  ->  {"failurePolicy": {"maxRestarts": -2}}

while a non-int dies as `TypeError: 'str' object cannot be interpreted as an
integer`. `ttl_seconds_after_finished` reaches a uint32 *wrapper* instead, so
protobuf does reject a negative -- as `ValueError: Value out of range: -5`,
which names no field.

`TorchRun` and `ClusterFailurePolicy` now validate their own fields, and
`ClusteredTaskEnvironment` checks `ttl_seconds_after_finished` beside the
`interconnect` check it already had.

feat(hermes): durable model turns via Hermes llm_execution middleware (#1591)

## What changed

The Hermes adapter (`plugins/agents/hermes`) documented `durable=True`
as a no-op because hermes-agent exposed no per-model-turn hook.
hermes-agent 0.17 added an `llm_execution` middleware that wraps every
provider call below the agent loop, so model turns can now be recorded
as `flyte.trace` leaves and replayed on a crashed or retried run, the
same way the openai, claude and crewai adapters do.

- New `_durable.py`: a middleware callback gated on a contextvar that
`run_agent` sets only while a `durable=True` call is in flight (the
Hermes middleware list is process-global, so the gate keeps other agents
in the process unaffected). It bridges the synchronous Hermes loop into
the async `durable_step` with `flyte._utils.asyn.run_sync`, matching the
CrewAI adapter.
- `_run.py` registers the callback idempotently and opens the gate
around `asyncio.to_thread`, with docstrings updated.
- Replay returns a recursively rebuilt `SimpleNamespace`. Verified
against installed hermes-agent 0.19.0 that the chat-completions and
anthropic transports read the response by attribute access only (no
`isinstance`, no `model_dump()`), and Hermes' own streaming path already
returns a `SimpleNamespace`. Because `durable_step` round-trips through
`loads` on the live pass too, the live and replayed shapes cannot drift.
- Streamed turns are fully drained before `next_call` returns, so they
are recorded as one completed turn. Replay does not re-emit deltas.
- `hermes-agent` bumped to `>=0.17` and re-locked. Example honesty notes
rewritten to describe replay. Nine new tests in
`test_hermes_durable.py`, and the old no-op test replaced with two
engagement tests.

## Why

Hopper asked in Slack whether Hermes' `llm_execution` middleware could
be wired to `flyte.trace` for durable model-turn replay, since the Union
docs say it is unsupported.

## Reviewer notes

- Only exercised with fakes. Replay on a real backend, and the codex and
bedrock api modes, still need a live run.
- The `durable=False` test asserts the gate stays closed rather than
that the callback is absent, since registration is process-global and
idempotent.
- The Union docs page for the Hermes integration should be updated after
this merges.

Add status filter to App.listall() and --status flag to flyte get apps (#1327)

## Motivation

There was no way to filter apps by deployment status server-side.
App.listall() only accepted created_by_subject, sort_by, and limit, even
though the underlying list_pb2.ListRequest supports arbitrary filters —
users had to fetch everything and filter client-side on
app.pb2.status.deployment_status.

 ## Summary
  
  SDK (src/flyte/remote/_app.py)
- App.listall() accepts a new optional in_status: str | Tuple[str, ...]
| None parameter, e.g. in_status="active" or in_status=("active",
"failed").
- Status names are case-insensitive and accepted with or without the
DEPLOYMENT_STATUS_ prefix; unknown names raise ValueError.
- A single status produces an EQUAL filter, multiple statuses produce
VALUE_IN, passed through the existing filtering() helper.

  **CLI (src/flyte/cli/_get.py)**
- flyte get apps gains a --status flag with choices generated from the
proto enum (unassigned, assigned, pending, stopped, started, failed,
active, scaling_up, scaling_down, deploying).
- Single-value for now, matching the existing --in-phase precedent; the
SDK API already accepts tuples
  so multiple=True can be added later.

  flyte get apps --status active
  flyte get apps --status failed --only-mine
  
  Wire contract (verified against a live backend)

The backend's app list endpoint filters on field="status_phase" and
matches by enum name (e.g. "DEPLOYMENT_STATUS_ACTIVE"), not the integer
enum value. This differs from the Action.listall phase
filter, which sends stringified integers — integer values silently
return zero rows here, and
alternative field names (deployment_status, status) are rejected by the
backend. Both EQUAL and
  VALUE_IN were verified to return exact matches.

  ## Testing
  
- New TestAppListallStatusFilter unit tests mock app_service.list and
assert the exact filter protos
sent: no filter when omitted, EQUAL/VALUE_IN shapes, case-insensitivity,
prefixed names, invalid-value
  error, and combination with created_by_subject.
- Live smoke test: flyte get apps --status active returns only ACTIVE
apps; server-side results match
  client-side filtering on deployment_status.
  - ruff and mypy clean.

feat: Add Anthropic Claude plugin for Flyte (#612)

## Summary

This PR adds a new plugin for integrating Anthropic's Claude API with
Flyte, following the same patterns as the existing OpenAI plugin.

### Features

- **`function_tool` decorator**: Convert Flyte tasks to Claude tool
definitions automatically
- **Automatic type conversion**: Python type hints → JSON schema for
tool input validation
- **`Agent` class**: Configure Claude agents with model, instructions,
and tools
- **`run_agent` function**: Execute agent loops that handle tool calls
and responses
- **Support for sync and async tasks**

### Usage Example

```python
import flyte
from flyteplugins.anthropic import function_tool, run_agent

env = flyte.TaskEnvironment("claude-agent")

@env.task
async def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Get the current weather for a city."""
    return f"Weather in {city}: sunny, 72F"

@env.task
async def agent_task(prompt: str) -> str:
    tools = [function_tool(get_weather)]
    return await run_agent(
        prompt=prompt,
        tools=tools,
        model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    )
```

### Files Added

- `plugins/anthropic/` - Plugin package
  - `pyproject.toml` - Package configuration
  - `README.md` - Documentation
- `src/flyteplugins/anthropic/agents/_function_tools.py` - Core
implementation
  - `tests/test_agents.py` - Test suite (19 tests)
- `examples/genai/anthropic_agent.py` - Example workflow

## Test Plan

- [x] All 19 unit tests pass
- [x] Type conversion tests (string, int, float, bool, list, dict,
Optional)
- [x] Function schema extraction tests
- [x] FunctionTool creation tests (regular functions, Flyte tasks,
async)
- [x] Agent configuration tests
- [x] Tool execution tests (sync and async)

## Why Anthropic?

Claude is one of the leading LLM providers alongside OpenAI. Having
first-class support for both enables users to:
- Choose the best model for their use case
- Easily switch between providers
- Use Claude's unique capabilities (longer context, better reasoning)

This plugin mirrors the OpenAI plugin's API design, making it easy to
switch between providers.

fix(artifacts): no source when a task publishes into another scope; say why scope is sent

The service's handler accepts an empty source scope and inherits the
artifact's, but flyteidl2's RunIdentifier validates org/project/domain as
min_len=1, so protovalidate rejects the request before the handler sees it;
the docstring now says so. And since the service only accepts a source in
the artifact's own org/project/domain, a task publishing into another
project sends no source rather than failing the publish (with empty scope
it would have been recorded as an action in the artifact's project, which
it is not).

rs_controller: publish flyte_core to crates.io

The Rust SDK at flyteorg/flyte-sdk-rs depends on this crate by git rev, and
crates.io refuses to publish a crate whose dependencies are not on the registry:

    all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when publishing.
    dependency `flyte_core` does not specify a version

So `flyte` cannot be released until `flyte_core` is. This makes that possible.

crates.io requires `description` and `license`, neither of which was set; the
repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0 but lives outside the crate directory, so this uses
the SPDX `license` key rather than `license-file`. Adds `repository`, `readme`,
`keywords` and `categories` alongside.

Adds `exclude` so the published tarball carries only the Rust crate. Without it,
uv.lock (81 KB), the wheel-builder Makefile and Dockerfile, and three hand-run
Python test scripts ship to crates.io. It affects the tarball only -- maturin
still reads pyproject.toml from the working tree, so wheel builds are unchanged.

The new workflow is deliberately separate from publish.yml. That one releases
the Python packages on `v*` tags, and its version comes from the Python release
train; folding the crate in would force flyte_core's version to track flyte's
and publish a crate on every SDK release whether or not the Rust code changed.
The crate version stays in Cargo.toml and is checked against the tag rather
than rewritten from it. Its pull_request trigger runs everything except the
upload, so the workflow is validated by this PR -- the idiom publish.yml already
uses -- and the upload step warns and skips while CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN is unset.

Feature defaults are untouched: `default = ["pyo3/auto-initialize"]` is what
flyte-sdk-rs wants today. Splitting a pure-Rust core out from the pyo3 bindings
needs flyteidl2 to make pyo3 optional first -- it is an unconditional dependency
there and annotates ~790 generated types as #[pyclass] -- so that is a later
breaking release. The new README documents both that and the flyte_core /
flyte_controller_base name mismatch.

Verified with `cargo publish --dry-run`, which now succeeds, and
`cargo package --list`, which shows the tarball free of the Python packaging.

Stream stderr as well as stdout to the UI's log viewer

`get_logs` tailed only stdout_path. sbatch gives each stream its own file, so a
job that failed usually has an empty .out and everything that matters in .err --
which made the log view blank for exactly the jobs someone opens it to read.

Found by calling get_logs against a real failed job on the cluster: it returned
0 lines, because that job's .out is 0 bytes while its .err holds the four lines
explaining the failure.

Both streams now stream, stdout first, each behind a `--- stderr: <path> ---`
marker so it is clear which is which, and an empty stream is skipped rather than
labelled. When neither has anything yet, one line says so and names the file
Slurm will create -- an empty response renders as a blank pane, which reads as a
broken viewer rather than as a job that has not written yet.

fix(extras): disjoint chunk-slice space across Volume forks

Volume.fork() previously cloned the metadata index byte-for-byte, leaving
parent and fork sharing the same nextChunk/nextInode/nextSession allocator
counters. Because JuiceFS chunk object keys are <vol>/chunks/<a>/<b>/<sliceid>_<idx>_<sz>
and the volume name is shared across a fork, both sides allocated identical
slice IDs after the fork point — same-size writes on either side overwrote
each other in the shared bucket.

Fix: bump nextChunk/nextInode/nextSession on the fork's metadata by a
random offset (random in [2^32, 2^32 + 2^56)) so the two sides allocate
from disjoint ID ranges. Applied to both engines (SQLite via direct UPDATE,
Redis via ephemeral redis-server + INCRBY) and to both fork paths (live
snapshot and cold download/upload). Also applied defensively to
migrate_metadata_engine since it has the same hazard if old + new engines
are ever used concurrently.

Overflow guard: clamp offset to half the remaining int64 headroom (JuiceFS
counters are signed int64) so deep fork chains don't overflow; raise if the
volume's allocator is exhausted.

Cold-fork path: replaces server-side File.copy_to with download → bump →
upload because counter mutation requires local access. Data chunks are
still not copied — only the metadata file.

Other changes:
- Pin _CLIENT_VERSION to 1.3.1 (verified counter schema matches 1.1.2's).
- Class docstring no longer says "SQLite index" — Redis is the default.
- New tests/flyte/extras/test_volume.py covers the bump helpers, the
  overflow guard, _client_bucket_uri, _default_bucket, the fork-isolation
  regression with a strict xfail for the original bug, and a SQLite↔Redis
  migration round-trip.

fix(extras): SQLite cold fork — track liveness explicitly, not via file

The cold-fork live-detection used "index.db exists on disk" as the
SQLite-engine signal. But commit() for SQLite WAL-checkpoints and
uploads — it doesn't unlink the local file. So a Volume that was
mounted, committed, and then forked (the canonical cold-fork shape)
would have its index.db still on disk and be misclassified as live,
falling back to _snapshot_and_upload_index instead of the new
File.copy_to server-side path.

Replace the heuristic with an explicit ClassVar[Set[str]] meta_dirs
set, populated by mount() and cleared by commit() — same lifecycle
shape as _live_redis. Now both engines route to File.copy_to in the
cold path; the previous bench showed only 2 of 4 cold cells hitting
the fast path because of this bug.

fix: degrade gracefully when keyring package is missing (FLYTE-SDK-6N) (#1301)

## Problem

`KeyringStore` token caching is best-effort: `store`/`retrieve`/`delete`
already swallow `NoKeyringError` and other keyring backend failures so
auth can proceed without a cached token. But the `import keyring` at
each call site was **unguarded**, so a broken/slim environment missing
the `keyring` package raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named
'keyring'` that escaped through the auth flow.

Sentry **FLYTE-SDK-6N** (on 2.5.6): the missing package surfaced as a
hard crash of the entire `SelectCluster -> upload -> run` path:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'keyring'
  @ _keyring.retrieve
  @ client_credentials.__init__
  @ factory.get_async_authenticator
-> RuntimeError: SelectCluster failed for operation=1: No module named 'keyring'
-> RuntimeSystemError: Upload failed for /tmp/.../spec.pb (org='archipelago', ...)
```

`keyring>=25.6.0` is a declared dependency, but partial/slim installs
can still be missing it. Token caching is purely an optimization — a
missing backend must degrade gracefully, not take down the run.

## Fix

Guard the `import keyring` in all three call sites
(`store`/`retrieve`/`delete`). A missing keyring package now degrades to
"no cached tokens" (return credentials unchanged / `None` / no-op),
exactly matching how `NoKeyringError` is already handled.

## Tests

3 new regression tests force `import keyring` to raise `ImportError`
(via `sys.modules["keyring"] = None`) and assert each method degrades
instead of raising. 22/22 keyring-store tests pass.

fixes FLYTE-SDK-6N

fix: report a missing file in an image definition as the user error it is

`ImageBuildEngine.build` asks `image_exists()` for the image tag before it
calls `image.validate()`, and computing that tag hashes the files the image
definition names. So a user who points `with_uv_project(uvlock=...)` at a
file that is not there gets a bare

    FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../does-not-exist.lock'

raised from inside `filehash_update`, and reported to Sentry as an SDK crash.

`UVProject.validate()` has had a clear message for exactly this mistake since
it was written -- "UVLock file ... does not exist" -- along with
`PoetryProject`, `PixiProject` and `UVScript`. None of them ever get to run on
this path, because the unguarded read in `update_hash()` always fires first.

Ask the layer to diagnose itself when a hash-time read fails, and rewrite the
error only when it actually objects. A read that fails while the layer
considers its own definition fine is not a mistake in the image spec, so it
keeps its original exception and stays reportable.

harden central MCP mode: rate limits, token-endpoint check, control-plane allowlist

The central endpoint is public and multi-tenant, so the endpoint allowlist is
the only thing between it and whatever else the server can reach. It previously
matched a parent-domain suffix, which is the wrong test: a shared parent domain
also carries app hostnames, per-cluster and per-tenant delegations,
infrastructure and third-party services, and zones whose DNS records are
written outside this system. A name whose address is chosen elsewhere is an
SSRF primitive that TLS verification does not catch. It was also incomplete —
not every managed control plane sits under one parent domain, so real tenants
were locked out.

Replaced with anchored control-plane patterns in which the org is exactly one
DNS label. That single-label rule is load-bearing: anything needing an extra

fix(controller): guard against None responses in informer watch loop

When gRPC deserialization fails, grpc._common._transform() logs the
exception and returns None instead of raising.  In the informer's watch
loop this caused an AttributeError on resp.control_message, which
crashed the loop and triggered a retry/backoff cycle.  During that
backoff window the trace-action completion event was never received, so
wait_for_action_completion() blocked forever.

Two fixes:
1. _informer.py: skip None responses with a warning so the stream stays
   alive and can receive the real completion update on the next message.
2. _core.py: add a 60-second timeout on wait_for_action_completion() for
   trace actions only (task actions may run for hours).  On timeout we
   fire the completion event ourselves so the caller is unblocked even if
   the server update was genuinely missed.  The timeout is configurable
   via _F_TRACE_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT.

fix(io): stop File/Dir from guessing blobs tagged by another transformer (#1650)

## Why

A custom `TypeTransformer` that represents its type as a blob with a
custom `format` and `structure.tag` loses to `FileTransformer` in
`TypeEngine.guess_python_type` whenever `flyte.io` is imported first.
`guess_python_type` returns the first registered transformer that does
not raise, and `FileTransformer.guess_python_type` accepted every SINGLE
blob except `PythonPickle`. `DirTransformer` has the same issue for
MULTIPART blobs.

That breaks running a deployed task by remote reference
(`flyte.remote.Task.get(...)` + `flyte.run`), where the interface is
guessed from literal types:

```
TypeError: Type conversion failed for variable 'artifact'.
Expected type: <class 'flyte.io._file.File'>
Actual type: <class '...GeoDataFrameArtifact'>
```

Plain `import flyte` does not load `flyte.io`, so the bug only shows up
once user code imports it, which makes it look like an import side
effect.

## What

`FileTransformer` and `DirTransformer` now raise `ValueError` from
`guess_python_type` when the literal type carries a `structure.tag`
other than their own, the same rule
`DataclassTransformer.guess_python_type` already follows. Untagged blobs
and blobs tagged `File` / `Dir` (including union variants) are still
claimed.

## Testing

- Added regression tests in `tests/flyte/io_types/test_files.py` and
`test_dirs.py`; they fail without the fix.
- `tests/flyte/io_types` and `tests/flyte/type_engine` pass.
- Reproduced end to end against a cluster: a custom blob transformer
plus `import flyte.io`, run by remote reference, fails on `main` and
succeeds with this change.

feat(github): form-encoded deliveries, GitHub App installation tokens, installation events (#1541)

Follow-up to #1540 (Slack): the same exercise for the GitHub plugin —
study how the internal agents actually use GitHub, and close the gaps in
`flyteplugins-github` that would block them (or any similar agent) from
adopting it.

## What the agents actually do with GitHub

- **Cally** (`oncall_agent/github_app.py`) holds no PAT: it
authenticates as a GitHub App and mints 1-hour installation tokens for
read-only clones, with a `GH_TOKEN` fallback and a
degrade-to-`None`-with-a-logged-reason contract. Its chat app
(`opencode_chat/mint_gh_token.py`) carries a **verbatim copy** of that
logic, with a docstring noting the copy exists because "the two projects
ship as separate code bundles and share no package."
- **Nodey** (`node_changer_agent.py::get_github_app_token`) is a **third
copy** of the same minting flow — with the app id and installation id
hardcoded and no error handling — feeding clones, pushes, and `gh pr
create`.
- **Engy** (`webhook_app.py`) runs the one hand-rolled GitHub webhook
receiver: `issue_comment.created` carrying a `/swe_agent fix` command,
plus `issues.labeled`. Its setup instructions have to warn users to
switch the webhook's content type to `application/json` — because
GitHub's *Add webhook* form **defaults** to
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, which naive receivers (and this
plugin, until now) choke on.

## Gaps closed

1. **Form-encoded deliveries.** `parse()` only accepted JSON bodies; a
webhook left on GitHub's default content type wraps the JSON in a
`payload=` form field and every delivery would have failed. `parse` now
sniffs and unwraps both shapes into the same `WebhookEvent` — same
`qualified_type`, same dedupe key — so a redelivery on the other content
type is still a redelivery. `verify` already covered both, since the
HMAC signs the raw body.
2. **GitHub App installation tokens** (`[auth]` extra, PyJWT[crypto]).
`mint_installation_token()` + `clone_url()` replace the three per-agent
copies: env-var configuration (`GITHUB_APP_ID` /
`GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` / `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`),
explicit-argument override, `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` fallbacks for
one-secret-at-a-time migration, and Cally's degrade-to-`None` contract
so half-configured deployments keep working unauthenticated instead of
crashing.
3. **`Installation` / `InstallationRepositories` event constants.**
Every GitHub App webhook receives these unconditionally, and all three
agent deployments authenticate as Apps; they normalize with no resource
and dedupe per delivery.

## Deliberately not done

- No `workflow_job` / `deployment_status` / `status` constants — no
agent touches them; raw strings still work if one ever does.
- No slash-command-style parsing: engy's `/swe_agent fix` trigger is
just an `issue_comment` body, which the existing normalization already
carries verbatim in `event.payload` (verified by a test modeled on
engy's exact trigger payload).
- No PyGithub wrapping beyond the existing review gate — unchanged
plugin boundary, now stated as "the parts every GitHub agent otherwise
duplicates."

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q` — 41 passed (new: form-encoded
parity with the engy-shaped `/swe_agent fix` payload,
signature-over-form-body, rejection of a form body with no `payload`
field, installation-event dedupe, and Cally's
JWT-verifies/fallback/outage/clone-URL matrix against a real RSA key
with the HTTP seam monkeypatched).
- `python examples/github_webhooks.py --local` now also replays the
sample delivery form-encoded and prints it landing on the identical
dedupe key.
- `uvx ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; conformance test
unchanged and passing.

The Hermes adapter (`plugins/agents/hermes`) documented `durable=True`
as a no-op because hermes-agent exposed no per-model-turn hook.
hermes-agent 0.17 added an `llm_execution` middleware that wraps every
provider call below the agent loop, so model turns can now be recorded
as `flyte.trace` leaves and replayed on a crashed or retried run, the
same way the openai, claude and crewai adapters do.

`run_agent` sets only while a `durable=True` call is in flight (the

rewritten to describe replay. Nine new tests in

types: preserve pydantic Field metadata on Annotated task inputs (#1670)

## Why

Task inputs like

```python
@env.task
def my_task(
    my_s3_uri: Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^s3://")],
    my_float: Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, le=1)],
): ...
```

produce a JSON schema of just `type: string` / `type: float`. The
`pattern`, `minimum`/`maximum`, and any `title`, `description`, `format`
or `json_schema_extra` on the pydantic `Field` were dropped.

The type engine unwrapped `Annotated` to find a transformer and
discarded the metadata, and `literal_type_to_json_schema` only read
`LiteralType.metadata` for STRUCT types. Enums went further and raised
on any `Annotated` wrapper.

## What

- `TypeEngine.to_literal_type` detects pydantic field metadata on
`Annotated` types (`pydantic.Field`, `annotated_types` constraints such
as `Gt`/`MinLen`, `StringConstraints`, `WithJsonSchema`) and records the
JSON-schema keys it adds over the bare type in `LiteralType.metadata`.
Pydantic's `TypeAdapter` does the mapping, so `min_length` becomes
`minLength` on a string and `minItems` on a list.
- Structural keys (`type`, `anyOf`, `$ref`, `items`, `properties`, ...)
and `default` are never copied. Whether an input is required still comes
from the function signature.
- `Annotated[Optional[str], Field(pattern=...)]` pushes the constraint
onto the non-None variant, mirroring pydantic. Keys recorded on the
union itself (`description`, `title`) are not repeated per variant.
- `literal_type_to_json_schema` overlays that metadata for non-STRUCT
types. Integral doubles from the protobuf `Struct` are turned back into
ints.
- `EnumTransformer` unwraps `Annotated` instead of raising, so
`Annotated[MyEnum, Field(description=...)]` works.
- Types pydantic cannot describe (e.g. a pandas DataFrame) log at debug
level and are left unchanged. Non-pydantic annotations (`Annotated[str,
"note"]`, renderers, transformers) are ignored as before.

The example above now yields:

```json
{"my_s3_uri": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^s3://"},
 "my_float":  {"type": "number", "format": "float", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1}}
```

## Notes

- This is schema only: values are not validated against
`pattern`/`ge`/`le` at runtime.
- The SDK-side consumers (`task.json_schema`, agent tool definitions)
pick the constraints up immediately. The constraints are also shipped to
the backend in `LiteralType.metadata` on registration, but the launch
form will only show them once the UI reads that field.

## Tests

Added cases to `tests/flyte/test_json_schema.py` covering constraints,
documentation keys, `json_schema_extra`, containers, structs, enums,
Optional/Union, value round trips, and the task-level schema. The JSON
schema, type engine, types, ai, cli, internal, models and signature
parsing suites pass; ruff and mypy are clean.

fix: don't report an exhausted upload retry as an SDK crash (FLYTE-SDK-7N, FLYTE-SDK-7P) (#1553) ## Why `_put_signed_url_with_retry` (`src/flyte/remote/_data.py`) PUTs the code bundle — and tracked-run metadata — to a signed object-store URL. It keeps its own retry table, and every entry in it means *"the store is unhealthy right now, send it again"*: ```python if put_resp.status_code in [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504] or _is_retryable_store_error(...): ``` plus, in the `except` arm, `httpx.TimeoutException / NetworkError / OSError`. When every attempt loses to the same condition, both arms raise `RuntimeSystemError`. **They were then reported inconsistently:** | half | how it fails | cause chain | reached Sentry? | |---|---|---|---| | transport (`httpx.ReadError`, timeouts, …) | `raise RuntimeSystemError(...) **from e**` | terminates in an httpx error | **no** — `_is_transient_network_error` filters it (it names `FLYTE-SDK-36` for this exact leg) | | HTTP status (502/503/500/…) | `raise RuntimeSystemError(...)` | **empty** — it is reacting to an `httpx.Response`, there is no exception to chain | **yes**, as an SDK crash | Same outage, same exhausted retries, opposite treatment. The filter never had anything to match on, because the failure the SDK is reporting was never an exception in the first place. Reproduced on `main` — an nginx `502` on every attempt: ``` raised: RuntimeSystemError code=UploadFailed __cause__: None _is_user_error (True == filtered from Sentry): False <-- leaks ``` and the sibling, for contrast: ``` TRANSPORT half -> code=UploadFailed cause=ReadError _is_user_error (filtered?): True <-- already fine ``` ## Impact `FLYTE-SDK-7N` (4 events, rel 2.6.5) and `FLYTE-SDK-7P` (6 events, rel 2.6.10) — both `Failed to upload …​ after 3 retries: status 502:`, one from `flyte run`, one straight from `_upload_with_retry`. 10 events of "the object store's gateway was down for four consecutive attempts" filed as Python-SDK crashes. **Update (2026-09-11):** `FLYTE-SDK-8C` (2 events, rel 2.7.2, first seen today) is the same leak on a different status — `Failed to upload … after 3 retries: status 503:` with an S3 `SlowDownPlease reduce your request rate.` body. 503 is in the retry table this filter keys off, so it is already covered by the change as written; no code change was needed to pick it up. Worth noting that the store asking us to slow down is about as clear a "not an SDK bug" as this class gets. Nothing in them is actionable in Python: the SDK asked for the object to be stored, retried on the schedule it advertises, and got a transient failure every time. ## What changed The exhaustion path gets its own error code, and `_sentry` filters on it. - `_data.py`: both exhaustion sites now raise `_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED_CODE` (`"UploadRetriesExhausted"`) instead of `"UploadFailed"`. Both, not just the leaking one — they are the same outcome, and a reader finding two different codes on two branches of one retry loop would be right to be confused. The transport half's filtering is unchanged either way (its cause chain still does the work). - `_sentry.py`: `_is_exhausted_upload_retry` joins the chain walk in `_is_user_error`. Keyed on the error **code**, not the message, so it cannot drift with wording. The code is read via `sys.modules.get("flyte.remote._data")` rather than imported: only that module raises this error, so if it was never imported no exception can carry the code — and a capture never drags in httpx/aiofiles/the remote client just to compare a string. ## Deliberately narrow - `"UploadFailed"` — a status the retry table **never** retries, e.g. a 403 on a signed URL — keeps reporting. - `"UploadUrlExpired"` keeps reporting. - This is strictly the **object-store PUT leg**. A 500 on the *control-plane RPC* leg arrives as a `ConnectError` and is untouched — `FLYTE-SDK-64` (276 events, `SelectCluster` → `Internal Server Error`) is real backend signal and still reports. There is a test pinning that. I tested the predicate across the whole unresolved corpus before writing it (71 issues / 1789 events): exactly `7N` and `7P` match, both `status 502`. Nothing else in the corpus is silenced. ## Tests `tests/flyte/test_sentry.py` — these drive the **real** retry loop to exhaustion rather than hand-constructing the error: - `test_capture_exception_skips_upload_that_exhausted_its_retries` — the production bug; also asserts `__cause__ is None`, which is *why* it leaked - `test_capture_exception_skips_upload_that_exhausted_its_retries_on_transport` — the two halves must not diverge again - `test_capture_exception_still_reports_a_non_retryable_upload_failure` — 403 still reports - `test_exhausted_upload_filter_ignores_other_system_errors` — guards the `FLYTE-SDK-64` class explicitly - `test_exhausted_upload_filter_tracks_the_code_data_actually_raises` — pins the premise, so renaming the constant in `_data` can't silently switch the filter off `tests/flyte/remote/test_upload_retry.py` — `test_exhausted_transient_status_gets_its_own_error_code`, `test_exhausted_transport_failure_shares_the_exhausted_code`, `test_non_retryable_status_keeps_the_plain_upload_failure_code`. Reverting only the wiring (keeping the symbols defined, so imports still resolve) fails 3 of them, including the capture test; the guard tests pass either way by design. ## Checks - `make fmt` — clean - `make mypy` — `Success: no issues found in 870 source files` - `ty check` on both changed files — `All checks passed!` - `make check-docstrings` — `523 files clean` - `pytest tests/` — 5712 passed; the 24 failures are pre-existing and reproduce identically on clean `origin/main` (local minio/sandbox and Docker dependencies) --- Sentry issues are not mirrored into GitHub issues for this repo (issues are disabled on `flyteorg/flyte-sdk`), so the trailers reference the Sentry short IDs: fixes FLYTE-SDK-7N fixes FLYTE-SDK-7P fixes FLYTE-SDK-8C - https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/?query=FLYTE-SDK-7N - https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/?query=FLYTE-SDK-7P - https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/?query=FLYTE-SDK-8C Signed-off-by: Haytham Abuelfutuh

feat(cli): flyte proxy app keeps a Union LLM gateway key sent as the bearer (#1618)

## Why
`flyte proxy app` drops the client's `Authorization` header and injects
the Union bearer that the app's auth edge needs. For a Union LLM gateway
behind Union sign-in, that also throws away the gateway's virtual key
whenever a client sends it the OpenAI way (`Authorization: Bearer
sk-un-…`). As a result, every OpenAI-compatible client going through the
proxy got:

```
401 virtual_key_required: virtual key is required. Provide a virtual key via the x-bf-vk header.
```

The only workaround was to know about the gateway's `x-bf-vk` header and
set it by hand (for example `default_headers={"x-bf-vk": ...}` in the
OpenAI SDK).

## What
`_filter_request_headers` still drops the client's `Authorization`
header, with one exception. When the client sends a Union LLM gateway
virtual key as the bearer (`Bearer sk-un-…`), the proxy moves the key to
`x-bf-vk`.
- The proxy still injects the Union bearer, as before.
- An explicit `x-bf-vk` from the client takes precedence.
- Any other client `Authorization` (other bearers, `Basic`, a bare key
without a scheme) is still dropped, so nothing else is forwarded that
wasn't before.

With this, the plain OpenAI SDK works through the proxy:

```python
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8600/v1", api_key="sk-un-...")
```

## Testing
- **Unit:** `tests/cli/test_proxy.py`, 9 passed (3 new):
  - the key moves to `x-bf-vk`;
  - an explicit `x-bf-vk` wins;
- other bearers, `Basic`, a bare key and an empty bearer are still
dropped.
- **Live**, against a Union LLM gateway behind Union sign-in on a canary
org (`flyte proxy app --url <gateway> --port 8601`):
- `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-un-…" …/v1/models` returns the
key's models. The unpatched proxy returns `401 virtual_key_required` for
the same request.
- The stock OpenAI SDK with `api_key="sk-un-…"` gets a chat completion.
- **Lint:** ruff check and format are clean.

Tools need a different mechanism here than in the client-side SDKs. The harness
has no tool-registration message: its wire protocol is `initialize` /
`session/prompt`, and its tool surface is whatever its Cordis composition
provides inside the runtime subprocess (its in-process `harness.registerTool` is
a TypeScript plugin API the Python SDK can't reach). What every composition does
provide is local bash in a workspace we choose, so each Flyte-task tool is
published there as an executable shim that calls back over a Unix socket into
`task.aio(...)` — a durable child action with its own container/resources,
retries and caching. The tool manual rides on the prompt, since there is no
tool-declaration channel either.

`DeepSeekHarness.run` is blocking, so it is driven via `asyncio.to_thread`; that
is what keeps the event loop free to serve tool calls while the agent works.

Durability is session resume rather than per-turn replay (the model loop is in a
subprocess Flyte doesn't intercept, as with the Claude adapter): the harness's
JSONL session store is mirrored onto a `flyte.Checkpoint`, keyed by a session id
derived from the task's action, so a retry continues the conversation. With
`memory_key` the same archive is kept in a keyed `MemoryStore` instead, giving
cross-run memory and subsuming crash-resume.

Also renders the run timeline into the task report, mapping the runtime's
session events (assistant turns with token usage, `tool/call` / `tool/result`,
`turn/end`) plus the bridge's per-tool outcomes.

Includes 61 tests — the bridge ones run the published shim as a real subprocess,
covering shim -> socket -> `task.aio` end to end, including concurrent calls and
tool failures — plus six examples and the adapter README.

feat(ray): support ReusePolicy — run Ray tasks on shared, reusable RayClusters (#1308)

## Why

`ReusePolicy` today only supports container/pod tasks (reusable actors).
Ray tasks always pay full RayCluster cold-start cost on every run, even
when many runs share an identical cluster spec.

This PR lets users opt a Ray task environment into a shared, reusable
RayCluster:

```python
ray_env = flyte.TaskEnvironment(
    name="ray_env",
    plugin_config=RayJobConfig(...),
    reusable=flyte.ReusePolicy(replicas=1, idle_ttl=600),
)
```

## What changed

Core stays plugin-agnostic, and the task type is unchanged — reuse is
signaled through the task's custom spec:

- **Core**: plugins opt in to reuse via a `supports_reuse_policy` class
attribute (checked by the `TaskEnvironment` reusable+plugin_config
guard) and an `apply_reuse_policy(task_template)` hook that task
serialization dispatches to instead of `add_reusable`. No Ray knowledge
in `reuse.py`.
- **Ray plugin**: validates the policy (`replicas` maps to the number of
shared clusters; only 1 supported for now, otherwise `BadConfiguration`)
and records it under a `reusePolicy` key in the task's custom (RayJob)
spec. The field is unknown to the RayJob proto and ignored by its
unmarshalling — the task type stays `ray`, so backends without
shared-cluster support simply run the task as a normal ephemeral Ray
job.
- Backends with shared-cluster support route on the presence of
`reusePolicy`: shared RayCluster (keyed by the Ray spec hash, so
identical specs reuse one cluster) when present, ephemeral otherwise.
The generic backend plugin interface lives in flyteorg/flyte#7460.
- Example: `examples/plugins/ray_reusable_cluster.py`.

## Tests

- `tests/flyte/internal/runtime/test_reuse.py` — core behavior unchanged
(9 passing).
- `plugins/ray/tests/test_task.py` — policy recorded in custom with type
unchanged; multi-replica rejection (9 passing).

Classify task load EIO as system error (#1264)

## Problem

Task import/load failures happen before the normal task execution
wrapper. The runtime already uploads an `error.pb` for these failures,
but a raw `OSError` with `errno.EIO` was converted through the generic
fallback instead of being attributed as a system failure.

That means filesystem/image read failures like `[Errno 5] Input/output
error` during module import can be surfaced with the wrong attribution,
even though `EIO` indicates the runtime failed to read bytes from the
underlying filesystem/storage layer rather than a deterministic
user-code error.

## Solution

Classify only task-load `OSError` values with `errno.EIO` as
`RuntimeSystemError` before converting and uploading the load failure
error document.

All other load-time exceptions, including non-EIO `OSError` values such
as `FileNotFoundError`, continue through the existing generic path.

tests/flyte/internal/runtime/test_entrypoints.py`
- `uv run python -m ruff check

tests/flyte/internal/runtime/test_entrypoints.py`

Fix: propagate sub-action error on parent recovery (USER error masked as SYSTEM) (#1270)

**Severity: Critical**

When a parent action recovers/retries and re-watches a sub-action that
is already in a terminal `FAILED` state, the controller passes the local
`action` stub (not the observed final state `n`) to
`handle_action_failure`. The stub has no phase/error, so a recoverable
**USER** error gets masked as a **SYSTEM** `UnableToConvertError: ...
None`. That synthesized error is itself recoverable, so the parent
retries and re-hits the same failed child indefinitely.

First attempts are unaffected — only the recovery path is broken.

## Fix
Pass `n` (the observed/cached final state) to `handle_action_failure` in
`_submit` and `_submit_task_ref`.

## Test
Adds a regression test for the recovery race (fails before, passes
after) and updates `test_submit_task_with_error`, which had asserted the
buggy fallback. `pytest tests/internal/controllers/` → 97 passed.

fix: retry GetActionData NOT_FOUND for actions already observed as terminal

The watch/poll stream can report ActionPhase.SUCCEEDED slightly before the
action's attempt/output record is queryable via GetActionData, which is
served by a different backend path. Calling run.outputs()/action.outputs()
right after seeing a terminal phase could hit this window and surface a
spurious "outputs not available" / "no attempts for action" NOT_FOUND,
even though the action really did succeed. The generic RPC retry
interceptor intentionally excludes NOT_FOUND (a real not-found shouldn't
be retried), so this transient race went straight to the caller.

_fetch_action_data now retries NOT_FOUND with backoff, but only when the
action is already known done() -- a NOT_FOUND for an action that isn't
terminal yet, or any other error code, still fails immediately.

feat(logging): log Python warnings through the root logger Flyte sets up

With reset_root_logger, Flyte gives the root logger its own handler, so
lines from libraries are formatted like Flyte's, as JSON under
LOG_FORMAT=json. Python warnings don't go through logging, though. They
are still printed to stderr as plain text, where a log collector that
reads severity from structured lines finds none, and GKE's Cloud
Logging marks every such line ERROR.

_setup_root_logger now calls logging.captureWarnings(True), so warnings
go to the "py.warnings" logger and propagate to the root handler it
just added, at WARNING and in the same format as other lines. It does
this only when it resets the root logger: without a root handler, the
standard library gives "py.warnings" a NullHandler and captured
warnings are dropped instead of printed.

fix: raise actionable error when module file is outside root_dir

the dotted module name from a Python file path. When the user runs

`PicklingError`/`TypeError` and the raw stack ends up in Sentry.

Wrap the version-hash computation and translate those pickle failures
into a `click.ClickException` that names the most common cause and
points the user at the `version=` escape hatch. This short-circuits
the Sentry filter added in #1039 so we stop logging user-side closure
mistakes as SDK crashes.

Closes FLYTE-SDK-21

docs: fix _Condition docstring example to use .aio() in async task (#1268)

The `_Condition` class docstring (which surfaces in the API reference)
shows:

```python
condition = await flyte.new_condition(name="my_condition", ...)
result = await condition.wait()
```

But `new_condition` and `_Condition.wait` are `@syncify` — the bare call
is sync (returns the value, not an awaitable), so `await
flyte.new_condition(...)` / `await condition.wait()` raise `TypeError`
inside an `async def` task. The correct async form is `.aio()`:

```python
condition = await flyte.new_condition.aio(name="my_condition", ...)
result = await condition.wait.aio()
```

This matches `examples/advanced/conditions.py` and the auto-generated
"use `.aio()` to call asynchronously" note. Docs-only (docstring); no
behavior change.

Surfaced while writing the External conditions user-guide page
(unionai-docs#1087); the page had copied this same pattern.

fix: don't crash-report a non-Connect endpoint answering a Connect RPC (FLYTE-SDK-77, FLYTE-SDK-7A) (#1411)

## What

`flyte run` and `flyte deploy` from a Windows host failed with
`RuntimeSystemError: Upload failed for C:\Users\...\fast….tar.gz`, whose
cause was a bare `ConnectError: No Content` — raised out of both
`CreateUploadLocation` (`_data.py`) and `SelectCluster`
(`controlplane.py`). Both were reported to Sentry as SDK crashes.

A Connect endpoint answers a unary POST with **200 + a Connect body**,
or with an **error status + a Connect JSON body**. HTTP **204 is
neither**. A *success* status that isn't 200 means the request never
reached a Connect handler at all — a proxy, VPN appliance, captive
portal, corporate TLS interceptor or misrouted ingress absorbed it and
answered on the backend's behalf. That's endpoint/network configuration,
not a Python-SDK logic bug, and the SDK can't recover from it.

This is the same rationale already applied to `UNIMPLEMENTED` in
`_USER_ACTIONABLE_CONNECT_CODES` ("a raw HTTP 404 from the ingress … the
endpoint config is wrong").

## Why the check looks the way it does

connectrpc maps only a handful of HTTP statuses onto Connect codes
(401/403/404/429/502/503/504). Everything else falls through to
`ConnectWireError.from_http_status`, which produces `Code.UNKNOWN`, **no
details**, and the stdlib reason phrase as the *entire* message. The
numeric status is dropped on the floor, so matching the phrase is the
only way back to the status class.

## Deliberately narrow — and why that matters

HTTP 500 produces an **identically shaped** error: `Code.UNKNOWN`, no
details, message `"Internal Server Error"`. Filtering on "message is a
bare HTTP phrase" would therefore have silenced real backend signal,
including **FLYTE-SDK-64 (276 events)**, 6S and 43. Only the 2xx class
is unambiguously "an intermediary answered instead of the backend", so
only it is filtered.

I checked this against the live corpus before writing the fix — every
`ConnectError` across all 67 unresolved issues, and the only ones
carrying a *2xx* phrase are 77 and 78. Genuine backend errors all carry
verbose Go-style messages (`rpc error: code = … desc = …`), and the
backend-collapses-code-into-UNKNOWN family (67/4T) is untouched.

Verified behaviour:

| response | code | message | filtered |
|---|---|---|---|
| 204 / 202 | UNKNOWN | `No Content` / `Accepted` | ✅ yes |
| 500 | UNKNOWN | `Internal Server Error` | ❌ no (real signal) |
| 302 | UNKNOWN | `Found` | ❌ no |
| 404 / 401 / 502 | UNIMPLEMENTED / UNAUTHENTICATED / UNAVAILABLE | — |
❌ no (already handled) |
| backend UNKNOWN + verbose msg | UNKNOWN | `rpc error: code =
Unavailable desc = …` | ❌ no |

## Tests

10 new tests. 7 fail without the `_sentry.py` change; the two
**regression guards** (500 and backend-UNKNOWN still reach Sentry) pass
both before and after — that's the point of them. Full file: 55 passed.

## Follow-up not included here

Filtering stops the false crash report but the user still sees
`ConnectError: No Content`, which is opaque. A clearer message ("the
endpoint returned HTTP 204 with no Connect payload — something between
this machine and `<endpoint>` intercepted the request") would need a
chokepoint at the RPC boundary; kept out of this PR to keep it
reviewable.

---

## Update: the same root cause via connectrpc's other rejection path
(FLYTE-SDK-7A)

Added in a follow-up commit on this branch. connectrpc has a second way
of saying "this is not a Connect response" — when the body's
content-type cannot be decoded by the codec:

```
ConnectError(Code.UNKNOWN, "invalid content-type: 'text/html'; expecting 'application/proto'")
```

An HTML page where a protobuf body belongs means the same thing a 204
does: a proxy, login page or misrouted ingress answered instead of the
backend. `_client_config.py` already draws exactly this conclusion for
this exact signature when it comes back from the auth metadata fetch
(#1235) —
[FLYTE-SDK-7A](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/?query=FLYTE-SDK-7A) and
[FLYTE-SDK-6P](https://unionai.sentry.io/issues/?query=FLYTE-SDK-6P) are
the same thing arriving on a data-plane call.

Kept as narrow as the status-class check: only `text/*` matches, so an
`application/*` mismatch — which would point at a codec bug on our side
— keeps reporting.

**Corpus check.** Following the same discipline as the 2xx
discriminator, the predicate was tested against `events/latest` for
*every* unresolved issue in the project. Exactly two match — 7A and 6P —
and no backend-owned issue does. Worth calling out explicitly:
FLYTE-SDK-3A and FLYTE-SDK-4K embed an **nginx HTML error page inside
the message** and do *not* match, because the filter keys on
connectrpc's own message shape rather than on any mention of HTML. There
is a regression test pinning that.

Note 6P is nominally tracked by #1340; its latest event has since
drifted to this content-type shape, so this is what would actually stop
it firing. Left the `fixes` line to #1340 rather than claiming it from
two PRs.

Add `flyte proxy app`: authenticated localhost proxy into a Flyte App

Adds a `flyte proxy app NAME` command — an authenticated localhost reverse
proxy into a no-auth-inside Flyte App. Reuses the CLI authenticator to inject a
fresh bearer on every request so a local HTTP client (an MCP server, curl, a
browser) reaches an app-edge-gated app with no token handling.

- Resolve the target by app name (App.get) or an explicit --url.
- Bind loopback on both 127.0.0.1 and ::1 so `localhost` (which resolves to ::1
  first on macOS) is not silently shadowed by a wildcard listener from another
  process (e.g. a container runtime on *:PORT with SO_REUSEPORT); a genuine
  conflict now fails loudly with EADDRINUSE instead of half-binding.
- Stream responses unbuffered and preserve Content-Encoding (SSE-safe for MCP
  streamable-HTTP).
- Drop inbound Authorization/hop-by-hop headers; inject the fresh bearer on the
  standard `authorization` header (the SDK auth flow may emit it under a
  gRPC-style metadata key the HTTP app edge never reads); refresh + retry once
  when the edge bounces an expired token to /login.
- --emit-mcp-config prints a generic HTTP-MCP client block.

Also materialize delayed app parameters (e.g. RunOutput) on the pod_template
serialization path: the container path already resolved them to a File/Dir URI,
but the pod_template path serialized the raw getter, so an app that set a
pod_template could not download its input. Thread parameter_overrides through
_get_k8s_pod / _serialized_pod_spec.

Unit tests cover header filtering, Content-Encoding preservation, JWT identity
display, and the MCP-config block.

fix(remote): use OS DNS resolver in pyqwest transport

pyqwest defaults to use_system_dns=False, which routes all RPCs through
the bundled trust-dns resolver. trust-dns happily returns AAAA records
even on hosts with no usable IPv6 default route (e.g. tethered mobile
hotspots that advertise IPv6 via RA but don't actually route it). The
result is every RPC hangs and eventually fails with:

    client error (Connect): dns error: proto error: io error:
    No route to host (os error 65)

curl works on the same network because it uses getaddrinfo, which
honors AI_ADDRCONFIG and suppresses AAAA records when there's no v6
default route.

Setting use_system_dns=True on the HTTPTransport routes lookups through
getaddrinfo, matching curl's behavior and eliminating the spurious
EHOSTUNREACH failures on flaky/tethered networks.

version. However, the version it produces doesn't take into account
files that may have changed (ie git is dirty). We used to just hash the
whl file itself - this behavior was circumvented when adding the logic
for the preset tag but we'll revert to it now by not setting the tag
when we're in dev mode.

We need the image tag to change because even if docker cache doesn't
kick in, these images are often run with IfNotPresent pull policy -
which means even though you've pushed an updated version locally as part
of your dev cycle, the Pod that kicks off might be using the older image
and you'd be none the wiser.

Add a namespace option to @env.task for same-named functions in one environment

A task's name is `<env_name>.<function_name>`, so two modules that define a
function with the same name can't share an environment: the second one
replaces the first (#1699 now warns about this). Giving each module its own
environment avoids that, but every environment is its own reusable-container
pool, so splitting environments only for naming costs warm pods.

`@env.task(namespace="train")` names the task
`<env_name>.train.<function_name>`. The task keeps its environment, image,
resources and reusable pool; only its name changes. The namespace is checked
when the decorator is created: letters, digits and underscores separated by
`.` or `-`, and never `__main__`.

fix(remote): carry extended_resources (GPU accelerator) through TaskDetails.override

TaskDetails.override(resources=...) only copied container.resources
(cpu/mem/gpu-count) and never set task_template.extended_resources, so a
per-run override like task.override(resources=Resources(gpu="L40s:1"))
dropped the accelerator (device -> nodeSelector/toleration) and the pod
scheduled on a non-GPU node. The build/deploy path already sets it
(task_serde.get_proto_extended_resources); mirror it in override, and
clear the field when the replacement resources carry no extended
resources so a stale accelerator isn't left behind.

Enables per-run GPU overrides instead of requiring the GPU to be baked
into the task at deploy time.

    if config_path:

        flyte.init_from_config(Config.auto(config_path))
    else:
        flyte.init_from_config()
    run = flyte.run(spew_logs)
    print(f"Run: {run.name}")
    print(f"URL: {run.url}")
    print("Tailing logs...")
    run.action.show_logs(raw=True)

fix: wrap uv export failures as ImageBuildError with stderr context

`_extract_editables_from_uv_export` runs `uv export --no-emit-project` with
`check=True` and let `CalledProcessError` bubble up unmodified during image
build. The default message — `Command '['uv', 'export', '--no-emit-project']'
returned non-zero exit status 2.` — drops the captured stderr, which is the
only useful piece of information (broken pyproject, lock conflict, etc.).

Catch `CalledProcessError`, include the stderr/stdout the subprocess emitted,
and raise as `ImageBuildError` so the existing Sentry user-error filter and
ClickException handler treat it as user-actionable. Also handle the
`uv`-not-installed case with a pointer to install it instead of leaking
`FileNotFoundError`.
